suggestion.title: Mobile Banking Trojan Installation Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Report quantifies: '162,275 packages related to mobile banking Trojans' discovered in Q1 2026. This represents the largest malware category by package count but zero detection UCs were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan mobile app repositories and user devices for installation packages matching known mobile banking Trojan signatures. Cross-reference app store submissions against threat intel feeds for banking malware identifiers. Alert on apps requesting credential-access or financial-service permissions.

suggestion.title: Mobile Ransomware Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Report documents: '439 packages related to mobile ransomware Trojans' in Q1 2026. Ransomware is a critical threat class yet generated zero detection coverage despite being explicitly quantified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file encryption operations, storage encryption initialization, or ransom note file creation on mobile devices. Detect apps requesting broad file system access combined with encryption library imports. Alert on mass file modification patterns characteristic of ransomware behavior.

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Botnet C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Synthient researchers identified a link between the notorious Kimwolf botnet and the IPIDEA proxy network. This network was later taken down.' Botnet infrastructure takedown indicates active threat but zero C2 detection signatures were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS lookups or IP connections to known Kimwolf C2 servers or IPIDEA proxy infrastructure. Detect characteristic botnet communication patterns (beaconing, proxied traffic). Alert on mobile devices joining known botnet networks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Obfuscation and Code Concealment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Trojan code, meticulously concealed, was embedded into the infected Android apps. The obfuscated malicious Rust library was decrypted using a Dalvik-like virtual machine.' Generic obfuscation detection for malware defense evasion is a foundational UC absent from output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze Android app binaries for excessive obfuscation, Rust-compiled code, or embedded encrypted resources unusual for legitimate applications. Flag apps with multiple layers of obfuscation, custom encoding schemes, or packing indicators. Score obfuscation entropy against app category baseline.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly signals RCE flaws across Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n requiring execution-phase detection. No detection use case was generated despite 'RCE' being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts targeting Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n services via HTTP/HTTPS requests with known RCE payload patterns, command execution post-exploitation (process spawning, script interpretation), and unusual child-process creation from patched-service parent processes.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'SQL Injection' vulnerability but pipeline generated zero use cases. SQL injection typically precedes data exfiltration and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SQL error responses or unusual query patterns from web application servers (Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP/VMware/n8n) indicating injection attempts; correlate with excessive database query volume, multi-table sequential access, or data exfiltration indicators (large result sets, unusual SELECT patterns).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Unpatched Vulnerable Service
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation is explicitly named in the title but zero UCs address token manipulation, access token impersonation, or local PE detection chains following initial RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token impersonation or SID-History injection post-exploitation (parent RCE process spawning child process with elevated privileges, CreateRemoteThread or similar token-manipulation APIs); correlate with process creation events from vulnerable service parents.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Service Version Fingerprinting and Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: A patch announcement article should trigger detection for asset inventory queries and exploitation attempts against specific vulnerable versions of Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n. No such use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect fingerprinting activity (version enumeration queries, banner-grabbing requests) targeting known Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n endpoints; flag subsequent exploitation probes matching known RCE/SQLi payloads within short time windows from same source.

suggestion.title: Windows Update Failure Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls this a HIGH-severity update failure; if the body describes threat actors leveraging error 0x800f0922 as a vector for privilege escalation or lateral movement, pipeline missed the core attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated failed Windows update attempts (0x800f0922) followed by suspicious driver installation, system modifications, or post-exploitation reconnaissance. Correlate update failures with abnormal process execution or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Driver Installation via Update Channel Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Error 0x800f0922 is often associated with driver compatibility; if article describes threat actors injecting malicious drivers disguised as updates, pipeline should have flagged T1547 (Boot or Logon Autostart Execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or revoked driver load attempts during update window; correlate driver failures (0x800f0922) with registry modifications to boot-start driver settings or kernel module loading from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm preinstall Hook Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker modifying package.json to inject 'preinstall': 'bun run index.js', which triggers before dependencies resolve. Quote: 'Each malicious package tarball contains...A modification to package.json adding: "preinstall": "bun run index.js". The preinstall lifecycle hook triggers automatically when a developer runs npm install, before any other installation logic executes.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installations for modifications to package.json that introduce or modify preinstall/postinstall scripts, especially those invoking external binaries (bun, node) with obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate with unusual child process spawns from npm/node processes executing unfamiliar executables.

suggestion.title: Orphan Commit Injection via Deleted Fork Retention
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker creating orphan commits in forked repository, deleting fork, but relying on GitHub's retained object storage. Quote: 'The attacker forked antvis/G2, created an orphan commit carrying the payload, then deleted the fork. GitHub's object storage retains commits from deleted forks until garbage collection runs, leaving the malicious commit accessible via its hash.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub optional-dependency references to commit hashes in legitimate repositories that do not appear in the public commit history or branch references. Detect git operations fetching commits via hash from URLs that previously hosted forks now deleted. Correlate with recent fork-delete events on target repository.

suggestion.title: Stolen GitHub Actions OIDC Token Abuse for Sigstore Signing
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals malware uses stolen GitHub Actions OIDC tokens to request signing certificates from Fulcio and create in-toto provenance via Rekor. Quote: 'Using stolen GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, the malware can then request signing certificates from Fulcio (https://fulcio.sigstore.dev) and create in-toto provenance statements via Rekor (https://rekor.sigstore.dev), producing packages with cryptographically valid SLSA Build Level 3 attestations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fulcio and Rekor for signing requests from CI/CD environments that do not match expected GitHub Actions runners (IP ranges, user-agent patterns). Flag SLSA attestations signed by OIDC tokens for repositories with no corresponding GitHub Actions workflow runs in the build timeline. Detect mismatches between commit author and OIDC token subject claim.

suggestion.title: Rapid Malicious Package Publication Burst Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents attacker publishing 300+ package versions across 323 packages in 22-minute window. Quote: 'published more than 300 malicious package versions across 323 packages in a 22-minute automated burst on May 19, 2026. The packages collectively represent approximately 16 million weekly downloads...First wave: 01:39–01:56 UTC (~317 versions), Second wave: 02:05–02:06 UTC (~314 versions).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single npm account publishing >50 package versions within any 30-minute window, especially across semantically unrelated packages. Flag publish bursts from accounts that historically publish at low frequency. Correlate with version bump patterns (multiple packages receiving identical version numbers or unusual version jumps simultaneously).

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Exfiltration via npm Install Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware establishing credential harvesting as core behavior within preinstall hook payload. Quote: 'The malware embedded in affected packages harvests developer secrets and cloud credentials, establishes persistent C2 access, and attempts to self-propagate to additional packages using stolen npm tokens.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm preinstall scripts or child processes spawned during npm install that enumerate environment variables (env, printenv), read credential files (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, .env), or make outbound HTTPS connections to non-npm registries. Monitor for command-line patterns searching for API keys, tokens, or credentials in common locations.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation via Compromised npm Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies self-propagation mechanism using stolen npm tokens to compromise additional packages. Quote: 'attempts to self-propagate to additional packages using stolen npm tokens' and 'credentials are rotated immediately as the malware harvests them and sends them to C2 servers for reuse.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm publish API calls using credentials harvested from different package maintainer accounts than the publishing account. Monitor for publish events from legitimate npm accounts immediately following install of malicious packages on CI/CD systems. Detect npm token usage from IP ranges or contexts inconsistent with the token owner's historical publish patterns.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Spawning SYSTEM-Context Child
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'SYSTEM Privilege Escalation'—article body missing prevents specific payload details, but exploitation artifact is low-privilege process creating or injecting into SYSTEM context. No phrase to cite due to corrupted source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag low-privilege processes (non-admin, non-SYSTEM) spawning children with SYSTEM rights, or accessing SYSTEM process handles for impersonation/token duplication. Correlate with absence of UAC elevation prompts or scheduled-task execution paths.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Suspicious Kernel Driver Load on Patched System
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'fully patched systems'—indicates kernel-level vulnerability, likely exploited via unsigned driver or kernel-mode abuse. Cannot cite source details due to missing article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned kernel driver loads, drivers from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%, or drivers signed by untrusted certificates. Correlate with parent process signature mismatches or processes that do not typically load drivers.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode API Calls from Unprivileged Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Windows 0-day privilege escalation to SYSTEM typically requires direct kernel API invocation (NtQuerySystemInformation, NtDuplicateObject, NtAdjustPrivilegesToken). Article content unavailable; inferring from vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect usermode calls to privileged kernel APIs from non-system processes; monitor ntdll-level token operations and handle duplication outside standard IPC/delegation workflows. Establish baseline of legitimate kernel-API callers per environment.

suggestion.title: SCADA Simulation System Binary/File Integrity Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states malware 'tampered with nuclear weapons simulations'—core attack vector is file-level modification of simulation software or configuration files. No detection use case was generated despite this central attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file modifications to simulation software binaries (.exe, .dll) and config files (.ini, .cfg, .dat) in SCADA/ICS directories. Alert on unsigned binary modifications, timestamp anomalies, or unauthorized writes to known simulation platforms (ANSYS, MATLAB, PLC firmware, HMI software).

suggestion.title: Code Execution Within Simulation Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Pre-Stuxnet malware achieving tampering implies code execution within or alongside simulation software. Title describes active malware, not passive compromise—suggests process-level injection or DLL loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned from simulation software binaries, particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, reg.exe, or net.exe. Flag DLL injection attempts, memory writes to simulation executables, or unexpected ImageLoad events from simulation process context.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Autostart/Scheduled Tasks in ICS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware that 'tampered'—implies sustained presence over time, not one-shot exploitation. Pre-Stuxnet malware required persistence mechanism for long-term manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, vendor-specific simulation autostart keys, scheduled tasks, and startup folders for suspicious executables or scripts. Alert on modifications adding system-level persistence targeting SCADA/simulation software accounts.

suggestion.title: Network Beacon from Air-Gapped SCADA Simulation Systems
suggestion.rationale: SCADA simulation systems should be network-isolated. Any outbound communication to external hosts or unusual internal traffic is anomalous and indicates C2, exfiltration, or lateral movement. Pre-Stuxnet malware required command infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS queries or TCP/UDP connections from simulation hosts to non-whitelisted external domains or IPs. Simulation environments typically have zero-trust network policies; external communication is high-fidelity indicator of compromise or active C2.

suggestion.title: Fake Apple Security Update via AppleScript Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'display a fake Apple security update message referencing XProtectRemediator, downloads a shell script using curl, and executes it silently via zsh.' XProtectRemediator is a known impersonation target; AppleScript execution with curl/zsh chaining is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Script Editor (osascript) execution launching with malicious payload; detect curl/zsh execution chains following AppleScript; flag processes referencing 'XProtectRemediator' in script content or command lines.

suggestion.title: Google Update Impersonation LaunchAgent Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'installs a script impersonating the Google software update and registers it using LaunchAgent. The script is executed every minute and acts as a beacon that sends system info to the C2.' Clear persistence mechanism with predictable naming pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents for new agents with 'google', 'update', or similar brand-impersonation strings; alert on minute-interval cron execution from LaunchAgent-spawned processes sending outbound traffic.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via macOS Keychain Password Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Upon launch, it prompts the user for their macOS password, which can then be used to access Keychain items, decrypt credentials, and access protected data.' Targets multiple password managers (1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass) and crypto wallets (MetaMask, Phantom).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes requesting user password via dialog/prompt followed by access to ~/Library/Keychains, ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data, or browser extension storage directories; correlate with curl/zsh execution chains.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Application Hijacking via app.asar Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When wallet applications are present, hijacks them by terminating their processes and replacing the legitimate core application file with a malicious one called app.asar downloaded from the command-and-control (C2) server.' Targets Exodus, Atomic Wallet, Ledger Live, Electrum, Trezor Suite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for termination of known wallet processes (exodus, atomic, electrum, etc.) followed by replacement of app.asar files in their application bundles; flag xattr commands clearing quarantine flags on modified app.asar files.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Extension and Cryptocurrency Wallet Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists targets: 'Browser data from Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Opera, Vivaldi, Arc, and Orion. Cryptocurrency wallet browser extensions, including MetaMask and Phantom. Password manager browser extensions, including 1Password, Bitwarden, and LastPass.' Filegrabber module collects files <2MB from Desktop/Documents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file reads from ~/Library/Application Support/[Chrome|Firefox|Brave]/Default/Login Data, Local Storage, and Extension directories; flag processes accessing ~/Desktop and ~/Documents recursively for .pdf, .xlsx, .docx files; correlate with curl exfiltration to C2.

suggestion.title: VM/VPN Detection and Device Fingerprinting on Staging Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the website fingerprints the visitor's device to check for virtual machines and VPNs, which may indicate an analysis machine and enumerate installed browser extensions for password managers and cryptocurrency wallets.' Intelligence gathering before payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS requests to staging domains (qq-0732gwh22[.]com, mlcrosoft[.]co[.]com, mlroweb[.]com) with fingerprinting payloads (User-Agent probing, WebGL/Canvas requests); flag POST requests with browser extension enumeration data.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Command Execution via Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article titled 'Agent AI is Coming'—strongly implies autonomous agent deployment risks. Prompt injection could force agents to execute unintended commands. No use case generated despite this being a core execution vector for hostile AI actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious command invocations spawned from AI framework processes (e.g., LangChain, AutoGPT, similar execution contexts). Flag commands with unusual argument patterns, encoded payloads, or lateral-movement intent originating from agent-orchestration endpoints.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Lateral Movement via Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Agents running with elevated privileges pose credential theft and lateral movement risk. Title signals threat discussion but pipeline generated no credential-access or lateral-movement use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track process spawning from AI-framework-controlled contexts attempting to access credential stores (LSASS, credential managers, cloud auth tokens). Monitor for unusual network connections to internal assets from agent-controlled processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistent Agent Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Autonomous agents as persistent threats. Article context suggests persistence risk but pipeline failed to map this kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious scheduled tasks, startup entries, or service installations created by or associated with AI framework processes. Track modifications to Python/Node package paths or interpreter configs that enable agent auto-restart.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Code Signing Activity via Compromised Microsoft Artifact Signing Service
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Fox Tempest Malware-Signing Service Abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to Certify Malware'—abuse of a trusted code-signing infrastructure to legitimize malware requires behavioral anomaly detection on signing operations and signature validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process executions where cryptographic signature validation passes but behavioral telemetry (network callbacks, privilege escalation, credential access) or file hash reputation contradicts the legitimate signature. Monitor for malware families with valid Microsoft Artifact Signing certificates; detect anomalous certificate-to-binary mappings in code-signing logs.

suggestion.title: Fox Tempest Malware-Signing Infrastructure Enrollment and Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Named actor 'Fox Tempest' with operational malware-signing capability is the subject of the entire article—pipeline missed actor identification and infrastructure abuse patterns entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enrollment or certificate-request activity against Microsoft Artifact Signing service from suspicious accounts, impossible travel, or previously unseen source infrastructure. Look for bulk signing requests, signing-service API calls from non-standard authentication contexts, or lateral movement to code-signing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Execution of Malware with Valid Microsoft Certificate
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: malware 'Certified' by abuse of legitimate signing infrastructure ('Certify Malware'). Masquerading via valid code signature is the delivery and execution mechanism that defeats user trust heuristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Behavioral analytics on processes bearing valid Microsoft signatures: flag for command-and-control callbacks, privilege escalation, credential dumping, or lateral movement despite passing signature verification. Correlate against malware family sandboxing or behavioral indicators to surface signed malicious binaries.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Access by Single Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article states 3,800+ internal repositories were exfiltrated. Pipeline missed detection for velocity-based pattern: single compromised GitHub credential accessing, cloning, or downloading abnormally large number of repos in short window. Title phrase: 'Exfiltration of 3,800+ Internal Repos'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls for repository access/clone operations. Flag single user or credential exfiltrating 50+ repos within 1 hour or 500+ within 24 hours. Cross-correlate with employee device compromise signals (malware detections, C2 beacons) on same user's registered device.

suggestion.title: Credentials Harvested from Compromised Employee Device
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain begins with employee device compromise. Title: 'Employee Device Hack Led to Exfiltration'. Pipeline should detect harvesting of stored credentials (GitHub tokens, SSH keys, OAuth tokens) from Windows/macOS credential vaults after device compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\GitHub, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, or browser credential stores on compromised device. Monitor for Credential Manager API calls (CredUIPromptForCredentials, CryptGetHashParam). Look for LSASS dumping or Mimikatz-like memory access patterns post-malware execution.

suggestion.title: GitHub Authentication from Unusual Geographic/IP Context Post-Device-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Employee's stolen credentials used outside normal login pattern. Article establishes device compromised, then repos exfiltrated—implies credentials used from attacker infrastructure, not employee's normal office/home IPs. Missing detection for out-of-pattern authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline each GitHub user's login geography and IP ranges (office, known VPNs, home). Flag authentication from IP not in baseline. Escalate if (1) new IP + bulk repo access, (2) new IP + VPN/proxy provider IPs, (3) successful login from 2+ countries within 15 minutes, or (4) login from known malware C2 IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Employee Device Malware Execution Preceding Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: employee device was compromised before exfiltration. Article title: 'Employee Device Hack'. Pipeline should map detection for malware execution, C2 callback, or exploit delivery on employee workstations as precursor to credential theft.

Correlate with network C2 beacons to known malware infrastructure. Cross-match against email events for phishing delivery in preceding 48 hours.

suggestion.title: Repository Exfiltration via Git Clone to External Storage
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed detection for attacker downloading entire internal repositories via git clone/pull and moving to attacker storage. Title: 'Exfiltration of 3,800+ Internal Repos'. Should detect high-volume git operations + data movement off-network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag git.exe or git command execution with 'clone' or 'pull' on user workstations. Correlate with large outbound network transfers (100MB+) or uploads to cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, Google Drive) by same user in same time window. Monitor for .git archives created in temp directories or moved to removable media.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP Actor Attribution via Operational Fingerprints
suggestion.rationale: Article names threat actor explicitly. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs including actor name. Should surface TeamPCP TTPs, infrastructure, and known malware variants (e.g., Mini Shai-Hulud worm mentioned in prior memory) associated with this group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest TeamPCP known C2 infrastructure, malware hashes, and phishing domains from threat feeds. Block TeamPCP-attributed IPs and malware at perimeter. Alert on detection of TeamPCP-associated tools (Mini Shai-Hulud, TaskScheduler persistence, Bun runtime injection) in environment.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Signature/Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'TanStack npm Attack' — supply-chain attack requires poisoned package delivery. No UC for package integrity verification despite HIGH severity on source-code theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm installs for hash/signature mismatches between registry metadata and downloaded artifacts. Alert on TanStack and consumer packages (Grafana, UiPath, DraftLab) where integrity fails. Correlate installation anomalies with unusual package.lock churn or version rollbacks.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise via Atypical Maintainer Push/Publish Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Grafana GitHub Breach' — breach implies account takeover enabling unauthorized repo commits and package publishes. No UC for Git/npm account abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub pushes from new geolocations, concurrent token usage across disparate IPs, or maintainer accounts. Alert on npm publishes outside normal cadence (e.g., multiple versions in minutes) or commits with atypical authorship/messages. Correlate unusual push patterns with downstream malicious package publishes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code Exfiltration from Grafana Private Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exposes Source Code' — indicates mass repo theft from Grafana GitHub. No UC for detecting repo exports, clones, or bulk downloads by compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on volume-based GitHub operations: bulk .tar.gz/.zip exports of private repos, unusual clone counts from single account/IP, or export of entire repo histories. Correlate timing of large code downloads with subsequent npm package publishes to establish exfil-to-poison pipeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection Detection in Installed TanStack Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes TanStack as distribution vector; no UC for runtime detection of injected payloads (spawned processes, network connections, secrets access) in poisoned packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor code imported from node_modules/tanstack/* for unexpected child-process spawning, outbound connections, or environment variable exfiltration. Use entropy/YARA signatures on installed packages. Track TanStack source patterns against baseline to detect injected obfuscated code.

suggestion.title: Grafana Supply-Chain Downstream Impact Assessment via Dependency Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Grafana...TanStack npm Attack' — threat propagates to all packages consuming poisoned TanStack. No UC for detecting malicious transitive dependencies in build pipelines or package lock files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit package.lock and package-lock.json for resolved malicious TanStack versions across internal and customer deployments. Alert when builds include compromised versions. Monitor GitHub Actions for secret access during npm install steps or unexpected post-install scripts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OneDrive API Activity from Uncommon Clients
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly frames OneDrive as C2 infrastructure. Pipeline missed the detection logic: legitimate endpoints (OneDrive) abuse requires behavioral baselines—spike in upload/download volume, API calls at off-hours, or from abnormal geographic locations. Article establishes 'command-and-control' as the attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Graph API and OneDrive REST API calls for access patterns inconsistent with user baseline: large data transfers, POST/PUT during off-hours, or authentication from impossible geographies. Correlate with process execution that rarely touches cloud services.

suggestion.title: Stolen or Leaked OneDrive OAuth Tokens Used for C2
suggestion.rationale: OneDrive-as-C2 implies either compromised user credentials or stolen OAuth tokens. Article does not specify initial access vector, but token theft is the probable persistence mechanism. 'Valid Accounts' (T1078.004) and 'Application Access Token' (T1550.001) are canonical MITRE techniques for cloud C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual Graph API token acquisition (out-of-band consent flows, suspicious redirect URIs), token reuse across mismatched device/location contexts, or token refresh patterns inconsistent with user behavior. Flag consent grants for OneDrive scopes from known-malicious IPs or impossible-travel scenarios.

suggestion.title: Process-to-OneDrive Communication (GraphWorm Lateral Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'GraphWorm malware,' implying process execution on compromised systems that communicates with OneDrive for command delivery. Pipeline ignored entirely. Detect processes spawning uncommon HTTP/HTTPS connections to graph.microsoft.com or onedrive.com—especially unsigned or recently-dropped binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation (unsigned binary, temp directory origin, or rare name) with outbound connections to graph.microsoft.com or onedrive.com on ports 80/443. Flag if process has no history of cloud API interaction. Enrich with DNS timestamps and TLS certificate anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unusual File Sharing and Delegation Changes in OneDrive (Persistence/Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: OneDrive C2 implies malware capability to read/write/share files and modify permissions. Article title does not exclude exfiltration; this is canonical data-exfil pattern for cloud-resident C2. Pipeline missed collection and exfiltration phase mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OneDrive for abnormal sharing patterns: bulk file shares to new external domains, sharing permission escalations (view→edit), or anonymous link creation in rapid succession. Correlate with failed sign-in attempts or token-based logins preceding the share events.

suggestion.title: GraphWorm Malware Hash and File Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'GraphWorm' as the malware. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should identify hashes, file paths, registry keys, or command-line signatures unique to GraphWorm samples if disclosed in the body (truncated here, but standard in threat intel releases).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for GraphWorm-specific file artifacts: hashes from public samples, DLL injection patterns, or registry persistence keys. Alert if binary detects as low-confidence AV (defense evasion via obfuscation common in cloud C2 malware).

suggestion.title: MSHTA Execution with Suspicious Script Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Hackers Abuse MSHTA Legacy Windows Tool'—direct statement of attack vector. MSHTA spawning with script/URL arguments is the entry point; pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mshta.exe execution with script arguments, encoded payloads, or remote URLs. MSHTA is a legitimate LOLBin frequently abused to execute HTML/VBScript while evading application whitelists. Flag any mshta.exe spawning with /e, /s, or http/file:// arguments.

suggestion.title: MSHTA Child Process Spawning and Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'Deliver[ed]' via MSHTA—requires execution step. Pipeline failed to map malware execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate mshta.exe process creation with spawned child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe). Malware droppers delivered via MSHTA typically establish execution context immediately. Alert on mshta parent process with suspicious child cmdlines or binary writes.

suggestion.title: LummaStealer Credential Access and Memory Scraping
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'LummaStealer'—a known info-stealer malware. Pipeline extracted zero malware family recognition and missed credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LummaStealer targets credential managers, browser databases, and clipboard. Detect suspicious process access to lsass.exe, WinLogon credential cache, or bulk SQLite reads from browser profiles. Monitor for credential dumping patterns and unauthorized sensitive data reads.

suggestion.title: Amatera Malware Persistence and Registry Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Amatera' as delivery payload. Zero IOC extraction or persistence-phase mapping despite clear malware naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Amatera likely establishes persistence via HKLM/HKCU Run registry keys or scheduled tasks. Monitor for suspicious registry writes post-MSHTA execution, unsigned binaries in startup locations, or scheduled task creation with script-based commands.

suggestion.title: Malware C2 Communication and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware delivery implies C2 callbacks and data exfiltration. Pipeline missed command-and-control and exfiltration phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from mshta.exe or child processes to suspicious domains. LummaStealer exfiltrates credentials and sensitive data over HTTPS. Detect anomalous C2 patterns: high-frequency reconnections, large data transfers, or known stealer C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Module Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'single-letter Go module typosquat.' Pipeline extracted zero module IOCs. Detection should flag suspiciously short/similar module names (e.g., single-character names like 'u' masquerading as 'uuid') being imported or installed during builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor `go get` and `go mod` operations for typosquatted module names (single-char or homoglyph variants of popular libraries). Flag imports from less-trusted registries. Cross-reference module publish date against org's first-seen timestamp to identify zero-day typosquats.

suggestion.title: Go Process Initiating Anomalous DNS Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'DNS-based backdoor'—pipeline missed entire C2 phase and corresponding detection surface. Go runtime processes should not be initiating arbitrary DNS queries to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go processes (go.exe, compiled Go binaries) performing DNS lookups to non-allowlisted domains. Flag beaconing patterns: periodic DNS queries to same subdomain, DNS tunneling indicators (high subdomain entropy, unusual query volume), or queries to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Go Module Dependency in Build Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack succeeds when malicious module enters dependency tree. Article context implies build-time compromise—go.mod/go.sum files should be audited for suspicious new entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor changes to go.mod/go.sum files in git commits. Flag addition of modules not in organizational dependency allowlist. Correlate module author reputation, publish date, and download counts to identify zero-day or unpopular typosquats. Alert on modules added outside normal dependency-management processes.

suggestion.title: Single-Character Go Package Name Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'single-letter' as typosquat technique—extremely rare in legitimate Go ecosystem. Direct pattern match on module registry logs should yield high-confidence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Go package registry (pkg.go.dev, proxy.golang.org) logs for module imports matching regex ^[a-z]$. Cross-reference against curated list of legitimate single-character modules (minimal/empty). Flag all matches as typosquatting attempts. Enrich with author email, module metadata, and first-published timestamp.

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Binary Execution from Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatted module imports execute attacker code at build-time via init() or build-time hooks. Process execution from build tools should trigger forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution spawned from Go build tools, package managers, or IDE contexts. Flag child processes with unusual parents (e.g., go.exe spawning system utilities, network tools, or credential-access binaries). Correlate with go.mod changes to link execution to new module imports.

suggestion.title: FsTx Malicious File Creation on USB/EFI Partition Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes attack vector: 'placing specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive or EFI partition' as exploitation prerequisite. No detection use case generated despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FsTx-prefixed file creation on removable media or EFI system partitions. Baseline legitimate autofstx.exe auto-recovery activity. Alert on suspicious FsTx variants created outside Windows patch windows, correlate with subsequent WinRE environment transition within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: WinRE Boot Transition to Unrestricted Shell Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation sequence: 'rebooting into WinRE, and then triggering a shell with unrestricted access to the BitLocker-protected storage volume by holding down the CTRL key.' WinRE-to-shell transitions require behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected WinRE environment boots followed by cmd.exe or powershell.exe process creation with SYSTEM privileges in WinRE context. Baseline legitimate administrative recovery boots and alert on anomalous boot sequences outside change-management windows with shell spawning.

suggestion.title: autofstx.exe Removal from Session Manager BootExecute Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states Microsoft mitigation requires 'removing the autofstx.exe entry from the Session Manager's BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ value.' Attackers exploiting YellowKey may remove or modify this registry value to enable persistent WinRE access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\BootExecute for deletion of autofstx.exe entries or substitution with unsigned executables. Detect both direct registry edits and PowerShell modifications. Alert on winpeshl.ini deletion from WinRE image directories.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Configuration Downgrade to TPM-Only Mode
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation states: 'configure BitLocker on already encrypted devices from TPM-only mode to TPM+PIN mode' requiring 'a pre-boot PIN to decrypt the drive at startup.' Reverse configuration (removal of PIN requirement) indicates YellowKey exploitation preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BitLocker mode downgrades removing pre-boot PIN requirement or downgrading from TPM+PIN to TPM-only. Detect via registry (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE), WMI queries, or Intune drift. Correlate with FsTx file creation and WinRE boot events within 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Multi-Zero-Day Correlation Chain: BlueHammer, RedSun, GreenPlasma, UnDefend
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' leaked five related zero-days in coordinated protest. Article explicitly notes 'BlueHammer and RedSun local privilege escalation zero-day flaws, both of which are now being exploited in attacks.' Detection must correlate across all five for sophisticated compromise identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish correlation rule across five zero-day exploitation signatures: (1) YellowKey FsTx files + WinRE boot, (2) BlueHammer LPE process patterns, (3) RedSun LPE indicators, (4) GreenPlasma SYSTEM elevation, (5) UnDefend Defender update blocks (Event ID 3002). Alert on 2+ detections within 1 hour as indicator of multi-exploit attack chain.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Definition Update Blocking (UnDefend Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies UnDefend as zero-day where 'attackers with standard user permissions can exploit to block Microsoft Defender definition updates.' This defense-evasion technique enables post-compromise malware persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Defender operational logs for repeated definition update failures. Baseline legitimate delays (network, offline systems). Alert on sustained update blockage from single system within 24 hours, particularly when correlated with other zero-day exploitation indicators or privilege elevation events.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Remote Code Execution via Public Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'PoC Exploit Released for PostgreSQL RCE'—explicit signal of execution phase via publicly disclosed exploit. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite unambiguous kill-chain trigger in headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning from PostgreSQL daemon (postgres, psql, pgbench) — particularly shells (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) or interpreters (python, perl). Correlate timing with connection logs. Flag execution context changes where postgres UID spawns non-database utilities.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Suspicious Outbound Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation typically followed by C2 communication or data exfiltration. Title phrase 'PoC Exploit Released' signals active exploitation scenarios requiring post-compromise detection. Zero network-based use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline PostgreSQL process network behavior (replication, backups to known hosts). Alert on postgres/psql processes connecting to non-standard ports, external IP ranges, or anomalous geolocation. Flag bi-directional traffic patterns consistent with C2.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection or Command Injection in PostgreSQL Logs
suggestion.rationale: RCE in PostgreSQL typically delivered via SQL injection or unsafe function calls (COPY, EXECUTE variants). Title mentions RCE but article body unreadable—pipeline should still generate injection-pattern detection from the known attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan PostgreSQL logs for SQL injection signatures: quotes escaping, comment sequences (--), union-based payloads, base64-encoded chunks in WHERE clauses, use of dangerous functions (CREATE LANGUAGE plpythonu, COPY, EXECUTE). Alert on malformed protocol or version-specific exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Privilege Escalation or Unauthorized Authentication
suggestion.rationale: 20-year-old vulnerability may involve auth bypass or privilege confusion. Title provides no details but known RCE patterns in legacy PostgreSQL often root in privilege mishandling or role confusion. Zero privilege-escalation detection UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed authentication attempts with unusual role names (e.g., 'postgres' from non-administrative source, or root-like role creation). Track role permission grants before/after suspicious connection. Alert on superuser privilege assignments to non-DBA accounts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Version Detection and CVE Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'PostgreSQL' RCE but provides no CVE ID or specific version. Pipeline extracted zero metadata (CVE, affected versions, CVSS). Should correlate live PostgreSQL version against known 20+ year old RCE CVEs (e.g., CVE-2004-0977 buffer overflow) and scan for exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract PostgreSQL version from server logs, connection banners, or diagnostic queries. Cross-reference against CVE database for RCE vulnerabilities. Generate signatures for known exploit delivery methods targeting the identified version. Alert if exposed instance version matches known vulnerable releases.

suggestion.title: Malvertising-Delivered Trojanized Productivity App Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article description states pipeline analyzes 'trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads.' This is the primary infection vector and should trigger detection UC covering malvertising payload delivery and suspicious productivity app launch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on productivity application (Word, Excel, PDF reader) execution from unusual paths (temp dirs, downloads, AppData/Local/Temp) combined with parent process being browser or network-delivery utility. Flag unusual network connectivity from productivity app to non-standard ports immediately post-execution.

suggestion.title: Certificate Reuse Across Malware Clusters
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Certificate ... Reuse' as tracking mechanism. This indicates TamperedChef clusters are linked via shared SSL/TLS certificates, enabling both clustering and detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unique certificate thumbprints/issuer combinations across malicious C2 domains. Flag IPs/domains presenting certificates used by known TamperedChef C2 infrastructure or sharing certificate issuer+validity window with known malware cluster samples.

suggestion.title: Code Reuse Clustering via Malware Binary Similarity
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Code Reuse' as detection technique for clustering TamperedChef variants. Suggests fuzzy-hash or disassembly-level similarity linking variants like DocuFlex and EvilAI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor binary uploads and endpoint detections for malware samples with high fuzzy-hash similarity (SSDEEP, tlsh) to known TamperedChef variants (DocuFlex, EvilAI, CL-CRI-1089, CL-UNK-1090). Flag clusters of samples sharing code blocks but differing in packaging or delivery method.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) Command-and-Control Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords and description identify TamperedChef as Remote Access Trojan; article implies C2 callback capability. Detection UC needed for post-execution network beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained outbound connections from trojanized productivity app process to unusual external IPs/domains. Flag DNS queries for suspicious TLDs or domains matching known C2 infrastructure patterns. Monitor for beaconing behavior: periodic callbacks at fixed intervals post-execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Productivity Application Capability Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically discover system configuration post-execution (OS version, installed software, user/domain info). Detection UC should cover discovery phase unique to trojanized productivity apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor productivity app processes (spawned child processes executing net.exe, whoami.exe, tasklist.exe, reg.exe query) for system enumeration. Flag unusual registry queries by Word/Excel/AdobeReader. Alert on WMI queries spawned from productivity app parent process.

suggestion.title: Staged Delivery from Certificate-Signed Malware Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article links TamperedChef via shared certificates; suggests infrastructure used for multi-stage delivery. Detection should cover secondary payload staging from C2 using same certificate infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by trojanized app making outbound HTTPS connections to IPs presenting certificates matching TamperedChef cluster signature (issuer, validity, thumbprint). Flag file writes to disk post-connection followed by child process execution.

suggestion.title: EchoCreep/GraphWorm Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names EchoCreep and GraphWorm backdoors; no detection use case for identifying their execution. Article headline establishes these are the primary malware families being deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of processes named or containing 'echocreep', 'graphworm', or associated obfuscated variants. Correlate with file write events to temp directories immediately preceding network C2 activity to Discord or Graph API endpoints. Focus on execution from email client temp folders and startup-run keys.

suggestion.title: Discord Webhook C2 Communication from Enterprise Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes Discord as primary C2 channel ('Deploys...Using Discord'); zero detection use case for Discord API abuse. Threat uses legitimate Discord API for command control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS traffic to Discord API endpoints (discordapp.com, discord.com) from non-browser processes or from SYSTEM/NETWORK SERVICE. Correlate with outbound POST requests to /api/webhooks/ paths and inbound webhook message parsing within 10 seconds. Exclude Discord client and authorized applications.

suggestion.title: Anomalous MS Graph API Tokens and Delegated Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names MS Graph API as attack vector ('Using...MS Graph API'); no detection for unauthorized Graph API token acquisition or scope escalation. This is the persistence and lateral-movement mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect grant of Mail.Send, Mail.ReadWrite, or User.ReadAll permissions to unexpected applications. Alert on Azure AD sign-in events with suspicious app IDs requesting graph.microsoft.com scopes immediately after user clicks phishing link. Correlate with subsequent large-volume /me/sendMail API calls within 15 minutes of token grant.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Operations via MS Graph sendMail API
suggestion.rationale: MS Graph API abuse described in title implies mass email campaign; no detection use case for identifying Graph API sendMail abuse pattern. 'Deploys' in title suggests propagation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >100 sendMail or sendAsUser API calls from single Azure AD service principal or user within 10-minute window. Correlate Graph API request logs with outbound mail transport rules or forwarding rule additions. Flag requests originating from non-corporate IPs or Tor exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Webworm Threat Actor Initial Access Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Webworm' as threat actor name; zero use cases for detecting initial compromise vector. Attack chain begins with credential compromise or phishing; no detection for entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: detect user OAuth consent screen approvals for unfamiliar applications requesting Mail/Graph scopes within 5 minutes of phishing email delivery (indicated by URLClickEventAction in MDO logs). Flag if approved app is new, unverified, or requests excessive permissions. Correlate timestamp with subsequent token issuance and immediate Graph API activity.

suggestion.title: Webworm Malware Family Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Webworm'; threat intelligence lacks detection for its indicators. Malware family name should map to file hashes, registry keys, injection patterns, or network signatures absent from article body due to corruption. Minimum viable extraction: file drops to %TEMP%, mutex creation, scheduled task persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run containing 'webworm' or 'echocreep'; file creation in %TEMP%\webworm* or %APPDATA% with .vbs or .ps1 extension; Task Scheduler task creation with Discord webhook in command line. Baseline on malware sandbox detections to extract PE imphash.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Authorization Code Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Comment explicitly describes compromise vector: 'employee shouldn't have clicked to view the shared document they got through email. And definitely shouldn't have copy & pasted the authorization code that most likely gave them access to their Auth Token for Salesforce.' This is the initial compromise mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for phishing emails containing Salesforce OAuth authorization code lures (e.g., 'verify identity', 'confirm access', 'authorize app'). Flag emails with shortened URLs, 'authorize' buttons, or copy-paste instructions. Correlate email recipients with successful Salesforce token generation events within 2 hours of email delivery.

suggestion.title: Bulk Franchisee Document Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' and ShinyHunters 'stolen over 600,000 records.' Indicates systematic collection phase targeting document storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Salesforce document access patterns. Alert on single accounts exporting >300 franchisee documents within 1 hour, accounts accessing multiple franchisee ORGs not previously contacted, or cascading reads of sensitive objects followed by archive creation events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Salesforce Account Access Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Breach occurred April 8, 2026 via stolen Salesforce credentials. Detection should identify account compromise indicators: unusual geography, off-hours access, API token generation by non-admin users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce login events for geographically impossible travel, logins from high-risk proxies or TOR exit nodes, off-hours access by desk workers, rapid API calls immediately after successful login, and access to sensitive object types by non-manager accounts.

suggestion.title: Large Data Archive Creation and Exfiltration (9.4GB Threshold)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site.' Exfiltration phase indicator is the creation and bulk transfer of encrypted/compressed archive files off-network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large archive creation (tar.gz, 7z, zip >500MB) on systems with Salesforce console access. Monitor egress to cloud storage (Dropbox, AWS S3, Mega) and anonymization infrastructure (Tor, residential proxy). Flag encrypted tunnels exfiltrating >500MB in <4 hours correlated with Salesforce data access.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Leak Site Monitoring for 7-Eleven Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay a ransom.' Threat intelligence must monitor breach forums and extortion boards for advertised datasets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to dark-web breach board monitoring for 7-Eleven, Salesforce, or franchisee-related data advertisements. Ingest alerts from ShinyHunters leak site scraping. Cross-reference exposed data with internal PII inventory. Generate customer notification and breach timeline artifacts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Against Exposed Salesforce Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Post-breach context: ShinyHunters extracted 600K+ records and 9.4GB archive. Secondary attacks should use exposed credentials for lateral movement or re-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-disclosure, monitor Salesforce login attempts from credential databases matching the exposed 600K records. Flag failed login bursts on leaked employee accounts, successful logins from new geographies, and secondary lateral movement from Salesforce to downstream services (AWS, Slack, Google Workspace) using compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Repository Compromise - Malicious Tag Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'All Tags Point to Imposter Commit.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for the compromised repository (actions-cool/issues-helper) and did not model tag-level persistence as an attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public GitHub Actions repositories for tag mutations—specifically, tags that are re-pointed to different commits, unsigned tags, or tags authored by accounts outside the repository organization. Cross-reference tag commit hashes against release notes and changelogs to identify orphaned/forged tags.

suggestion.title: Compromised Public GitHub Action Downloaded and Executed in CI/CD Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms action is compromised; supply-chain attack vector is execution in consuming workflows. Pipeline did not generate use case for detecting workflow invocation of malicious actions-cool/issues-helper versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows that invoke actions-cool/issues-helper or other public actions, especially with non-pinned versions or major-version-only refs. Correlate with commits that added or updated the action reference. Flag actions pulled during time-window of compromise across all consuming repositories.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Environment - CI/CD Secrets Access
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials.' Pipeline did not model credential exfiltration as a detection use case, nor extract indicators of the exfiltration target (URL, IP, domain).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect actions accessing GitHub-provided secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, custom secrets) and subsequently making outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections, especially to non-GitHub hosts. Flag actions that base64-encode or otherwise obfuscate credentials in logs, or that instantiate curl/wget commands with credential arguments.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Integrity Check - Public Action Signature and Commit Verification
suggestion.rationale: Malicious commit persisted across all tags because verification is insufficient. Pipeline did not suggest detection for workflows that fail to validate action GPG signatures or commit hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enforce and audit cryptographic verification of public GitHub Actions: validate GPG-signed tags, verify commit hashes match expected values, check author key fingerprints against trusted registries. Alert on workflows using loose refs (e.g., `@v1` instead of `@v1.2.3`), unsigned tags, or tags signed by keys outside organizational trust anchor.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Connections from CI/CD Runner Environment
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration implies outbound network traffic carrying credentials. Pipeline did not model detection for unexpected egress from GitHub Actions runners or CI/CD execution environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted destinations. Alert on connections to newly-registered domains, IP space owned by threat-actor infrastructure, or known credential-exfiltration services. Correlate connection timing with workflow steps that access secrets or environment variables.

suggestion.title: Repository Audit Log for Unexpected Tag Creation or Modification Events
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates attackers modified all tags to point to malicious commit. Pipeline did not suggest detection for GitHub audit events showing unauthorized tag manipulation or branch protection bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs for create/update/delete events on tags, especially in public actions repositories. Alert on tags modified after initial release, branches created with suspicious naming patterns, or branch protection rules disabled. Correlate with commit authorship anomalies (unexpected authors, service accounts).

suggestion.title: node-ipc Malicious Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'node-ipc' as malicious package published to npm; attack vector is 'npm supply chain.' Pipeline extracted zero package names despite this being primary IOC surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe, npm.cmd, and yarn process execution for 'install node-ipc' arguments or package.json modifications adding node-ipc dependency. Alert on lock file changes (package-lock.json, yarn.lock) reflecting node-ipc versions outside known-safe baseline. Flag installations from non-official registries or mirror fallback behavior during resolution.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Payload Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious versions' suggesting code execution payload. npm packages execute postinstall hooks during installation — pipeline did not map to execution phase or detect install-time process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from npm install lifecycle (node.exe, npm.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe). Alert on postinstall/preinstall hooks containing obfuscated commands, external URL downloads, or network calls. Monitor for scripts executing in node_modules/.bin/, .npm/_cacache, or global npm directories with suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: node-ipc Module Code Execution via require()
suggestion.rationale: Installed malicious package executes when imported. Article does not detail mechanism but is inherent to npm supply-chain attacks. Pipeline did not generate detection for module require() or import execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from Node.js applications requiring node-ipc module. Correlate package installation event with subsequent unexpected process execution within minutes. Alert on unusual file access from node_modules/node-ipc directories followed by network or credential access events.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Compromised Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware establishes C2. Article states 'active' attack implying ongoing communications. Pipeline did not generate network-based detection for exfiltration or command channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS from node.exe or npm.exe processes to suspicious or newly-registered domains. Alert on large or periodic data exfiltration from developer machines post-npm-install. Detect DNS queries to known node-ipc malware C2 infrastructure (cross-reference external threat feeds). Flag encrypted tunnels (SSH, VPN, proxy) initiated after package installation.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Tampering or Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'malicious versions published to npm' — implies either registry account compromise or man-in-the-middle. Pipeline should detect package signature/hash failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed npm package signature verification (if npm audit or --verify-signatures enabled). Detect mismatches between lockfile hash and downloaded package hash. Monitor for unexpected npm registry mirror fallback or delayed/incomplete downloads. Flag installations from non-official npm endpoints or suspicious CDN redirects.

suggestion.title: Persistence via node-ipc Cron/Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware establishes persistence for re-execution. Article describes 'active' campaign; persistence mechanism not detailed but typical for npm backdoors. Pipeline did not map to persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron jobs or Windows Task Scheduler entries created by npm or node processes post-installation. Detect scripts added to node-ipc plugin directories, ~/.node-ipc/, or npm global directories. Alert on startup scripts or scheduled tasks executing obfuscated commands or external payload downloads. Flag tasks with 'node' or 'npm' binaries as action with suspicious working directories.

suggestion.title: Nx Console 18.95.0 Extension Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'Compromised Nx Console 18.95.0' — version is a direct IOC and attack surface. Pipeline failed to extract this as initial_access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation or update of Nx Console VS Code extension targeting version 18.95.0 specifically. Track file operations in .vscode/extensions/ directory, npm package install events, or manifest parsing of extension metadata to identify the compromised package version as it hits the target environment.

suggestion.title: Extension Host Process Credential Store Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies malware capability as 'Credential Stealer' — pipeline must detect when extension code accesses credential stores. T1552.004 and T1005 techniques not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by VS Code extension host (node.exe under extension context) accessing Windows Credential Manager (vaultcmd.exe, cmdkey /list), reading SSH private keys from ~/.ssh/, AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials, or enumerating LSASS tokens via Win32 API calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Network from VS Code Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer capability requires data exfiltration phase. Article title implies C2 communication but pipeline generated zero network-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS traffic from VS Code extension host process to non-standard IPs or domains outside legitimate Nx infrastructure (nx.app, api.nrwl.io). Flag dynamic DNS, custom TLDs, infrastructure-as-a-service IPs, or any connections matching known C2 signatures.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Persistence via Manifest Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Targeted VS Code Developers' — implies attackers expect payload to survive updates and restarts. Pipeline did not map to persistence techniques T1547.013.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to Nx Console extension manifest (package.json activationEvents, contributes.commands) or VS Code settings.json configuration to ensure malicious code executes on extension load. Track file modifications to .vscode/extensions metadata and activation trigger changes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-55241 Entra ID Token Forgery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2025-55241, a critical Entra ID flaw patched in July 2025, illustrated this precisely: an attacker could forge tokens accepted across any tenant, leaving no trace in victim logs.' Requires detection of unexpected cross-tenant token acceptance and validation bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Entra ID SigninLogs for authentication events where token validation succeeds across unexpected tenant boundaries, or where token claims indicate cross-tenant acceptance. Flag successful authentication with invalid tenant context, particularly service principals or managed identities accepting tokens issued for different tenants. Baseline expected cross-tenant patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Office Macro Execution in Enterprise Documents
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Microsoft Office vulnerabilities surged 234% year over year, rising from 47 to 157, with critical vulnerabilities jumping from 3 to 31... Macros, document sharing, preview panes, HTML rendering, new AI capabilities, and add-ins create a unique landscape for exploitation. When Office vulnerabilities spike, users remain the most reliable entry point via social engineering.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office process (WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE, POWERPNT.EXE) spawning child processes with command-line arguments, particularly POWERSHELL.EXE or CMD.EXE. Monitor for msiexec.exe spawned by Office with suspicious arguments. Track Office document load events followed by unexpected process execution, especially for macro-enabled filetypes (.docm, .xlsm, .pptm). Establish baseline of legitimate Office macro behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Windows Preview Pane Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'seven CVEs in 2025 exploited it [preview pane] as an entry point.' Specific entry point enumerated with quantified attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor explorer.exe and other shell processes for attempts to parse and render files through preview pane mechanisms (shell namespace handlers, property pages, preview protocol). Detect when preview pane rendering triggers child process creation or unexpected DLL loading (particularly in context of historically exploited formats: PDF, Office, image files). Correlate file access to uncommon filetypes with process execution.

suggestion.title: Service Account Privilege Escalation via Elevation of Privilege CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Elevation of Privilege vulnerabilities (accounting for 40% of all CVEs)' and 'treating service accounts and AI agents with the same scrutiny as human identities, and disabling the Windows preview pane.' 40% of CVE population targeting privilege escalation requires detection of elevation attempts from service account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline service account privilege usage patterns (which services run as which accounts, token elevation attempts). Alert on service accounts calling elevation mechanisms (CreateProcessAsUser, ShellExecute with runas), UAC bypass patterns (registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System), or token elevation requests. Monitor for service accounts accessing SYSTEM-level resources they do not normally require.

suggestion.title: Living Off the Land Binary Execution from Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Threat actors no longer need noisy exploits or mass malware campaigns if they can quietly escalate access and move laterally using legitimate credentials and Living Off the Land tactics.' Requires detection of built-in tooling abuse for lateral movement and reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor service accounts and compromised user contexts for execution of reconnaissance and lateral movement tools: PowerShell with specific modules (ActiveDirectory, Hyper-V), WMI queries (Get-WmiObject, wmic), net commands (net user, net group, net share), Tasklist, systeminfo, ipconfig. Alert when these tools execute from service account context or with unusual parent processes. Correlate baseline discovery tool usage with subsequent logon attempts on enumerated systems.

suggestion.title: Azure Cloud Misconfiguration and Excessive Service Principal Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Azure and Dynamics 365 decreased slightly in total vulnerability count, but critical vulnerabilities spiked dramatically, jumping from 4 to 37 in a single year... A single misconfigured identity in Azure can hand an attacker the keys to your entire tenant, and most organizations wouldn't know until the damage was done.' Requires detection of dangerous permission patterns and dangerous service principal activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service principal creation with excessive permissions (Owner, Contributor roles at subscription/tenant scope). Alert on unexpected Service Principal Token Issuance (STS) requests, particularly from unusual IP ranges or locations. Detect modifications to role assignments that grant dangerous permissions (User.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All) to service principals with unverified ownership. Flag access to sensitive Azure resources (Key Vault secret retrieval, managed identity token endpoints) from unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: Azure Artifact Signing Certificate Volume Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fox Tempest has created over a thousand certificates' — pipeline must detect abnormally high certificate creation rates per subscription/tenant to catch MSaaS operators before abuse scales.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Artifact Signing API calls (Microsoft.SigningService/certificates/create) for unusual velocity (>10 certs/hour per subscription) or newly provisioned tenants with immediate high certificate volume. Correlate with identity-verification errors or geographically anomalous creation patterns.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Spoofing Legitimate Software Names with Code-Signed Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware impersonating 'Microsoft Teams, AnyDesk, PuTTY, and Webex' installers that are 'digitally signed and trusted as legitimate software by both users and operating systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes with filenames matching legitimate software (Teams.exe, AnyDesk.exe, PuTTY.exe, Webex.exe) but executing from atypical directories or with parent-child relationships inconsistent with legitimate installers. Flag even if code-signed — valid signatures from Artifact Signing service are now compromised; cross-reference certificate thumbprints/serialnums against Microsoft's revocation list.

suggestion.title: Oyster Malware Loader and Ransomware Deployment Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'When unsuspecting victims executed the falsely named Microsoft Teams installer files, those files delivered a malicious loader, which in turn installed the fraudulently signed Oyster malware and ultimately deployed Rhysida ransomware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multi-stage execution chains where an installer-named process (Teams, AnyDesk, etc.) spawns unsigned/suspicious child processes (loader), followed by network callbacks and registry persistence hooks. Oyster is the intermediate loader — flag its known file hashes and command-line patterns that precede ransomware execution.

suggestion.title: Cloudzy Infrastructure Abuse for Malware Signing VMs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fox Tempest evolved its operation earlier this year by providing customers with pre-configured virtual machines hosted through Cloudzy infrastructure. Customers uploaded malware to the VM environments and received signed binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound communications to Cloudzy infrastructure (IP ranges, reverse-DNS patterns) from development/build systems or user machines. Monitor for SSH/RDP sessions to Cloudzy-hosted VMs from corporate networks. Track HTTP/HTTPS uploads of suspected malware binaries to Cloudzy-hosted endpoints.

suggestion.title: Telegram EV Certs Promotion Channel C2 Signaling
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'The malware-signing platform was promoted on a Telegram channel named "EV Certs for Sale by SamCodeSign," with pricing ranging from $5,000 to $9,000 in bitcoin.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user/developer machines connecting to Telegram channels discussing code-signing services, malware-as-a-service, or certificate sales. Flag cryptocurrency payment discussions paired with malware signing procurement. Correlate Telegram channel membership with subsequent uploads to signing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Azure Tenants and Subscriptions for MSaaS Fronting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fox Tempest created more than 1,000 certificates and established hundreds of Azure tenants and subscriptions as part of the operation' — operational security red flag requiring audit of tenant provisioning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure for subscriptions with abnormally high Artifact Signing certificate counts (>50 per tenant). Correlate tenant creation with suspicious email domains or identity-verification failures. Detect rapid Azure resource provisioning (VMs, compute) shortly after tenant creation, then sudden certificate generation and disuse — pattern typical of pay-per-signing operations.

suggestion.title: DirtyDecrypt PoC Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'DirtyDecrypt PoC Released'—indicates active exploitation will execute the PoC binary. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; missing detection for exploit execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of 'dirtydecrypt' binary or command-line patterns invoking the exploit (e.g., git clone + compile + execute). Detect suspicious shells launching exploit payloads targeting CVE-2026-31635.

suggestion.title: Linux Privilege Escalation via CVE-2026-31635 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies vulnerability as 'LPE' (local privilege escalation); pipeline failed to generate privilege-escalation kill-chain phase or detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged user spawning root processes, setuid/setgid syscall sequences targeting vulnerable kernel functions, or capability manipulation (cap_sys_admin, cap_sys_module). Monitor for sudo/su elevation attempts followed by LPE exploit execution.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Loading for CVE-2026-31635 Exploitation
