suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cobalt Strike beacon signatures: rundll32/powershell process spawning with suspicious injection patterns, HTTP POST beaconing to non-standard ports, memory injection via CreateRemoteThread. Monitor for DNS queries to Cobalt Strike default C2 domains and JA3/TLS fingerprint anomalies.

suggestion.title: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) Loading Attempt
suggestion.rationale: "Tried to deploy... a vulnerable driver, likely to disable endpoint protection using the Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) technique." Defense evasion mechanism targeting EDR, ultimately blocked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned/revoked driver load attempts from user-writable directories (AppData, Temp, Downloads). Flag known-vulnerable driver names (gdrv.sys, DBUtil_2_3.sys, GIGABYTE, MSI variants). Correlate with recent EDR process termination or anomaly in Sysmon Event ID 6 (driver load).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Tax-Themed Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake income tax assessment pages'—initial access vector. Should detect access to newly registered or spoofed domains impersonating tax authorities (malformed *.tax TLDs, non-official tax.gov lookalikes, tax keywords on suspicious registrars).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users resolving/connecting to domains with 'tax', 'irs', 'assessment' keywords registered <30 days ago, or non-government ASNs claiming to be .gov domains. Alert on redirect chains from legitimate-looking tax pages to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Fake Tax Page Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'infect Windows systems'—execution phase. Detect suspicious process execution immediately after downloads from non-official tax domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file downloads (from non-tax-authority domains) to %Downloads% or %temp%, then alert on child process execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, .exe/.scr/.zip launch) within 2 minutes. Flag if parent process is browser.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Registration—Tax Authority Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires registering fake tax assessment domains. Should detect newly registered domains mimicking tax infrastructure: 'fake income tax assessment pages' indicates domain registration with spoofing intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WHOIS registrations with tax keywords in last 30 days, non-government registrars, or nameservers outside official tax authority IP ranges. Cross-reference against historical .gov CNAME records to catch lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Domain Masquerading—Legitimate Tax Authority Brand Abuse
suggestion.rationale: 'Fake income tax assessment pages' is a masquerading attack. Should detect domains or pages using legitimate tax authority visual/textual identity without legitimate source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSL certificates issued for domains containing 'tax', 'irs', 'revenue' but registered to non-government entities. Alert on HTTPS connections where cert CN/SAN claims government authority but issuer is third-party CA or self-signed.

suggestion.title: FsTx Malicious File Placement on USB or EFI Partition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'placing specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive or EFI partition, rebooting into WinRE.' This is the primary attack delivery vector; pipeline extracted no file-based IOCs or detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or presence of files with FsTx extension on USB-connected devices, external media, or EFI system partitions. Alert on any FsTx file activity as they are non-standard Windows components. Correlate with subsequent WinRE boot or shell spawning events.

suggestion.title: WinRE Shell Execution via CTRL Key Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'triggering a shell with unrestricted access to the BitLocker-protected storage volume by holding down the CTRL key.' Pipeline completely missed this execution and privilege-escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from WinRE or Recovery Partition context with file system access spanning BitLocker volumes. Flag abnormal parent processes during boot recovery scenarios. Monitor for CTRL key sequences during WinRE if telemetry available.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification: BootExecute autofstx.exe Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation: 'removing the autofstx.exe entry from the Session Manager's BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ value.' Attackers may preemptively remove this defense; registry modification was not extracted as IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager BootExecute value for removal or disabling of autofstx.exe entries. Alert on any modification to BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ. Baseline legitimate entries and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BitLocker Configuration Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Article advises configuring BitLocker from 'TPM-only' to 'TPM+PIN' mode as mitigation. Attackers may reverse this; pipeline missed detection for BitLocker security posture degradation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BitLocker configuration transitions from TPM+PIN back to TPM-only or suspension of pre-boot authentication. Alert on unexpected BitLocker disablement or key material export. Track administrative BitLocker cmdlet execution (Disable-BitLocker, Suspend-BitLocker).

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Definition Update Blocking (UnDefend Zero-Day)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'UnDefend, another zero-day that attackers with standard user permissions can exploit to block Microsoft Defender definition updates.' Defense-evasion technique with standard-user exploitation—no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Defender definition update failures, service disruptions, and signature push failures. Alert on repeated failed update attempts followed by Defender degradation. Correlate timing with suspicious non-admin process execution.

suggestion.title: Active Exploitation of BlueHammer / GreenPlasma LPE Zero-Days
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) and RedSun...are now being exploited in attacks' and 'GreenPlasma...attackers can abuse to obtain a SYSTEM shell.' Both active exploits with zero IOCs extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation from user context to SYSTEM without explicit elevation prompts, consistent with LPE exploitation. Track suspicious code paths known to trigger BlueHammer, GreenPlasma, or RedSun. Alert on abnormal process nesting and token elevation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Code-Signed Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'malware-signing service behind ransomware attacks' — suggests threat actors obtaining valid code signatures to bypass Windows SmartScreen and UAC warnings. Missing UC for detecting execution of binaries with suspicious signing certificates or recently-issued certs tied to known malicious services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with code signatures issued by newly-discovered CAs, or signatures failing chain-of-trust validation. Alert on binaries signed by certificates subsequently revoked by Microsoft. Cross-reference signer thumbprints against blacklists of known malware-signing services.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Signed Package
suggestion.rationale: Article implies ransomware delivery mechanism using valid signatures. Missing UC for detecting suspicious download/execution patterns of newly-signed executables, especially those distributed through common infection vectors (email, watering holes, supply chain).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of executables with code signatures issued within 7 days of known ransomware families. Flag cases where download source is unusual for software distribution (personal email, file-sharing services). Correlate with ransomware telemetry.

suggestion.title: Certificate Authority Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Service that signs malware implies either CA compromise or insider abuse of legitimate certificate-issuing authority. Missing UC for detecting anomalous certificate issuance patterns, bulk signing requests, or creation of intermediate CAs by unauthorized accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor certificate request/issuance logs for unusual patterns: batch requests, out-of-hours signing, issuance to non-whitelisted departments, or requests by newly-created service accounts. Alert on creation of subordinate CAs or changes to certificate validation policies.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Installation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title states extension was 'Compromised'—implies malicious install/update. Pipeline missed detection for unexpected extension installs across organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console VS Code extension installations where the extension was not previously present in the environment. Alert on version downgrades or installs from non-standard sources. Baseline approved extension versions and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Build Process Behavioral Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension would alter Nx CLI behavior. Phrase 'Compromised' implies runtime malicious activity during build execution. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of anomalous child processes or network egress during builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected child processes spawned by Nx CLI (npm, node, build tools). Alert when unexpected processes (PowerShell, cmd, curl, wget) execute during Nx build phase. Detect exfiltration-pattern network connections (DNS, HTTPS to non-CDN domains) initiated from Nx CLI context.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Manifest Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of extension implies malicious manifest modification or unauthorized code injection. Pipeline missed detection for extension metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to extension manifest files (package.json, extension metadata in %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions). Alert on unsigned or untrusted manifest updates. Detect injection of new entry points or script changes post-installation.

suggestion.title: Build Pipeline Credential Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev tool could steal build-time credentials (git tokens, npm tokens, cloud keys). Title alone establishes high-privilege execution context. Pipeline failed to suggest monitoring for credential exfiltration during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution reading credential files (.npmrc, .git/config, ssh keys, environment variables) during Nx build execution. Detect environment-variable enumeration (env, printenv) or credential-store queries. Alert on exfiltration of these values over HTTP/HTTPS to non-organization domains.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Version Control Integrity
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension implies version pinning bypass or malicious auto-update. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of unexpected extension version transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Nx Console extension version across all developer machines. Alert on spontaneous version changes (especially downgrades or jumps to unsigned/beta versions). Detect registry/manifest modifications that disable extension signature verification or allow unsigned extensions.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Nx CLI Execution Profile Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise means malicious code executes in every developer's build context. Pipeline failed to suggest baseline detection for abnormal Nx invocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Nx CLI command-line patterns, invocation frequency, and timing across developer population. Alert on statistical outliers: unusual times of day, abnormal command-line arguments, invocations from user accounts not typically running builds. Detect lateral spread patterns (same compromise signals across multiple machines in short time window).

suggestion.title: Setuid/Setgid Binary Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Local Privilege Escalation Flaw Allows Silent Root Access' — Pardus Linux CVEs typically exploit setuid/setgid mechanisms. Detection needed for suspicious setuid bit modifications or execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected changes to setuid/setgid bits on system binaries, execution of setuid-enabled binaries from anomalous directories, or parent-child relationships violating expected privilege inheritance. Baseline per-user capability sets.

suggestion.title: Sudo Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Local Privilege Escalation Flaw' — common Linux vector involves sudo misconfiguration or CVE. Sudo execution patterns must be monitored for exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocation with NOPASSWD flag, sudo execution by non-standard users, unusual command-line arguments, or sudo commands executing scripts from world-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Unexpected UID 0 Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Allows Silent Root Access' — must detect privilege escalation from unprivileged user to UID 0. Baseline user privilege levels and detect unauthorized transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline UID/GID per user and process. Alert on unexpected privilege level transitions (unprivileged → UID 0, or unprivileged → system groups). Monitor process ancestry for privilege boundary violations.

suggestion.title: Kernel Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Pardus Linux privilege escalation CVEs frequently exploit kernel vulnerabilities. Title 'Flaw Allows Silent Root Access' suggests kernel-level attack vector. Detection must monitor for kernel-level anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious syscall patterns associated with kernel exploits (ptrace/ioctl sequences, direct memory access, mmap with unusual flags), kernel module loading from user processes, or abnormal exception/segfault clustering.

suggestion.title: Pardus Linux System Binary Integrity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation CVEs exploit vulnerabilities in core system utilities. Pardus-specific binaries likely to be targets. Detection requires file integrity baseline against package manifest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hash and permission integrity of privilege-escalation-sensitive binaries (/usr/bin/sudo, /bin/mount, /usr/sbin/useradd, /bin/ls, /bin/chmod). Alert on modification timestamp anomalies or permission changes outside patch windows.

suggestion.title: Linux Privilege Escalation via PinTheft Exploit Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states vulnerability 'Let Attackers Gain Root Access' on Linux. Detection should identify exploitation attempts and successful privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Linux privilege escalation syscalls (setuid, setgid, CAP_SYS_ADMIN usage) correlating with PinTheft exploit signatures. Alert on unexpected transitions from non-root to root context, particularly via exploitation vectors. Baseline normal privilege escalation patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Public PinTheft PoC Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'PoC Released', signaling public availability of working exploit. Early detection of PoC usage prevents exploitation cascades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track download and execution of PinTheft public exploits. Monitor for characteristic PoC filenames, repository URLs (GitHub, GitLab), or signature patterns. Alert when users execute unknown binaries or scripts targeting Linux privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Access Patterns on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Root access is the stated impact. Should detect unauthorized elevation outside expected maintenance windows or change control processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authorized root access initiators (sudo users, service accounts) and elevation timing. Alert on root shell spawns from unexpected parent processes, out-of-window escalations, or repeated failed privilege escalation attempts indicating exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable System Identification - PinTheft Linux Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Linux-specific vulnerability requires asset discovery. Title constrains scope to Linux platform; pipeline should drive inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Linux systems. Cross-reference against PinTheft CVE data (when disclosed) to identify vulnerable Linux kernel versions, distributions, or configurations. Flag unpatched systems and track remediation timelines.

suggestion.title: Gaming Account Credential Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata states goal of 'securing gaming communities' (from description)—credential attacks are the primary initial-access vector for gaming account compromise. Pipeline should have inferred this from title/description despite corrupted body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect brute-force and spray attacks targeting gaming accounts: >10 failed logins per account within 5 minutes, >50 failed logins across unique accounts in 10 minutes, or MFA exhaustion attempts. Correlate with IP reputation, geolocation anomalies, and user-profile baseline.

suggestion.title: Gaming Account Takeover via Session Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Metadata references 'unique challenges' of securing gaming platforms—session hijacking and account takeover are core threats requiring detection based on deviation from baseline player behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-account baselines (login time-of-day, geography, device type, in-game activity cadence). Alert on suspicious deviations: login from new country without prior access, impossible travel >1000km/h between sessions, or in-game activity at times inconsistent with historical player pattern.

suggestion.title: Gaming Service Availability Attack (DDoS)
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Securing the gaming' and emphasis on protecting platforms implies availability is a core concern. Gaming platforms are high-value DDoS targets; this UC should have been generated from title context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric and application-layer DDoS: sustained traffic >3x baseline during off-peak hours, abnormal packet-per-second variance, HTTP requests with low user-agent diversity, or rapid connection-exhaustion patterns. Correlate with player-latency spikes and session-drop rates.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Process Accessing Credential Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes credential theft as attack outcome: 'poisoned extension breached GitHub' implies unauthorized access to GitHub credentials, likely via extension code reading .git config or environment variables containing PAT tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension host process (codeserver.exe, extension.js runner) for file system access to .git/config, .gitconfig, or .ssh directories. Alert on reads of GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN environment variables or access to credential manager APIs from extension context.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'poisoned extension' indicates the extension itself is the attack vector; either installed maliciously or compromised after legitimate installation. Pipeline should detect unusual extension installation sources or unsigned extension loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension installation from non-official registry (typosquatted package name in extensions.json, offline .vsix install, or HTTP-only download). Monitor for extensions requesting file system or network permissions. Track extension installation sources and flag registry writes from non-VSCode processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Activity from VS Code Extension Host
suggestion.rationale: Breaching GitHub implies exfiltration of credentials to attacker infrastructure; extension code must beacon out to C2 domain with stolen tokens. Title establishes external data flow: 'poisoned extension...breached GitHub' = data egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound domains from VS Code extension host process (code-server, vscode-server). Alert on: DNS queries to suspicious TLDs, HTTPS connections to rare/never-seen domains from extension context, POST requests with base64 or URL-encoded credential-like data patterns, or connections to known malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via VS Code Extension Load
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: extension runs arbitrary JavaScript in privileged VS Code context. Title 'poisoned extension' implies code execution as primary payload delivery. Pipeline should detect extension activation hooks loading arbitrary code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension activation events for suspicious entry points: extensions.json declaring non-standard activation events (on-demand, wildcard patterns), extension.js/index.js files containing eval(), require('child_process'), or obfuscated code. Alert on extensions modifying PATH or installing shell scripts during activation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Developer Machine to GitHub via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title outcome: 'breached GitHub' — implies attacker pivoted from compromised developer machine to GitHub account using stolen credentials. Pipeline should detect suspicious GitHub API calls or git push/clone operations from non-standard contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: git commands (push, clone, config) executed from VS Code extension process or child process. Monitor for unusual GitHub API calls (Create repos, list private repos, push to unexpected branches) using stolen PAT tokens. Correlate with extension code execution timeline and credential access events.

suggestion.title: Persistence via VS Code Extension Autostart
suggestion.rationale: For sustained breach, attacker extension must survive restarts and reinstalls. Title 'extension' implies it persists across sessions. Should detect extensions modifying VS Code settings, user data, or system startup mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or malicious extensions modifying settings.json (autoload, execute on startup), creating VS Code keybindings pointing to attacker payloads, or writing to %APPDATA%/Code/User/globalStorage for persistence markers. Alert on extensions registering shell commands or modifying system PATH.

suggestion.title: Certificate Subject Reuse Across Malware Families
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse'; indicates shared certificate infrastructure across multiple malware families (TamperedChef, DocuFlex, EvilAI). Pipeline must detect clustering via certificate fingerprint/subject commonality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events where unsigned or self-signed certificates match between samples attributed to different malware families. Correlate certificate subjects/issuers across DeviceProcessEvents and TLS traffic logs to identify infrastructure reuse patterns indicating coordinated campaigns.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign to RAT Delivery Chain
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'malvertising' and 'Remote Access Trojan'; article discusses trojanized productivity apps delivered via malicious ads. No detection for malvertising vector in output despite being primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious ad network redirects followed by executable downloads and process execution. Correlate malvertising infrastructure (ad domains) with known RAT C2 infrastructure; flag process execution chains initiated from browser with parent process being updater or productivity app.

suggestion.title: Code Similarity Clustering for TamperedChef Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Code Reuse' as clustering signal; indicates multiple samples share significant code portions. Pipeline should surface code similarity thresholds (fuzzy hash matches, TLSH) as attribution technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag binaries with high code similarity (TLSH ≥ 80, ssdeep ≥ 85) to known TamperedChef samples in event logs or endpoint telemetry. Track file hashes uploaded to internal sandbox or downloaded from external sources; correlate similarity scores with known campaign identifiers (CL-CRI-1089, CL-UNK-1090).

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies malware family as 'Remote Access Trojan'; RATs inherently perform C2 communication. Keywords field explicitly lists this attack type. No detection use case generated for RAT-specific C2 patterns despite high severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing patterns: regular outbound connections from known trojanized app processes to low-reputation domains; DNS queries for dynamic DNS providers; unusual port usage (non-standard HTTP/HTTPS). Correlate process ancestry (browser → updater → RAT process) with network events.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Productivity Application Launch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Metadata references 'Appsuite PDF' and trojanized productivity apps as delivery vehicle. No detection for modified/replaced legitimate applications despite this being primary infection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation from unexpected paths for legitimate applications (e.g., Adobe Reader, Microsoft Office not in Program Files); monitor for file replacement events in app directories; correlate with subsequent child process execution for unsigned or obfuscated binaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via RAT Persistence
suggestion.rationale: RAT capabilities inherently include credential harvesting. Article severity [CRIT] combined with 'Remote Access Trojan' classification indicates credential exfiltration is core objective. Pipeline missed RAT-specific credential access TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to credential stores (LSASS, credential manager, browser storage); monitor registry access to Credential Provider paths; flag screen capture API calls from RAT process trees or unusual child processes spawned from trojanized app (e.g., reg.exe, tasklist.exe, ipconfig.exe).

suggestion.title: Malicious Android App Installation from Play Store or Third-Party Store
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes '455 malicious apps' distributed at scale; typical initial access vector. Pipeline failed to surface detection for app installation anomalies despite this being the entry point for the entire attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of apps matching Trapdoor characteristics (family name, code signatures, publisher patterns). Baseline legitimate app installations against known Play Store publishers. Alert on bulk installations from third-party app stores or sideloading vectors.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated DEX and APK Signature Detection in Android Apps
suggestion.rationale: Ad fraud malware typically employs DEX obfuscation to evade static analysis. Title implies malware sophistication at scale (455 variants); pipeline should have flagged code obfuscation as key evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze installed APK files for DEX obfuscation patterns (stripped symbol tables, control flow flattening, string encryption). Flag apps with high obfuscation entropy and minimal readable strings matching legitimate libraries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ad Network Click and Impression Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Generate Fake Clicks' — the impact is fraudulent ad interactions. Pipeline completely missed detection for the attack's purpose: fake click generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ad network traffic from Android devices for abnormal click-through rates, rapid repeated clicks on same ad from single device, or clicks generating no user engagement. Baseline normal ad interaction patterns and alert on statistical outliers.

suggestion.title: Device Fingerprinting and Information Collection in Malicious Apps
suggestion.rationale: Ad fraud operators require device metadata (IMEI, Android ID, carrier, location) to target ad networks and coordinate fraud campaigns. Title indicates large-scale coordinated operation (455 apps); implies systematic device fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor apps for excessive queries to device identifiers (IMEI, Android ID, MAC address), location services, carrier information, or SIM details. Flag apps requesting INTERNET + READ_PHONE_STATE + FINE_LOCATION permissions together with no legitimate use case.

suggestion.title: C2 Command and Control Beaconing from Malicious Ad Fraud Apps
suggestion.rationale: Coordinating 455 malicious apps requires central command infrastructure. Pipeline should have flagged C2 communication patterns (callbacks, config fetch, botnet heartbeat) as likely detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS and HTTP traffic from Android devices for connections to C2 infrastructure. Alert on periodic beaconing patterns (fixed intervals), DGA-like domain patterns, or data exfiltration attempts. Correlate across multiple devices with same C2 endpoint.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Android Boot or Logon Autostart Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Ad fraud operation requires persistent presence on 455+ devices. Pipeline missed detection for persistence mechanisms (e.g., boot receivers, system partition placement) ensuring malware survives device restart.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze Android app manifests for BOOT_COMPLETED receivers without user-visible functionality. Monitor system partition modifications and installation of apps with boot-time startup. Flag apps with hidden persistence code unrelated to declared functionality.

suggestion.title: Session Token Abuse from Infostealer-Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers stole 'browser sessions and account credentials' and used them for unauthorized purchases. Phrase: 'session data...can be used to log in to the victim's account without needing credentials and...bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) checks.' No detection posture for this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect session tokens used for authentication from impossible travel geographies, concurrent sessions from different devices within minutes, or sessions replayed outside the typical client signature window. Stolen sessions lack expected browser user-agent consistency or device certificate patterns from legitimate logins.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass via Stolen Session Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article states session tokens 'can bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) checks.' Indicates a critical detection gap: legitimate MFA flows don't trigger on token-based auth, but session reuse from new geographies or devices should still alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication via session tokens from IPs with no prior association to the user's account, especially if MFA was bypassed (indicated by signin_risk_level='low' despite impossible-travel condition). Correlate session token use with device fingerprint changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Purchase Activity Post-Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers used 5,800 stolen credentials to make 'unauthorized purchases totaling about $721,000.' This is the measurable impact phase. Phrase: 'cybercriminals used 5,800 to make unauthorized purchases.' No detection for abnormal transaction patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline purchase velocity, payment method frequency, and shipping address diversity per user. Flag transactions exceeding 5x baseline quantity, using new payment methods stored by browser (from credential theft), or shipping to addresses never seen in 90-day history. Correlate with session token misuse timeframe.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot Communication for Stolen Data Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker infrastructure: 'information was then processed and sold through specialized online resources and Telegram bots.' This infrastructure communication is a C2 signal. No detection for lateral communication to data market facilitators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for client devices making TLS connections to Telegram API endpoints or telegram.org within 24-48 hours of infostealer infection indicators. Flag process execution of Telegram desktop client (unexpected on servers or production systems) communicating with known dark-market bot API patterns.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Transaction Anomalies Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'suspect engaged in cryptocurrency transactions with his accomplices' to move stolen funds. Phrase indicates money laundering signals. Detection gap: no baseline for spotting when legitimate user accounts suddenly initiate crypto transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for user crypto-exchange login patterns and transaction sizes. Alert on first-ever crypto transfers, transactions to newly-added wallets, or amounts exceeding prior patterns. Correlate with preceding account compromise indicators and geographic mismatch.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Malware Execution on Consumer Devices
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins with 'infostealer malware that secretly infected users' devices, collected login credentials.' Phrase establishes initial execution vector. No detection for malware execution or process behavior typical of credential-stealing tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or poorly-signed executables making repeated calls to browser credential stores, passwords APIs, or cookie jar locations. Monitor for spawning of rundll32/powershell to extract browser session data. Flag processes with high entropy outbound connections to C2 servers immediately after credential access.

suggestion.title: Ethereum Smart Contract C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Uses Ethereum Smart Contracts for ... C2 Infrastructure.' Pipeline missed the core attack vector. Detection should identify hosts making periodic queries to blockchain nodes and smart contract addresses, correlating with subsequent command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts with recurring outbound connections to Ethereum node IPs (TCP 8545, 8546) or Infura/Alchemy endpoints, where connection patterns coincide with process execution within 60 seconds. Smart contract interaction (web3 calls, eth_call/eth_sendTransaction) indicates C2 command retrieval. Alert on non-developer machines exhibiting this pattern.

suggestion.title: Smart Contract State Exfiltration for C2 Commands
suggestion.rationale: Title describes blockchain smart contracts as C2 mechanism; 'seizure-resistant' implies commands persist in immutable state. Pipeline failed to identify how botnet retrieves and executes commands stored in contract state variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for hosts decoding hex-encoded or base64 payloads retrieved from Ethereum blockchain transactions or contract ABI calls. Look for patterns where raw data from web3 library calls (eth_getStorageAt, eth_call returns) is decoded and immediately executed via powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or script interpreters. Correlate decoded strings with process command lines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ethereum Node / RPC Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Ethereum Smart Contracts'—implying discovery or reconnaissance of blockchain infrastructure. Pipeline missed initial-access or discovery phase where botnet or attacker probes for Ethereum nodes or public RPC endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes (especially those spawned by office macros, browsers, or scripts) that enumerate common Ethereum node ports (8545, 8546, 9545) or public RPC endpoints (infura.io, alchemy.com, quicknode.com). Alert on sequential connection attempts across multiple Ethereum endpoints or wallet address enumeration via eth_getBalance queries.

suggestion.title: Wallet Address Enumeration for Victim Status Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Botnet using 'seizure-resistant' blockchain C2 implies persistent victim tracking via wallet addresses or contract identifiers. Pipeline missed detection of bots querying blockchain to check victim status or retrieve wallet balances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated eth_getBalance or eth_call queries to the same set of wallet addresses from botnet-infected hosts. Detect patterns where a single host queries 50+ unique addresses in sequence, typical of botnets tracking victim payment or status via blockchain. Correlate with known blockchain explorer APIs (etherscan.io, blockscout).

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Command Execution Post-Blockchain-Query Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes blockchain as C2 mechanism; pipeline failed to correlate blockchain node connectivity with subsequent process execution. This is the closure of the C2 loop—data retrieval followed by command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build 60-second correlation rule: Identify hosts with outbound traffic to Ethereum nodes/RPC endpoints followed by anomalous process creation (unsigned binaries, living-off-the-land tools). Alert on patterns where network queries occur 30–60 seconds before script execution or system modifications, indicating C2 command fetch-and-execute cycle.

suggestion.title: Non-Standard Ethereum Node Port Abuse for C2 Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain infrastructure typically uses alternative ports (8545, 8546, 9545); 'seizure-resistant' C2 implies obfuscation. Pipeline did not identify non-standard port communication as evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect hosts initiating outbound connections to Ethereum node standard (8545, 8546) and non-standard ports (9545, 8080, custom ranges) to avoid firewall/proxy detection. Alert on connections to these ports from machines without a legitimate blockchain development/mining justification. Correlate with process ancestry to rule out developers.

suggestion.title: Webworm/EchoCreep Discord C&C Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'Deploys EchoCreep...Using Discord' as C&C channel. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for Discord-based backdoor communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from production systems to Discord API endpoints (discord.com, cdn.discordapp.com) with unusual frequency or timing. Alert on Discord bot token creation from non-development hosts. Detect Discord webhook registrations followed by process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: GraphWorm MS Graph API Abuse and Token Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'GraphWorm Backdoors Using...MS Graph API' indicating unauthorized Graph API activity. Zero detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous Microsoft Graph API calls from compromised service principals or user accounts (high volume, off-hours, unusual scopes like Mail.Send or User.ReadWrite.All). Alert on new OAuth app registrations followed by Graph API activity. Flag Graph API token exfiltration via unusual authentication paths.

suggestion.title: Webworm Backdoor Initial Execution and Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Deploys...Backdoors'—execution and persistence are implicit kill-chain steps not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unsigned executables or living-off-the-land tool execution (powershell, cmd, cscript) spawning unusual child processes or performing network connections. Detect DLL injection patterns into system processes. Alert on execution from temporary directories or recycling bin with subsequent Discord/Graph API network activity.

suggestion.title: MS Graph API Persistence via Mail Forwarding and Delegated Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Using MS Graph API for backdoor suggests account manipulation or persistence mechanisms. Article title implies multi-tenant environment targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of mail forwarding rules via Graph API from service principals. Alert on delegation of 'Mail.Send', 'Calendar.ReadWrite', or other sensitive scopes to previously unknown or low-trust applications. Monitor for mass permission grants to OAuth apps within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Webworm C&C Callback Pattern Recognition—Discord + Graph API Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Dual-channel C&C (Discord + MS Graph) suggests command execution relay pattern. Pipeline should detect behavioral clustering of both channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Discord API calls with Graph API calls from same source IP/user within 5-minute windows. Alert when both channels activate simultaneously on previously dormant accounts. Detect Graph API exfiltration (Mail.Read, User.Read, Drive.Read) immediately preceded by Discord webhook triggers.

suggestion.title: Webworm Reconnaissance—Enterprise Directory Enumeration via Graph API
suggestion.rationale: MS Graph API abuse for backdoor implies prior reconnaissance of target environment structure. Title does not exclude reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk Graph API calls to enumerate users, groups, organizational hierarchy (directory objects, team membership). Alert on service principal requesting 'Organization.Read.All' or 'Directory.Read.All' scopes without justification. Flag discovery queries clustered before persistence or exfiltration activities.

suggestion.title: Claude Code Network Sandbox Escape Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Network Sandbox Vulnerability.' This is a privilege-escalation/process-boundary-bypass vector. Zero use cases were generated for sandbox escape despite this being the core attack surface.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration and Theft Post-Sandbox-Escape
suggestion.rationale: Title states: 'Exposes User Credentials.' After sandbox compromise, attackers harvest credentials. No detection use case exists for post-escalation credential access.

suggestion.title: Source Code Repository Bulk Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states: 'Exposes Source Code.' No use case was generated to detect archive creation, large file reads, or network transmission of .git directories or source trees.

suggestion.rationale: HIGH-severity designation implies specific version(s) are vulnerable. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs—expected minimum: vulnerable version identifiers or build fingerprints. Detection use case needed to flag at-risk deployments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VS Code Extension Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: malicious 'Nx Console VS Code Extension'—attack vector is compromised extension installed from marketplace. Extension code executes in VS Code context with full access to local credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation and activation (extensions directory writes, extension activation events). Baseline known extensions per user and alert on new installations of dev tools (Nx, build tools) that correlate with subsequent network anomalies or credential access.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Reconnaissance and Exfiltration via Stolen Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached'—requires compromised credentials. Malicious extension harvests GitHub tokens from local git config or VSCode auth context, then enumerates/exfiltrates repos via API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid GitHub API calls (GET /repos, GET /contents) from development machines to api.github.com, especially outside business hours or from first-time callers. Flag unauthorized token usage in unexpected geolocations. Alert on bulk repository cloning or tar/zip export via API followed by exfiltration to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Source Code Exfiltration from Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Breach of 'internal repositories' implies attacker extracted proprietary code. Malicious extension likely archives and sends repositories to attacker C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tar/zip creation of .git directories followed by large outbound transfers to non-whitelisted destinations. Flag VS Code or node.exe child processes with unexpected network connections to uncommon ports/protocols. Correlate file compression with exfiltration using time-proximity rules.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Local Git Credentials and SSH Keys
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension runs with user privileges; can access ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, .git-credentials, and GitHub PAT tokens stored in shell history or git config.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file reads from VS Code/node.exe processes accessing SSH key directories (~/.ssh), git credential helpers, or .netrc. Flag when these accesses are followed by process execution of curl/wget or base64 encoding detected via command-line monitoring.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Connections from VS Code to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension exfiltrates stolen data and receives command directives from attacker C2. Article describes breach implying active communication channel.

Alert on encrypted outbound traffic (HTTPS) to newly registered or low-reputation domains. Correlate with file exfiltration timing.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Extension Auto-Update Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension persists by abusing VS Code's built-in auto-update feature; updates could be silently applied without user interaction.

Alert on extension code execution that deviates from expected behavior (network calls to non-npm/GitHub domains, credential access, process spawning).

suggestion.title: Gremlin Stealer PE Resource Section Decryption and C2 Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'C2 URLs and Exfiltration Paths in Encrypted Resource Sections'—pipeline missed detection for accessing/decrypting PE .rsrc sections. Resource obfuscation is Gremlin's primary evasion mechanism.

Hunt for processes (rundll32, cmd, explorer, svchost) reading from non-standard PE sections (.rsrc, .reloc), performing bitwise operations (XOR, RC4) on extracted bytes in memory, and resolving strings matching domain patterns.

suggestion.title: Gremlin Stealer C2 Beaconing to Resource-Derived Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'C2 URLs' and 'Exfiltration Paths'—pipeline should detect outbound C2 communication to attacker-controlled endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-resource-decryption, Gremlin establishes C2 over HTTP/HTTPS. Detect parent processes spawning from suspicious executables making repeated connections to previously unknown external IPs/domains with regular timing intervals, consistent payload sizes, and User-Agent strings anomalous for the parent process.

suggestion.title: Gremlin Stealer Browser and System Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Stealer classification implies credential theft. Article mentions 'exfiltration'—infer harvesting of passwords, cookies, and tokens from browsers and credential vaults.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Gremlin accesses browser credential stores (Chrome User Data/Login Data, Firefox Places.sqlite, Edge LocalState) and Windows credential manager. Hunt for suspicious processes querying HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Protected Storage or accessing %APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data with FILE_READ_DATA+FILE_WRITE_DATA.

suggestion.title: Gremlin Stealer Data Exfiltration to C2 Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Exfiltration Paths'—pipeline should detect bulk data theft. Stealer malware compresses harvested credentials and uploads to C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After harvesting, Gremlin packages stolen data (typically .rar/.zip) in %TEMP% and initiates outbound HTTP(S) POST with large payloads (>512 KB) to C2 domains. Detect process creating compressed archives from credential directories, followed by network upload to beaconing infrastructure identified from resource decryption phase.

suggestion.title: Gremlin Stealer Execution via LOLBin and Unsigned DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Gremlin Stealer' malware—pipeline should detect execution signatures. Stealer variants execute as rundll32, regsvcs, or MSBuild with unsigned/dropped DLLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Gremlin execution often follows phishing delivery. Detect suspicious parent-child: explorer.exe/winword.exe → cmd.exe/powershell.exe → rundll32.exe with DLL in %TEMP% or ProgramData, or direct rundll32 execution with inline export matching Gremlin signatures, preceded by recent file download or email attachment access.

suggestion.title: Drupal RCE Exploitation Attempt via Serialization Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'RCE Attacks'—the vulnerability enables remote code execution. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the central threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal installations for malicious serialized objects (PHP object notation: O:*) in request bodies or parameters, particularly targeting known gadget chains. Flag POST requests to serialization-vulnerable endpoints (field handling, entity handlers) with encoded payloads from external sources.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Drupal Core Version in Production Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Drupal Core Flaw'—affected versions and patch status are primary IOCs. Pipeline extracted zero version information.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Drupal version via HTTP headers (Server), changelog.txt, or CHANGELOG.md endpoints. Cross-reference against CVE database for RCE-critical versions. Alert inventory teams on unpatched Drupal Core installations within 24h of disclosure.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Backend Compromise Signals from Web Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL Sites'—post-RCE execution will generate database queries from web-server process. Pipeline missed this post-exploitation indicator chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs for queries originating from web application processes (apache, php-fpm, nginx) with anomalous table access patterns, bulk data queries, or privilege escalation attempts post-infection.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution from Drupal Web Root
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies code execution on the server. Pipeline failed to generate detection covering unexpected executable context within web application directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell_exec, system(), or exec() function calls within Drupal core or module paths. Correlate with POST request patterns or web requests to suspicious parameters. Flag processes spawned from php-fpm or Apache processes executing non-standard binaries.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Outbound Database Proxy Connections
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically leads to data theft. Article threat model includes 'Exposes' data—detection should cover exfiltration via compromised database connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound database connections from compromised Drupal servers to external hosts or cloud storage (S3, Azure Blobs). Flag large data transfers over PostgreSQL or secondary tunneled connections initiated post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Remote Access Tool Installation from Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Tech-support fraud workflow requires remote access tool deployment (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, etc.) following social engineering. The article title establishes 'tech-support fraud' as the vector; pipeline should detect execution of known RAT tools post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, chrome remote desktop) initiated by non-IT users during business hours or in rapid succession with failed login attempts. Cross-correlate with email logs for phishing campaigns in preceding 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing with Subsequent Valid Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Tech-support fraud schemes rely on credential theft through phishing emails/pages. Article context establishes credential access as primary attack vector; missing detection for phishing payloads delivering credential stealer malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email messages with credential harvesting payloads (fake login pages, form-grabber attachments) followed within 48 hours by successful logon from anomalous IP address or geographic location inconsistent with user baseline. Flag if logon precedes large data transfer.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Data Transfer Post-Remote Access Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Tech-support fraud terminal objective is data theft or financial fraud. Article establishes large-scale victim targeting; pipeline missed detection for exfiltration phase following remote access compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large volume outbound transfers to non-corporate IPs within 2 hours of remote access tool activation. Monitor for archive/compression utilities (7zip, rar, winrar) executed by RAT process or child processes, followed by outbound SMB/HTTPS data exfiltration to overseas IPs.

suggestion.title: India-Based IP Geolocation Anomaly in Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article context establishes India-based fraud ring; pipeline should detect administrative logons or sensitive system access originating from Indian ISP ranges inconsistent with organizational baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful RDP/SSH logon from Indian IP ranges (confirmed fraud actor infrastructure) to administrative accounts or servers during off-hours. Cross-reference IP reputation feeds and compare to baseline user access patterns. Flag if logon immediately precedes file enumeration or credential dumping activity.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Phishing Campaign from Spoofed Legitimate Domain
suggestion.rationale: Tech-support fraud initiates via email/phone social engineering. Article title indicates organized multi-victim scheme; pipeline should detect mass phishing campaigns using domain impersonation or lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk email campaigns with lookalike or typosquat domains (e.g., microsoft-supprt.com, apple-security.net) requesting user credentials or prompting urgent action. Cross-correlate message body keywords ('verify account', 'confirm identity', 'urgent') with known phishing templates. Alert if recipient clicks link and authenticates from the phishing domain server.

suggestion.title: Legal Entity / Executive Name Attribution from Fraud Enforcement Action
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Two U.S. Executives Plead Guilty'—names, company affiliations, and organizational structure should be extracted for threat intelligence. Pipeline failed to identify or attribute the fraud organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract executive names, company names, call center locations, phone number ranges, email domain registrations, and bank account details from enforcement action. Correlate with historical phishing campaigns, malware C2 registrations, and documented victim complaints. Flag all associated infrastructure for network indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation and Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Nx Console v18.95.0 as malicious Marketplace extension delivering credential-theft payload to developer workstations. Attack: extension installation → subprocess execution → credential harvesting from local Git/SSH/AWS storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VSCode parent (code.exe) spawning child processes with unusual privileges or file access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git, ~/.aws, ~/.kube/config. Monitor extension installation events correlated with immediate credential-access events or outbound network beaconing to non-Marketplace infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Enumeration with Stolen Developer Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates stolen GitHub tokens extracted from local git config used for repository discovery and access enumeration. Attack pattern: credential extraction → API reconnaissance of accessible repos → staging for exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for repeated GitHub API calls (GET /user/repos, /user/keys, /user/installations, /search) from same auth token across different source IPs or unusual geographic patterns. Alert on token reuse across process contexts (shell, Python, curl) within short timeframe after credential-access indicators.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Cloning and Source Code Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised developer credentials enabling large-scale GitHub repository cloning for source-code theft. Detection should cover abnormal git clone volume, targeting multiple private repos, or exfiltration to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git clone operations for unusual velocity (multiple repos cloned rapidly), targeting private repositories, or git protocol traffic to non-standard ports or attacker-controlled infrastructure. Correlate with stolen token indicators and credential-access events. Alert on repository archival (tar/zip) immediately followed by large file exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Local Developer Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates Nx Console and supply-chain malware harvesting SSH keys, git credentials, and cloud-provider tokens from developer environment. Core attack vector: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.git/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.azure/* file access by non-credential-manager processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process file access to sensitive developer paths: private key reads from ~/.ssh/, config reads from ~/.git/, credential scraping from ~/.aws/credentials or ~/.kube/config. Alert on credential-tool processes (ssh-agent, git-credential) spawned by non-standard parents (extension, malware). Correlate with network exfiltration of credential-like data.

suggestion.title: Compromised Supply-Chain Package Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes durabletask PyPI compromise and malicious Nx Console Marketplace extension delivery. Detection covers package manager installation of known-malicious versions and immediate suspicious post-install behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/npm execution for installation of known-compromised package versions (e.g., durabletask, Nx Console v18.95.0) or packages from unsigned/newly-registered publishers. Alert on VS Code extension installation from non-verified Marketplace vendors. Correlate package installation with immediate spawning of credential-theft or C2 processes.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing and Credential Exfiltration from Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious extensions and packages establishing persistent C2 for ongoing credential harvesting and command dispatch. Attack: extension execution → C2 registration → periodic beacon with exfiltrated credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from VSCode, Python, or package-manager processes to newly-registered or threat-intel flagged C2 domains. Alert on beaconing patterns (regular interval connections at fixed hours or byte counts). Detect DNS queries for infrastructure associated with Nx Console, durabletask, or GitHub Actions spoofing campaigns. Correlate C2 communication with credential-access and exfiltration timeframe.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Agent Lateral Movement via Scripted Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly frames Agent AI threat readiness; typical threat narratives in this domain discuss automated agents executing commands or scripts without human interaction. Article body was not readable due to parsing failure, but title strongly indicates agent execution at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, suspicious process spawning from a single parent (e.g., Python, Node.js, bash) with arguments suggesting script execution or automation frameworks. Alert on anomalous command patterns consistent with agent-directed lateral movement (e.g., credential passing, remote execution invocations, service enumeration).

suggestion.title: Agent AI C2 Callback Detection via Anomalous Outbound HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Agent-based attacks typically establish command-and-control channels. Article title emphasizes preparedness for agent threats; standard agent payloads beacon to C2 infrastructure for tasking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTPS destination diversity per host. Alert on endpoints initiating connections to low-reputation or newly-registered domains at regular intervals (heartbeat pattern). Correlate with process telemetry to attribute to suspicious binaries (interpreted languages, reverse shells).

suggestion.title: Agent AI Credential Harvesting via Memory Dumping or Registry Access
suggestion.rationale: Autonomous agents operating in multi-user or sensitive environments will attempt credential access. Article premise is agent readiness/threat; credential theft is a primary agent objective in enterprise compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Handle/Registry access to HKLM\SAM, HKLM\SECURITY, or credential manager paths. Detect calls to ntdump, procdump, or MiniDump APIs. Alert on LSASS process access from non-system, non-svchost contexts. Correlate with ProcessCreationEvents for suspicious parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: RPC Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'crafted RPC request that triggers an overflow during path canonicalization'—concrete attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection for exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for malformed RPC packets targeting port 135 (Windows RPC Endpoint Mapper) on Windows Server systems, particularly patterns consistent with buffer overflow payloads. Correlate source IP reputation and packet fragmentation anomalies. Baseline against legitimate RPC client tools.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4250 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline missed the asset inventory/scanning use case entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check all Windows systems exposing RPC services on TCP 135 against patch compliance baseline. Flag systems where vendor OS version is below patched threshold (post-2008 Windows Server 2003 SP2 or later). Generate exception list for EOL systems and correlate with network segmentation controls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from RPC Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code'—exploitation would result in code execution. Pipeline did not generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by services.exe or svchost.exe handling RPC traffic (particularly on port 135). Baseline known RPC-triggered service processes. Flag interactive-shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or unusual binary paths from RPC service context as high-fidelity indicator of post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Windows RPC Service Crash and Recovery Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow exploitation typically causes service crashes. Article mentions 'Windows Server Service' as vulnerable component. Pipeline missed sentinel event pattern for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Windows RPC service (svchost.exe -k rpcss) crashes/restarts with preceding anomalous RPC network traffic on port 135. Alert on repeated crash-restart cycles within 5-minute windows. Collect memory dumps from crashed RPC service processes and review kernel debugger output for overflow signatures in stack traces.

suggestion.title: DirectX quartz.dll Parser Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted QuickTime media file' processed by 'QuickTime Movie Parser Filter in quartz.dll'. No detection logic was generated despite explicit execution outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of child processes, DLL loads, or elevated privileges from media player processes (e.g., Windows Media Player, iexplore.exe) following receipt or opening of .mov or .qt media files. Monitor for quartz.dll crashes or code injection patterns post-file-open.

suggestion.title: Suspicious QuickTime Media File Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article attack vector is 'crafted QuickTime media file' — attack requires file delivery/receipt but no intake detection suggested. Article phrase: 'arbitrary code via a crafted QuickTime media file'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag uncommon .mov or .qt file downloads from external/suspicious sources, especially via email attachments or untrusted web hosts. Correlate with subsequent crashes or spawned processes from media-processing binaries within 60 seconds of file creation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2009-1537 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and publishes federal remediation deadline (2026-06-03) — no asset-exposure or patch-status detection use case generated despite explicit urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unpatched or outdated Microsoft DirectX versions and quartz.dll presence on end-user systems, especially media-facing workstations. Flag assets still running vulnerable DirectX builds post-patch-due-date (2026-06-03) as incident candidates.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Media File Size or Binary Signature Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'NULL byte overwrite' exploitation — detection should hunt for malformed or suspiciously-crafted QuickTime files that differ from benign samples. Article phrase: 'NULL byte overwrite vulnerability in the QuickTime Movie Parser Filter'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor QuickTime media files for null-byte sequences, truncated headers, or binary anomalies in file structure. Flag malformed or suspicious .mov files before they reach vulnerable parsers using YARA/binary analysis or file-magic validation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2009-3459 Vulnerable Software Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Adobe Acrobat and Reader contain a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability' with explicit federal patch due date '2026-06-03'. Requires immediate software inventory scan and patch-lag correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Defender VULN, Qualys, Nessus) for Adobe Reader and Acrobat versions pre-dating CVE-2009-3459 patch release. Correlate against endpoint inventory to identify systems with patch lag. Alert on at-risk assets, especially high-value targets (finance, engineering, C-suite workstations) with unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Adobe Reader/Acrobat Process Crash & Heap Corruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'crafted PDF file that triggers memory corruption'—heap overflow exploits manifest as process crashes, access violations, or abnormal process termination post-PDF load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AcroRd32.exe and Acrobat.exe for unexpected crashes, memory access violations, or abnormal exits immediately following PDF file open events. Alert on heap corruption indicators (memory exception codes). Correlate PDF file operation with child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) as post-exploitation RCE indicator.

suggestion.title: Malicious PDF Attachment Email-Based Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector as 'crafted PDF file'—standard delivery for PDF exploits is email attachment/phishing, typical for 2009-era vulnerability reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt email gateway logs for PDF attachments sent to external recipients or from untrusted senders. Flag suspicious patterns: obfuscated filenames, mismatched file magic bytes, bypass of email sandbox analysis. Correlate attachment extraction/write-to-disk with subsequent Adobe Reader process spawning on recipient machine.

suggestion.title: Post-PDF Processing Arbitrary Code Execution Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code'—must detect code execution chain following successful PDF-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish temporal correlation: PDF file open → parent process (AcroRd32.exe/Acrobat.exe) → child process spawn (system interpreter, unsigned binary, %TEMP% execution). Alert on any Adobe Reader/Acrobat spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, or rundll32.exe. Flag registry modifications (HKLM\RUN, task scheduler) immediately post-PDF processing as persistence setup.

suggestion.title: CVE-2010-0806 Detection in Vulnerability Scanner Results
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]'. Must detect CVE-2010-0806 in scanning infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners detect CVE-2010-0806. Correlate with software inventory to identify systems with Internet Explorer installed. Flag all findings immediately given federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-03.

suggestion.title: IE Process Anomaly Detection Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'use-after-free vulnerability...remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via vectors involving access to an invalid pointer'. Post-exploitation detection must hunt abnormal child processes from iexplore.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child processes spawned from iexplore.exe (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, certutil.exe, rundll32.exe). Flag DLL injection into IE, code execution from IE temp directories, or IE spawning system utilities with privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched IE Inventory Before Federal Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-03. Inventory hunt must identify all systems with unpatched IE versions before deadline approaches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for systems with Internet Explorer version below patched threshold. Enumerate days remaining to 2026-06-03. Generate prioritized remediation list for desktop/endpoint teams. Cross-reference with open tickets to ensure tracking.

suggestion.title: Remote IE Exploitation Attempt Detection (Network)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'remote attackers' and implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets'. Network-based detection required to catch initial exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on known IE exploit server C2 beacons, malformed HTTP requests exploiting IE parsing logic, or suspicious binary downloads to IE cache directory (typically %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Temporary Internet Files). Monitor for connections to infrastructure attributed to IE zero-day campaigns.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched Microsoft Defender Instances CVE-2026-41091
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for this CVE. Primary detection use case for CISA KEV entries is scanning for vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-41091 against deployed Defender versions and running process telemetry. Flag systems running Defender versions below patch threshold. Alert on systems where vulnerability scan reports vulnerability but no patch event recorded.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Microsoft Defender Link Following CVE-2026-41091
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally'—explicit privilege escalation kill-chain phase. Pipeline missed this detection requirement entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege elevation attempts originating from Microsoft Defender process or child processes spawned by Defender service. Track token elevation from standard user to SYSTEM/admin context. Alert on suspicious registry modifications or sensitive file operations executed with elevated context under Defender process scope.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Deadline Tracking: CVE-2026-41091 Federal Remediation Due 2026-06-03
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline 2026-06-03 with explicit requirement that 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Pipeline missed temporal compliance detection window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily inventory report: systems unpatched for CVE-2026-41091 grouped by days-to-deadline. Escalating alerts at 14-day, 7-day, and 1-day thresholds before 2026-06-03. Flag any systems still reporting vulnerable Defender version post-deadline as noncompliant.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Service Crash or Restart Anomaly (CVE-2026-45498 Impact Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows for denial of service.' Pipeline missed detection for the actual impact mechanism. Exploitation should trigger process termination, service unavailability, or watchdog-enforced restarts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal termination or restart of Microsoft Defender processes (MsMpEng.exe, WinDefend service) preceded by or correlating with suspicious input or network activity. Alert on rapid process crashes within short time window, service recovery cycles, or KERNEL_CRASH entries in event logs indicating DoS impact.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Microsoft Defender Version Inventory (CVE-2026-45498 Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides patch deadline (2026-06-03). Pipeline missed inventory detection—organizations require immediate visibility into unpatched Defender instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint management, vulnerability scanners, and WSUS for Microsoft Defender version < patched build. Flag instances still running vulnerable versions post-remediation deadline. Correlate with public-facing asset inventories to assess T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) risk.

suggestion.title: Post-Deadline Patch Compliance Check (CVE-2026-45498, Federal Due 2026-06-03)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline. Pipeline missed compliance-driven detection. Post-deadline, unpatched instances are active breach triggers and audit findings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-06-03, alert on any Microsoft Defender instance not at CVE-2026-45498 patch level. Include SLA for remediation and flag deviations for compliance reporting. New installations of unpatched Defender versions post-deadline warrant immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt via Malformed Input to Defender Service (CVE-2026-45498)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unspecified vulnerability' without technical vector details. Detection should focus on behavioral anomalies (malformed inputs, API abuse) that precede crash indicators and may be observable at network/API layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious calls to Microsoft Defender APIs, RPC endpoints, or service interfaces from untrusted sources. Alert on abnormally large payloads, repeated API errors, or malformed requests preceding service crashes. Prioritize process-interaction anomalies and network noise from potential exploit sources.

suggestion.title: NFC Relay Transaction Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'NFC relay attacks'—the core attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection around this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android devices for rapid NFC reader initialization followed by unexpected payment/credential transactions. Alert on multiple NFC transactions from same device within short time windows, especially when device location indicates card-present environment (retail terminals, ATMs).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Admin Permission Grants
suggestion.rationale: Title states malware 'traps victims' via 'kiosk mode,' which requires device admin privileges. Article implies credential access via relay—both require elevated permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device admin permission requests to apps with low/unknown publisher reputation or apps requesting NFC+DeviceAdmin together. Monitor for grants that persist after initial install, suggesting persistent kiosk lock-down setup.

suggestion.title: Kiosk Mode Activation Outside MDM Policy
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes kiosk mode as mechanism to 'trap victims.' Pipeline missed defense-evasion tactic explicitly stated in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected kiosk mode enablement on consumer devices (non-enterprise) or activation triggered by non-system, non-MDM apps. Alert on kiosk mode that disables HOME button, disables Settings access, or traps user in single foreground app for >5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Process/Window Confinement Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'trap victims during NFC relay attacks' indicates forced confinement to malicious UI. Pipeline generated zero detection around this behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent foreground app activity spanning >60 seconds with back-button interception, home-button disable, or recents-task list hiding. Correlate with NFC activity to identify relay attack confinement patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via NFC Relay—Payment Terminal Simulation
suggestion.rationale: NFC relay attacks imply credential/payment data interception. Article describes 'relay attacks' requiring C2 infrastructure to redirect/capture card data.
