suggestion.rationale: VS Code extensions have access to git credentials, SSH keys, API tokens stored in environment or .env files. Article describes tool compromise; exfiltration of secrets is a primary payload. Article describes compromise but pipeline should surface credential theft as primary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when VSCode.exe or extension processes read .env files, ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, token caches, or registry credential stores (HKCU\Software\GitCredentialManager). Correlate with network exfiltration or parent process creation from unexpected paths.

suggestion.title: Source Code / Workspace Exfiltration from VS Code
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension in user's IDE with access to open workspaces. Attacker can steal entire codebases, IP, secrets in source. 'Compromised' extension implies code theft / IP exfiltration as likely secondary payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file read or compression of source code directories (src/, lib/, .git/) by VSCode.exe or child processes followed by network transfer. Flag if file I/O access is anomalous (e.g., extension reading outside workspace, unexpected tar/zip creation, network write to unfamiliar IP).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines often have elevated access to repos, CI/CD, internal infrastructure. Compromised extension can become pivot point. Article severity (HIGH) and target audience (developers) suggest lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by VSCode (git clone, ssh, curl to internal hosts, kubectl) or credentials re-used on anomalous hosts after extension installation. Flag if VSCode triggers connections to internal infrastructure, builds, or artifact repositories outside normal development patterns.

suggestion.title: ROADtools Execution and Azure Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords establish ROADtools as primary attack vector; open-source framework misused for cloud intrusions requires execution detection paired with discovery-phase Graph API calls
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ROADtools Python execution or Azure CLI/PowerShell commands (Get-AzureADUser, Invoke-GraphRequest) launching high-volume Microsoft Graph API calls to /users, /groups, /devices endpoints within minutes, signaling post-compromise reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Microsoft Graph API Enumeration Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools core capability: enumerate Entra ID users, groups, and devices via Graph API; article emphasizes Graph API abuse as discovery phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single user/service principal issuing 50+ Graph API calls to directory endpoints (directoryObjects, users, groups) within 10 minutes, especially from non-standard client IPs or user agents.

suggestion.title: Token Theft and Replay via Service Principal Refresh Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state persistence mechanism: stealing and replaying refresh tokens to maintain access; article discusses cloud credential compromise as persistence vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect refresh token requests from new service principals or application accounts, especially those created in same session as Graph API enumeration, followed by token reuse from geographical outliers.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Azure Role Assignment to Attacker-Controlled Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes nation-state tactics moving from discovery to persistence; role assignment to newly created service principal is documented escalation pattern in cloud compromises
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Owner, Contributor, or Global Administrator role assignment to service principals created in same session or within 2 hours of suspicious API activity; flag if assigner is user account not in admin group.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Service Principal Creation by Compromised User Account
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persistence mechanism: attackers create hidden service principals after establishing Entra ID foothold; article emphasizes nation-state persistence tactics
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service principal or application registration creation by user accounts lacking application management role, especially creation timestamps within hours of Graph API enumeration or token request anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Exfiltration via OneDrive or SharePoint API Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After Entra ID compromise, nation-state actors use Graph API to enumerate and exfiltrate data from cloud storage; article implies data access as attack objective
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service principals or compromised accounts issuing bulk download or copy commands to OneDrive/SharePoint after Graph API discovery phase, especially targeting sensitive file types or multiple users' shares.

suggestion.title: RDP Brute Force or Anomalous Access from Suspicious Geographies
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Russian Threat Groups Use RDP...for Initial Access'—a primary attack vector—yet pipeline generated zero RDP-focused detection. T1021.001 is a foundational technique requiring both brute-force and session-anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed RDP login bursts (>10 failures in 5 min from single source IP), successful logins from geographies inconsistent with user profile, and successful RDP sessions followed immediately by unusual process execution or file access patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Trusted Vendor Software or Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Supply Chain Attacks' as initial-access vector. No detection use case generated despite T1199 being critical for supply-chain persistence and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process execution from vendor-controlled processes, unexpected egress traffic from vendor software to known attacker infrastructure, and privilege-escalation attempts originating from third-party vendor service accounts.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Social Engineering Campaign Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Social Engineering' as initial-access vector. Zero detection use case generated despite phishing/credential-harvesting being foundational to multi-stage compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spearphishing emails with malicious links or attachments targeting sensitive roles, followed by credential-entry events, impossible-travel indicators, or new-device logins within 24 hours of phishing delivery.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Anomalies and Lateral Movement via VPN Tunnels
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Russian Threat Groups Use...VPN...for Initial Access' but pipeline produced no VPN-related detections. This is a critical gap for both access compromise and lateral-movement persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed VPN authentication bursts from single IP, successful logins from new geographies or off-hours, and lateral movement patterns from VPN entry points to internal systems inconsistent with user baseline (e.g., access to domain controllers or admin shares).

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Registry Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly states 'AppDomainManager hijacking' as attack method; no detection use case generated. Screening Serpens uses this for persistent .NET code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKLM/HKCU with 'AppDomainManager' or 'AppInitialize' in path; correlate with rare .NET loader processes (AppHost, etc.). Flag unsigned/untrusted assemblies loaded via registry-specified paths.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading from Suspicious Paths
suggestion.rationale: Keywords list 'DLL Sideloading' as explicit technique; pipeline generated zero detection. Core Screening Serpens TTPs per article description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DLL loads from non-standard directories (temp, downloads, profile) by legitimate Windows/Office processes. Correlate with unusual .DLL naming or obfuscated filenames. Cross-reference parent process to detect search-order manipulation.

suggestion.title: MiniJunk/MiniUpdate RAT Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new RAT variants MiniJunk, MiniUpdate' with no IOCs extracted and no signature-based detection. These are named malware families requiring specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known MiniJunk/MiniUpdate hashes and file signatures. Monitor for .NET process spawning with suspicious command-line patterns (base64, obfuscated C2, embedded URLs). Flag network connections to uncommon ports from identified malware processes.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Phishing Campaign Detection (Screening Serpens)
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'social engineering' and 'operation security'; no initial-access detection generated. Social engineering is documented entry vector for Iranian APT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with Iranian language, spoofed defense/tech company domains, or macro-enabled Office attachments. Monitor for unusual attachment execution patterns (zip → macro → DLL). Flag user interactions with phishing links leading to secondary payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Runtime Invocation by Foreign Process
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'tech and defense sectors' with AppDomainManager + RAT; no detection for anomalous .NET execution chains. Critical for catching supply-chain or lateral-movement scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-standard processes (notepad, calc, explorer, Office) invoking CLR.dll, System.Runtime.InteropServices, or AppHost. Monitor for .NET assembly reflection/invocation with unusual argument patterns or unsigned assembly loading.

suggestion.title: Apex One Server Directory Traversal Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability exploitation step: 'directory traversal vulnerability in the Apex One (on-premise) server could allow a pre-authenticated local attacker to modify a key table.' Article confirms active exploitation but pipeline generated zero detection coverage for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Apex One server filesystem for directory traversal patterns (../, ..\ sequences, symbolic link operations) in file access logs targeting server configuration and key storage directories. Establish baseline for legitimate admin activity and alert on anomalies from authenticated accounts outside scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Apex One Critical Key Table Modification
suggestion.rationale: Direct attack payload delivery: 'pre-authenticated local attacker to modify a key table on the server to inject malicious code.' This is the pivot point enabling supply-chain corruption but appears nowhere in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes/modifications to Apex One registry keys and configuration files (HKLM\SOFTWARE\TrendMicro) outside change control windows. Correlate with concurrent suspicious process activity (script execution, compilation, binary staging) in the same security context. Establish per-environment baseline of legitimate update patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Apex One Agent Package Deployment Outside Maintenance Windows
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation lateral movement: 'inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations.' Pipeline missed detection for abnormal agent deployment patterns despite this being the infection vector to enterprise endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Apex One server for agent package modifications and deployments occurring outside documented patch windows. Track file hash and size changes to agent distribution payloads. Correlate package modifications with suspicious admin activity and key table changes on the same system within same time window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution from Apex One Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: Endpoint impact: malicious code 'deploy[ed] to agents on affected installations' will execute on protected systems. Pipeline failed to generate any endpoint-level detection despite organization-wide blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish behavioral baseline of legitimate Apex One agent child processes per environment. Alert on agent spawning PowerShell, cmd.exe, certutil, bitsadmin, or other LOLBins with suspicious arguments. Correlate process execution timing to recent agent updates or deployments. Flag network connections from agent processes to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Apex One Server Compromised Admin Account Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation prerequisite: 'a potential attacker must have access to the Apex One Server and already obtained administrative credentials.' Detecting anomalous admin behavior reveals compromised credentials enabling this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Apex One server admin logins by user, time-of-day, source IP, and logon type. Alert on interactive RDP/console from non-standard geolocation, failed authentication storms, or lateral admin access from unexpected source systems. Flag interactive command execution (reg.exe, PowerShell, WMI) from admin accounts outside change windows.

suggestion.title: Endpoint Privilege Escalation via Apex One SEP Agent Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article separately mentions 'seven local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Apex One Standard Endpoint Protection (SEP) agent that attackers can exploit if they have permission to execute low-privileged code.' This post-compromise escalation vector received zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoints for exploitation patterns against known vulnerable Apex One SEP components (driver impersonation attacks, token theft, DLL injection targeting agent processes). Alert when low-privileged processes invoke vulnerable agent executables with suspicious parameters or appear in unexpected parent-child process relationships.

suggestion.title: RoleMember user accessing admin-only API endpoint POST /api/v1/cron
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'cron routes `POST /api/v1/cron` and `PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id` are wired through `commonHandler` (any authenticated user) rather than `adminHandler`' — this is the core privilege-escalation vector. Pipeline failed to create a UC focusing on role-based access control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST/PATCH requests to /api/v1/cron where user role field is 1 (RoleMember) or where request source has no explicit admin grant. Correlate against user provisioning to identify newly-promoted or laterally-moved RoleMembers accessing these endpoints for the first time.

suggestion.title: Cron task creation with empty server list and cover-all flag
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RoleMember user can create a scheduled cron task with…' (body truncated) but implies empty servers list + cover=1 flag to execute on all servers across tenants. Pipeline's UC_6_4 captures this but the new UC should focus on the **cross-tenant** aspect and the permission-check bypass logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /api/v1/cron requests with JSON body containing servers=[] (empty array) AND cover=1, especially from RoleMember roles. Correlate with request source IP and authentication session to identify if the same RoleMember is being used against multiple tenant contexts in short time window.

suggestion.title: Permission check bypass: 403→200 transition on protected API endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass' — this suggests authorization logic that returns success when it should fail. Need UC to detect auth-decision anomalies, not just post-RCE actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/v1/cron endpoint responses. Flag patterns where same user/IP receives 403 Forbidden on one request then 200 OK on similar-structure request within seconds, or where permission-check fields in API response switch from deny to allow without corresponding user/role update in upstream identity logs.

suggestion.title: Cross-tenant cron task execution: single request targeting multiple server IDs
suggestion.rationale: Article's title emphasizes 'cross-tenant RCE' — suggests attacker can pivot via single API call to multiple isolated server contexts. Pipeline UCs don't explicitly hunt for multi-server requests from single RoleMember.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /api/v1/cron requests where the request body references or executes against multiple server_ids, especially when cover=1. Flag if the executing user's assigned server list in directory/user-provisioning system does NOT match the targets touched by the cron task.

suggestion.title: Nezha-agent cron execution: parent process is sshd, crond, or systemd (not manual shell)
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker's shell command runs under nezha-agent parent. Key indicator: parent is scheduler (crond) or systemd triggered (not interactive user shell). Pipeline's UC_6_5 catches credential access but doesn't distinguish cron-triggered execution from manual reverse shell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is nezha-agent AND grandparent is crond, cron, systemd, or init, executing shell interpreters or credential-dumping tools. This strongly suggests scheduled cron execution rather than interactive compromise.

suggestion.title: API-triggered execution: shell command spawned within 100ms of HTTP request to /api/v1/cron
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via REST API — pipeline should correlate HTTP request timestamps with process-creation events to show causality. Current UCs are post-hoc but don't prove the API triggered the execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Web proxy/WAF logs (POST /api/v1/cron, HTTP 200) with endpoint process-creation logs. Flag if shell process (sh, bash, python, curl, cat, grep) spawns on the server within 100-500ms of the HTTP request timestamp, and parent process chain includes nezha-agent or cron. Time correlation proves the API call triggered code execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Installation of Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' were compromised and distributed. Organizations must detect when composer install/update retrieves affected versions from Packagist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install, composer update, and direct Packagist API calls for laravel-lang package retrieval. Flag installations of versions within known-compromised ranges (if version info available in threat intel). Correlate with subsequent suspicious PHP execution or network activity.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Takeover - Unexpected Commit Activity to Open Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '700 GitHub Repos' were hacked, implying unauthorized access and commits. Detect anomalous commit patterns to popular open-source repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to high-value repositories (popular open-source projects) from unexpected authors, outside business hours, or from new IP addresses. Flag disabling of branch protection rules, unexpected webhook additions, or collaborator role elevation in repositories.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Unusual Release Velocity
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages likely exhibit abnormal release patterns—multiple versions published in short timeframe or outside normal release cadence ('233 Versions' suggests bulk updates).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist/npm/PyPI release feeds for laravel-lang package. Alert on version releases outside historical maintenance windows, multiple releases within hours, or version bumps inconsistent with commit history. Baseline normal release patterns and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Compromise Preceding Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: 700 repository breach implies initial credential theft or token exfiltration. Detect failed authentication, tokens used from anomalous locations, or PAT creation by dormant accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub authentication anomalies: failed logins preceding successful access, Personal Access Tokens created outside business hours, tokens used from new geolocations, or API calls from residential IPs. Flag bot/automation tokens accessed by human-interactive sessions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Integrity - Package Signature/Hash Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package versions will have altered code but same version number. Detect mismatches between local artifacts and known good package databases or signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA256 hashes of installed laravel-lang files against package database or security vendor IOC feeds. Alert on file integrity mismatches, unexpected code obfuscation in vendor directories, or modifications to package files post-installation.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' — zero detection logic for exploitation attempts against this critical perimeter device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP access logs for HTTP requests with exploitation signatures, abnormal payloads to admin interfaces, or known CVE patterns. Track failed authentication bursts followed by successful access, and monitor for configuration API calls from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: SSH Lateral Movement from Compromised F5
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gain SSH access and pivot into enterprise Linux networks' — no detection for outbound SSH connections originating from F5 appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected outbound SSH from F5 (typically management only); alert on SSH connections from F5 to Linux targets outside administrative scope. Flag rapid SSH attempts to multiple internal systems or SSH activity during unusual hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Linux Process Execution Post-SSH from F5
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful pivot 'into enterprise Linux networks' implying command execution — no detection for suspicious activity following SSH logon from F5-sourced connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound SSH events from F5 source IPs with subsequent suspicious process execution: privilege escalation utilities (sudo/su), reconnaissance tools (whoami, id, uname), credential harvesting, or lateral movement payloads.

suggestion.title: Valid Account Abuse via SSH (Linux)
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'gain SSH access' — could indicate credential theft or account compromise; no detection for anomalous SSH logon using valid service/admin credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH successful logons from F5 IPs using service accounts or admin users that never historically connect from appliances. Detect password spray patterns, rapid-fire authentication attempts, or logons to systems outside expected administrative domains.

suggestion.title: F5 Persistence via Configuration or Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation would require persistence mechanism — no detection use case for F5 configuration tampering, unauthorized user creation, or persistence installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 audit logs for unauthorized configuration changes, SSH key deployment, new administrative user creation, or modifications to network/routing settings. Flag changes outside maintenance windows or attributed to unexpected users.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Pivoted Linux Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Multi-system compromise via Linux pivot typically includes data collection/theft — no detection for suspicious egress traffic or exfiltration from compromised internal systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevated data transfer volumes from Linux targets compromised via F5 pivot. Flag connections to non-business cloud services, P2P networks, external file-share platforms, or known attacker infrastructure from systems with recent SSH activity from F5.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Installation Triggering Credential Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states goal is stealing CI secrets; attack succeeds only if malicious code reads env vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_KEY, etc.) during package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned during composer install/update (php.exe, bash) that read or expand CI secret environment variables. Look for env, printenv, export, or getenv() calls within 10 seconds of composer package fetch operations.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration from PHP/Composer Process to Non-Repository Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stolen secrets; stolen data must transit network from CI runner to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and outbound connections initiated by php or composer processes to domains outside known package repository whitelists (packagist.org, github.com, gitlab.com) during composer install/update in CI/CD runners.

suggestion.title: Multiple Composer Package Repository Tags Modified Without Matching Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'every tag across multiple Composer packages rewritten'—indicates repository-level manipulation outside normal commit workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git tag creation or force-push events in laravel-lang package repositories pointing to commits not in public release branches, or bulk tag operations (>5 tags in 1 hour) without corresponding code review records.

suggestion.title: Composer Lock File Pinning to Unverified or Rapid-Patch Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack affecting all tags suggests victims install compromised versions; composer.lock will show anomalous version pins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan composer.lock files for laravel-lang package family versions that lack corresponding public releases on packagist.org, or versions updated across multiple projects in short time window before public advisory.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Privilege Escalation via RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Run Scripts as Root'—a privilege escalation + code execution scenario. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by LiteSpeed daemon (litespeed, lsphp) or cPanel services with SYSTEM/root privileges, especially script interpreters (bash, perl, python). Monitor for execution from temporary directories or unexpected working directories within cPanel installation paths (/usr/local/cpanel/*, /opt/litespeed/*).

suggestion.title: Malicious HTTP Requests to LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Plugin vulnerabilities require HTTP requests to plugin interfaces; no initial-access detection generated despite 'exploited' in title indicating active campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests (POST/GET) to LiteSpeed or cPanel plugin management endpoints with suspicious parameters (path traversal, code injection, shell metacharacters). Correlate with 5xx responses indicating failed exploitation attempts or 200 responses followed by root process spawning.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Writes to LiteSpeed/cPanel Directories Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE as root enables persistence via file modification; no persistence-phase detection for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file writes to /etc/litespeed/conf/, /usr/local/cpanel/base/addons/, plugin cache directories, and cron/systemd service paths by web server processes or unexpected UIDs. Flag creation of executable files (*.sh, *.pl, *.py) in non-standard locations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply chain attack via Laravel-Lang packages. Pipeline missed the core detection: identifying installation of compromised package versions from composer/npm repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (composer, npm) execution for installation of Laravel-Lang packages with known-malicious versions. Correlate package installation timestamps with credential access attempts or unusual process execution from vendor directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution from Package Manager Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential stealer' payload. Pipeline failed to generate detection for malware execution originating from PHP/composer vendor directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on credential-access techniques (registry queries, browser credential access, API hooking) originating from processes spawned or loaded from vendor/laravel-lang or similar package manager paths. Establish baseline of legitimate vendor directory process execution.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Communication from PHP/Composer Processes
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain credential stealers exfiltrate stolen data. Pipeline missed C2 detection for processes spawned from package manager contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by PHP processes (php.exe, php-cgi) or child processes of composer/package managers. Flag connections to non-standard ports, newly registered domains, or IP geolocation mismatches with development team location.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Laravel Application Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential stealer in packages targeting Laravel. Pipeline missed post-installation code execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious code additions to Laravel config files, bootstrap files, or service providers immediately following package installation. Look for eval(), system(), or file_get_contents patterns pointing to external URLs.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Drupal Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CISA KEV...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Drupal patch level must be detected to identify vulnerable instances before they are exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Drupal instances running versions prior to the patch cutoff for CVE-2026-9082. Query vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) for Drupal Core detections; cross-reference web server logs for Drupal directory access patterns (/admin, /sites) combined with version string identification from HTTP headers or response bodies.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attempt Against Drupal Database API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SQL injection vulnerability...via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' Detection must surface malformed or anomalous database queries originating from Drupal application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal endpoints known to use the database abstraction layer (e.g., `/admin/config/*`, `/admin/structure/*`) for SQL metacharacters or encoded payloads (UNION, SELECT, `--`, `/*`, `*/`). Pair with database query logging to detect anomalous statements (schema enumeration, privilege escalation queries).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Drupal SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states SQL injection 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Post-exploitation, detect elevation of user roles, group membership changes, or administrative account creation within Drupal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal user and role tables for anomalous modifications: creation of new administrative users, elevation of existing users to admin role, or bulk privilege grants. Correlate with preceding SQL injection HTTP requests and unusual database API calls.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack chain culminates in 'remote code execution.' Detect command execution, file uploads, or PHP code eval following successful SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for unexpected process spawning from Drupal application (e.g., PHP-FPM, Apache, Nginx child processes executing shell commands). Flag file uploads to web-accessible directories; monitor for eval() or system() function calls in Drupal logs or PHP error logs.

suggestion.title: LNK shortcut execution from email attachment with PowerShell payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file as an attachment.' Direct initial access vector with named execution—should detect .lnk→PowerShell spawn chain from download/temp directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .lnk file extraction from email attachments (ZIP payload). Detect parent process explorer.exe spawning powershell.exe with command line referencing external URLs or IEX. Cross-reference timing: LNK execution followed by temp file writes.

suggestion.title: PowerShell temporary script execution with registry Run key persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Drops "$temp\fixed.ps1" ... Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup'. Multi-step persistence pattern: staging + auto-exec.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Registry Set operation on HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with masqueraded value name (YandexBrowser, Chrome, etc.) pointing to temp directory .ps1. Alert on PowerShell writing to \temp\fixed.ps1 followed by registry entry creation in same parent process.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH tunnel and Tor proxy chain for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Patched OpenSSH', 'Reverse SSH tunneling', 'RevSocks Tor tunneling'. Named tools and tunnel-based C2 infrastructure—specific to this group's methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH client initialization with -R (reverse) flags or SSH listener on non-standard ports. Detect Tor client spawned by non-browser processes (PowerShell, svchost, services.exe). Alert on ReverseSocks proxy bind/listen operations.

suggestion.title: Browser credential theft via credential grabber component
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber)' and 'Browser checker' tool. Explicit credential access component targeting stored browser secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes (cmd.exe, PowerShell, svchost) accessing browser data directories (%APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, etc.) or reading HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer cookies. Detect LSASS.exe read access from PowerShell context.

suggestion.title: Multi-user RDP enablement via termsrv.dll patching
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll'. Specific DLL modification for concurrent RDP sessions—lateral movement and persistence enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file modification to System32\termsrv.dll (hash change, timestamp anomaly). Alert on termsrv.dll load from non-system directories. Detect RDP service restart or policy changes (AllowMultipleConnections registry key) correlating with termsrv.dll write.

suggestion.title: Decoy document delivery to hide malware staging
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Downloads and drops "$temp\rar.zip"... Extracts "*.pdf" from the downloaded "$temp\rar.zip" [for] distraction phase'. PDF decoys indicate social engineering + distraction during malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell downloading RAR/ZIP archives to temp directory followed by PDF extraction and opening (e.g., AcroRd32.exe spawned). Correlate PDF opening with concurrent malicious script execution (fixed.ps1 running in parallel).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SQL Injection Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specially crafted requests' exploit 'without authentication' to trigger 'arbitrary SQL injection.' Core attack vector that must be detected at ingress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal endpoints containing SQL injection indicators (UNION, OR 1=1, comment sequences, time-delay patterns) sent without valid session/auth tokens. Focus on database abstraction API paths.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Fingerprinting and Patch Status Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: 8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.4.9, 10.5.x–10.5.9, 10.6.x–10.6.8, 11.0.x–11.1.9, 11.2.x–11.2.11, 11.3.x–11.3.9. Unpatched instances are identifiable targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract Drupal version from HTTP headers, admin endpoints, or changelog.txt. Alert on instances within vulnerable version ranges 30+ days post-advisory (May 18, 2026).

suggestion.title: Anomalous SQL Commands from Web Application Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'arbitrary SQL injection' resulting in 'information disclosure' and potential 'remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as unauthorized database commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs for UNION-based injection, information schema enumeration (pg_tables, pg_catalog), or dangerous functions (COPY TO/FROM, lo_export) executed by web application database accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'remote code execution' potential. PostgreSQL can enable shell command execution; successful exploitation would spawn child processes from web-server PIDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from apache/nginx/php-fpm processes following SQL injection attempts, including shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe) or script execution.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Payload Staging in Web-Root Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE capability mentioned in article could enable attacker to write files. Detection should catch malicious file artifacts dropped during exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to web-root directories (DocumentRoot, SCRIPT_FILENAME paths) with suspicious extensions (.php, .phtml, .inc, .sh) created by database or web-server processes immediately following SQL injection log entries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Patch Compliance and Upgrade Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article urges 'upgrade immediately' with specific version thresholds. Post-remediation validation required to verify patches applied and vulnerable instances removed from inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Drupal instances in vulnerable version ranges; validate transition to safe versions (10.4.10+, 10.5.10+, 10.6.9+, 11.1.10+, 11.2.12+, 11.3.10+) within SLA. Flag instances remaining unpatched >45 days post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: VPN C2 Infrastructure Connection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: '25 Ransomware Groups' operated through single dismantled VPN service. Pipeline produced no C2-phase use cases despite explicit infrastructure takedown scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound VPN protocol connections (OpenVPN, WireGuard, proprietary) from corporate endpoints to known takedown infrastructure IPs/domains. Correlate connection timing with ransomware campaign windows. Flag sustained encrypted tunnels from non-user systems.

suggestion.title: Post-Takedown VPN Failover Detection
suggestion.rationale: 25 ransomware groups suddenly lost primary C2 infrastructure—article implies operational continuity hunt. Pipeline did not suggest detection for rapid failover to alternate VPN providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown: detect new VPN client installations on ransomware-staging systems. Monitor for bulk domain/IP resolution switching to new VPN gateway providers (ProtonVPN, Mullvad, custom) within 48-72 hours of takedown announcement.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Infrastructure Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article states 25 distinct groups shared infrastructure—implies behavioral/timing patterns, malware compilation timestamps, or operator timezone signatures during VPN use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound VPN connections by beacon interval, SSL certificate chains, and geographic source-to-endpoint mappings. Group endpoints by timing patterns; flag clusters matching known ransomware-gang operational hours (e.g., RU-TZ operators, business-hours campaigns).

suggestion.title: Law Enforcement Takedown IOC Ingest
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'dismantled' service with implied IP/domain IOCs from law-enforcement action. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite headline indicating specific infrastructure seizure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest VPN gateway IPs, ASNs, domains, and SSL certificates from law-enforcement filings/statements. Retrospectively hunt corporate traffic to those endpoints for credential-stuffing evidence, lateral-movement staging, or data exfil tunnel setup.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration Targeting Major Events
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes fifa26[.]shop as typosquatting: 'common trick known as typosquatting, which involves on a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes.' Pipeline generated no detection for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration for patterns mimicking high-value targets (FIFA, World Cup, etc.) with character substitutions, additions, or TLD variations. Correlate registration timing with major sporting/commercial events. Flag domains within edit distance 1-2 of legitimate brands.

suggestion.title: Landing Page Mimicry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow.' This visual mimicry is explicit but no detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare phishing domain landing page structure, CSS, and asset layout to known legitimate sites. Flag high-similarity matches with low domain reputation or recent registration. Alert on fake branding elements (logos, color schemes) served from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Registration Form Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake registration forms asking for 'name, email address, and phone number' and notes 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange.' No credential-access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST requests to newly registered domains that include credential fields (email, name, phone, address, payment details). Correlate with phishing URLs and alert when registration forms are submitted to suspicious domains matching typosquatted patterns.

suggestion.title: Payment Form Submission to Attacker-Controlled Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article shows fake checkout flows: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site.' No detection for payment data exfiltration or card harvesting was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credit card data (PAN, CVV patterns) or PII submitted via HTTP POST to domains with low reputation, recent registration, or matching phishing/typosquatting signatures. Alert on payment form submissions that bypass official payment gateways.

suggestion.title: Search Engine and Social Media Ad Abuse for Phishing Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media.' No detection for ad-based initial access was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sponsored search results and social media ad networks for ads linking to typosquatted or newly registered domains. Correlate ad content with legitimate brand names (FIFA, World Cup). Alert on high click volumes to phishing URLs originating from ad networks.

suggestion.title: Event-Driven Phishing Campaign Timing Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes scammers 'know exactly how to exploit this demand' and 'Posing as the FIFA association or the official World Cup website, the imposter sites target people' during high-demand period. No detection for event-triggered phishing clusters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate spikes in typosquatted domain registrations and phishing submissions with upcoming major events (World Cup, Olympics, Black Friday, etc.). Flag clusters of similar-pattern domains registered within 30 days of high-visibility events, especially around ticketing/merchandise keywords.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'began with an exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance' — no detection UC for initial F5 exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP management interfaces (8443, 443) for exploit signatures, failed authentication chains, or suspicious REST API calls. Correlate with known CVEs in BIG-IP versions (CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21911 class). Alert on successful authentication from non-standard source IPs followed by icontrol or tmsh command sequences.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'threat actor attempted Kerberos relay' — no UC detecting relay techniques against Linux or Windows targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kerberos relay by correlating TGT/TGS requests with immediate lateral movement attempts. Alert on TGS-REQ with non-standard delegation flags, Kerberos traffic crossing security boundaries without corresponding user login events, or NTLM relay indicators (Type 3 messages after unexpected Type 1).

suggestion.title: Confluence Server Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'pivoted to an internal Confluence server for credential theft' — no UC for detecting post-exploitation Confluence activity or credential exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence process (Java) for suspicious child processes (sh, bash, curl), credential storage access patterns (reading /etc/shadow, /home/*/.ssh, Confluence home directory). Alert on Confluence process spawning system utilities or making unexpected outbound connections, especially to non-standard C2 ports.

suggestion.title: Linux Multi-Stage Implant Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage Linux intrusion' — no UC for detecting payload staging, shellcode execution, or persistence mechanisms on Linux edge/internal devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux process execution for: (1) suspicious parent-child chains (web server → shell), (2) base64/hex decode operations followed by execution, (3) /dev/tcp connections or curl/wget with pipe-to-shell patterns, (4) process injection or library loading from /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Edge to Internal Confluence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pivot 'from edge appliance to enterprise compromise' and 'internal Confluence server' — no UC for detecting lateral movement post-edge-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from F5/edge appliance to internal Confluence server (typical ports 8080, 8443, 443) with payloads. Correlate with successful Confluence authentication or exploitation attempt signatures. Alert on edge device making internal network scan or port-scan behavior.

suggestion.title: Identity Compromise via Credential Theft Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'credential theft and identity compromise' — no UC detecting credential access pipeline from Confluence database or memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence user database access (confluence.cfg.xml, database files), authentication token extraction (session files, login attempts with harvested credentials), and subsequent use of stolen credentials across domain. Alert on Confluence process reading its own credential stores or config files, followed by successful logins from unexpected IPs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Prometheus Malware Attachment to Government Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware'—phishing is the explicit delivery mechanism; no use case captured this initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateway logs for messages targeting .ua government domains with attachment MIME types (exe, dll, zip, docm) or suspicious URLs. Correlate sender domains with known phishing infrastructure. Alert on low email volume to high-value government accounts with external attachment headers.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution via User Action
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Prometheus Phishing Malware'—execution phase is implicit in phishing+malware pattern but not mapped to detections or kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with parent=explorer.exe, winword.exe, or outlook.exe spawning suspicious child processes (powershell, cmd, rundll32) with low-reputation file hashes or living-off-the-land binary usage. Correlate with recent attachment opens within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Phishing+malware campaigns require C2; article does not specify C2 IOCs or detection rules for post-exploitation network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from infected endpoint to non-whitelisted IPs/domains. Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains or those with Russian IP geolocation from government networks. Detect anomalous port usage (non-standard HTTP/HTTPS) for C2 beacon callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Government entity compromises typically involve credential theft and lateral movement; article genre suggests multi-stage attack but pipeline captured no lateral movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed RDP/SMB connections from compromised workstations to multiple internal targets within 15 minutes, especially to high-value targets (domain controllers, file servers). Detect pass-the-hash attempts (credential reuse without login) and unusual service account activity.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500 / SQL Errors from YesWiki Bazar Form Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement.' Blind SQLi typically generates error responses during enumeration. Current UCs detect request volume but not response errors that signal active probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 500 errors or SQL error keywords ('MySQL', 'SQL syntax', 'database error', 'constraint violation') in responses from /BazaR?vue=formulaire endpoints within a 5-minute window. Combine with source IP and escalate if repeated across multiple requests.

suggestion.title: Oversized POST Parameters to YesWiki Form-Import
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injection into INSERT statement via form-import path. SQLi payloads are verbose; detect unusually large request bodies or parameter values that exceed baseline for form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to BazaR endpoints where body size exceeds 8KB or individual parameter values contain SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR, INSERT) or quote-escape sequences. Correlate with non-browser user-agent for higher fidelity.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of yeswiki_users or Database Schema via SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Post-injection, attackers enumerate schema via INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries or table SELECTs. HTTP-layer detections miss this critical phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If database query logging is enabled, hunt for SELECT queries against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES or INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS followed immediately by SELECT * FROM yeswiki_users or SELECT password FROM yeswiki_users. Multiple failed queries (blind SQLi) followed by successful credential retrieval is the expected pattern.

suggestion.title: Bulk Extraction of Password Hashes from YesWiki Users Table
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'read...yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Attackers will extract all hashes post-exploitation. Database audit logs should show anomalous table scans or full table selects not matching application query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential or repeated SELECT statements on yeswiki_users.password column from single source IP/session context within short timeframe (seconds to minutes). Compare against baseline application queries; legitimate reads should be infrequent and user-scoped.

suggestion.title: Account Creation or Privilege Escalation via SQLi INSERT/UPDATE
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated SQLi into INSERT statement permits account creation or privilege escalation for persistence. Article does not mention observed privilege escalation, but is a logical follow-on to database write access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for INSERT or UPDATE statements against yeswiki_users with admin=1 or privilege flags, especially those originating from Bazar form-import request context or lacking corresponding user-creation events in application logs.

suggestion.title: Successful FileBrowser Quantum path traversal exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory' but no hunt detects successful execution via HTTP 200/success response codes to PATCH with traversal payloads. UC_15_1 detects the request form only, not outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP 200/204 responses to PATCH `/public/api/resources` containing `fromPath` or `toPath` with `..` segments. Correlate with subsequent file system operations (move/delete/write) on files outside the documented share directory to confirm traversal success.

suggestion.title: File system operations on paths outside FileBrowser share directory post-PATCH
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables file operations 'outside shared directory' but no hunt looks for the actual file-level impact (move, rename, delete on out-of-bounds paths). Current hunts stop at the HTTP layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` with `..` payloads against file system logs showing the FileBrowser process (typically unprivileged) creating, modifying, or deleting files whose paths fall outside the documented `share.Path` root directory.

suggestion.title: ISP/Telecom Infrastructure Compromise via SSH, RDP, or Trusted Relationship Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hackers Abuse Middle East Telecom Networks.' This describes initial compromise of ISP edge infrastructure—the foundation of the attack. T1199 (Trusted Relationship) or T1133 (External Remote Services) or T1021.004 (SSH) are the primary paths to ISP access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed/successful authentication attempts to telecom AS boundary routers, VPN concentrators, or BGP route reflectors from external IPs. Track privilege escalation on infrastructure devices immediately post-authentication. Correlate geolocation of login source with known threat regions.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale C2 Traffic Tunneled Through Compromised Telecom Backbone
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly claims 'large-scale Command-and-Control Operations' via telecom networks. Pipeline produced zero detection for C2 traffic exfiltration through ISP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag persistent outbound connections from ISP infrastructure to known or suspected C2 domains/IPs. Detect DNS queries for DGA-like domains or suspicious TLDs originating from telecom backbone. Correlate command-like HTTP user-agents or binary payloads in traffic flows.

suggestion.title: BGP Route Hijacking or Anomalous ASN Announcements from Telecom Provider
suggestion.rationale: Telecom infrastructure compromise frequently manifests as BGP anomalies, route hijacks, or unexpected path prepending. This is a direct indicator of infrastructure-level compromise but pipeline produced no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BGP updates from Middle East telecom ASNs for unexpected route announcements, path length anomalies, AS-path prepending, or RPKI validation failures. Cross-reference with downstream BGP community tags and validate against known legitimate ISP operations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from ISP Infrastructure to Downstream Customer Networks
suggestion.rationale: Title's phrase 'large-scale' implies victims beyond the ISP itself. Telecom compromise is a pivot point to customer networks, yet pipeline generated zero lateral-movement detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify traffic originating from ISP backbone infrastructure (peering points, route reflectors) to customer networks outside normal BGP paths. Alert on infrastructure-to-customer SSH/RDP/WinRM connections with binary payloads or suspicious process spawning.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known-Compromised NPM Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'art-template npm Package' was backdoored. Pipeline must detect when a flagged compromised version is installed. No behavioral or signature detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package installation events (npm install, yarn install, npm update) against maintained CVE/advisory list of known-compromised packages. Alert on installation of art-template versions matching published compromise range. Include lockfile modifications and dependency resolution logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks via npm packages execute payload via malicious scripts field in package.json during install. Phrase 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' implies active execution; pipeline generated no detection for this critical execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as direct child of npm.exe or node.exe during install/update operations. Flag processes with obfuscated arguments, Base64 encoding flags, registry modifications, or suspicious network utility invocations (curl, wget). Baseline and exclude known legitimate post-install scripts from popular packages.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network Connections from Node.js Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks require C2 callback for attack delivery. Article implies command-and-control phase ('launch attacks'). Pipeline missed network-based detection for backdoor communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP connections from node.js processes to destinations outside curated whitelist of npm CDN/registry IPs and known-benign package dependencies. Correlate timing with recent npm install/update. Detect DNS requests from node processes to suspicious or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized NPM Package Version Release or Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: To distribute backdoor, attacker compromised package publish capability. Pipeline missed initial-access detection at registry level—should detect abnormal package release activity, new versions from unexpected accounts, or rapid version churn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry publish API and audit logs for art-template: flag unexpected new versions, releases from non-canonical maintainer accounts, version metadata modifications (new scripts, dependencies added), or multi-version releases within short windows. Establish baseline of legitimate release cadence and maintainer accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Version Yanking or Emergency Package Unpublishing
suggestion.rationale: When compromised package discovered, maintainers typically unpublish or emergency-patch. Pipeline should detect incident-response pattern indicating active exploitation discovery. Phrase 'Hackers Backdoor' implies recent event with remediation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unpublish or rapid version removal of popular packages (>1M weekly downloads). Correlate against CVE/CERT advisories published within 24h of unpublish event. Alert on emergency patch releases (patch bump surge) following security disclosure. Flag to threat-intel team for investigation into active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Pollution via Transitive Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package may be installed indirectly as dependency of legitimate packages. Pipeline must account for transitive compromise—developers using packages that depend on art-template become victims without direct install awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock for transitive dependencies matching known-compromised packages. Alert on any package (direct or transitive) pinning a compromised version, even if parent package appears benign. Monitor dependency resolution for unexpected nested installs of flagged packages.

suggestion.title: NF-e Invoice Lure — Malicious Batch File Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious batch file named Consultar_NF-e.bat distributed via WhatsApp or phishing links'—foundational initial-access detection completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .bat files with names mimicking Brazilian document types or financial institutions, especially Consultar_* or Nota_* patterns. Alert on batch files received via email, messaging, or downloaded from non-corporate file-sharing; correlation with financial-sector targeting strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution Hidden Within Batch File
suggestion.rationale: Article states batch file 'triggers concealed PowerShell command'—direct code execution evasion pattern critical to this attack and a high-signal detection absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell (powershell.exe or pwsh.exe) spawned directly or indirectly from batch files (.bat, .cmd). Flag encoded, obfuscated, or dynamically reconstructed command lines. Monitor for parent-process chains: cmd.exe → powershell.exe with suspicious argument patterns.

suggestion.title: AES-256 Encrypted Payload Staging via msedge.txt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'downloads encrypted payload (msedge.txt) via AES-256 encryption'—staged encrypted downloads are high-fidelity C2 indicator missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of files with deceptive names (msedge.txt, st.txt, st.php, payload.php) from suspicious domains or IP:port combinations. Flag retrieval immediately after batch/PowerShell execution. Inspect file entropy for encrypted content.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence — Minute-Interval PowerShell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'hidden scheduled task launching PowerShell every minute for up to 9,999 days'—persistence mechanism central to attack operationalization, not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scheduled task creation with execution intervals ≤5 minutes. Flag tasks invoking powershell.exe with hidden attributes or unusual repeat counts (>1000). Correlate with batch-file or unusual PowerShell spawning in same session.

suggestion.title: Banking Overlay Injection — Fake Security Prompt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'injects fake banking overlays mimicking security updates'—fraud-enabling collection mechanism that should trigger impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected window/UI injection into banking applications (Itau, Bradesco, Santander, Caixa, Banco do Brasil clients). Flag screen-capture API calls immediately before network activity to banking domains. Alert on unexpected pop-up overlays or prompts in banking session context.

suggestion.title: QR Code Replacement During Financial Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'intercepts/replaces Pix QR codes during transactions'—transaction fraud indicator tied to Brazilian payment systems, critical to impact assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate screen-capture events (T1113) with clipboard or file-system writes containing QR code data during active banking sessions. Alert on clipboard modifications following image-processing or screen-capture API calls. Flag session where Pix transaction QR differs from server-provided QR.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized User Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes six-layer persistence; user account creation is a standard persistence vector. No detection UC was generated despite 'maintain access' implying account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX admin user database or system audit logs for creation of new local accounts outside maintenance windows. Watch for accounts created with default or weak credentials. Cross-reference with changes to FreePBX permission assignments.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Configuration File Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence implies modification of configuration files as a persistence mechanism. Article emphasizes 'maintain access' but pipeline generated no config tampering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/asterisk config files, FreePBX database backend configs, and extension configuration XML. Alert on edits outside change windows. Correlate with unusual process or user access to FreePBX directories.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Scheduled Task Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence architecture described in title should include scheduled task abuse. No UC for cron or at-job persistence on FreePBX was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cron tables (/var/spool/cron/crontabs/) and at daemon for new entries added by unprivileged or service accounts. Alert on cron jobs executing from /tmp or world-writable directories, or invoking shell interpreters with obfuscated parameters.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Web Shell Implantation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence on a web-facing PBX system highly likely includes web shell placement. Article title implies sustained access mechanism not captured by any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX web directories (/var/www/html/admin, /var/www/html/configs) for creation of new PHP, Python, or shell script files. Cross-reference with HTTP access logs for unusual POST requests or parameter patterns. Alert on executable permissions added to non-standard files.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Privilege Escalation via Service Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining persistent access on a system-level service (Asterisk/FreePBX) likely requires privilege escalation or service-level backdoors. No privilege escalation or service manipulation UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Asterisk/FreePBX service startup scripts and systemd unit files for unauthorized modifications. Alert on processes spawned by the asterisk service user running commands outside expected binaries. Detect sudoers file modifications allowing unprivileged users to restart/reload services.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Module Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: PBX systems support custom modules/extensions for functionality extension. 'Six-layer persistence' likely includes persistent module installation not addressed by any generated UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the FreePBX modules directory and AMI (Asterisk Manager Interface) module logs for installation of unsigned or unknown modules. Alert on modules loading from non-standard paths or created by non-root users. Cross-reference module names against known legitimate FreePBX extensions.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet C2 Outbound Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'DDoS Botnet Operator' implying operational C2 infrastructure; botnet coordination requires command channels. No UC captures abnormal outbound traffic patterns, beaconing, or C2 protocol indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained outbound connections from non-server endpoints to rare/newly-seen IP:port combinations at regular intervals; correlate with malware hash, known botnet C2 domains, or DGA-derived domains. Detect anomalous DNS queries to infrastructure domains associated with Kimwolf operators.

suggestion.title: Volumetric DDoS Attack Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'DDoS-for-hire attacks' and botnet operator role; DDoS attacks are the primary impact vector but pipeline contains no detection for volumetric/UDP flood/SYN flood patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden surge in outbound traffic from single or clustered infected hosts to external targets (volumetric flood signature); monitor for anomalous packet rates, UDP floods, or SYN floods originating from compromised systems. Threshold alert on outbound bandwidth > 500 Mbps or packet rate > 1M pps to non-whitelisted destinations.

suggestion.title: Botnet Recruitment / Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies subject as 'DDoS Botnet Operator' — implies active botnet spreading, vulnerability exploitation, or malware distribution. No UC addresses how systems become compromised or added to botnet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts against known vulnerabilities correlated with botnet families; flag failed/successful attempts to execute payloads from suspicious URLs. Monitor for indicators of botnet payload execution (process creation from temp directories, registry modifications, scheduled tasks for persistence).

suggestion.title: DDoS-as-a-Service Command Panel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'DDoS-for-hire' service model — implies web/remote access infrastructure (admin panel, payment portal, attack control panel). No UC covers detection of panel logins or control-plane activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) connections to known DDoS panel infrastructure (known IP:port, domains), unusual login patterns from distributed IPs, or payment processing activity correlated with botnet C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Kernel Driver Loading
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits vulnerable drivers to gain kernel access without requiring custom exploitation code. Article discusses 'making vulnerable drivers exploitable'—pipeline must detect driver loading events from user-mode processes attempting kernel access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned, low-reputation, or known-vulnerable drivers being loaded into memory. Alert on processes in %WINDIR%\Temp or user writable paths loading .sys files, or registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\* adding driver image paths pointing outside System32 or trusted driver folders.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Driver Installation via SC or Registry
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires installing a vulnerable driver; attack 'does not require hardware' suggests local installation mechanism via service control or direct registry modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of 'sc.exe create', 'sc.exe start', or direct HKLM registry writes to Services keys, especially when source process is user-mode or from temp directories. Cross-correlate driver image path with vulnerable driver signatures (CVE-linked driver versions).

suggestion.title: Process Attempting Kernel Communication via Vulnerable Driver Device Path
suggestion.rationale: Once a vulnerable driver is loaded, exploitation requires user-mode process to communicate with kernel via device interface (e.g., \Device\, \Global??, CreateFile on driver device).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes opening handles to driver device objects or calling device I/O control (DeviceIoControl). Alert on non-system processes repeatedly querying or writing to \Device\* or \Global?? paths, especially from LOLBin or command-line contexts.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Code Execution Following Driver Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article frames BYOVD as enabling privilege escalation 'without hardware'; the payload execution step must be detected as kernel code execution or process elevation immediately following driver load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver installation events with subsequent process token elevation, privilege level changes, or access to SYSTEM-owned resources. Alert if a user-mode child process gains SYSTEM privileges within 5 seconds of a driver load event in the parent process chain.

suggestion.title: Driver Persistence via Boot Registry or Service Autostart
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits are typically leveraged for persistent access; detection must cover driver registration for autostart to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services for new entries with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) and Start=0x2 (auto-start). Alert on registry modifications that add driver entries with unsigned, low-reputation, or test-signed image paths.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'targets 5,561 repos with malicious CI/CD workflows'—direct evidence that the primary attack vector is injected/compromised workflow files in .github/workflows/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files with suspicious payloads: base64-encoded commands, exfiltration of secrets via curl/wget, environment variable logging, or inline script execution from untrusted sources. Correlate with commits from accounts not in CODEOWNERS or from unusual IP/geo.

suggestion.title: Repository Compromise via Account Takeover or Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attacker achieved write access to 5,561 repos to inject workflows—requires either account compromise or stolen OAuth tokens. Article implies scale suggests credential compromise as initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits and workflow modifications from anomalous geographic locations, new IP ranges, or at off-hours compared to account baseline. Flag sudden bulk repository access pattern changes or OAuth scope elevation requests requesting 'repo' and 'workflow' permissions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Automated Package Publishing Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: With 5,561 repos compromised (likely open-source), attackers can auto-publish malicious package versions via CI/CD, directly impacting downstream consumers.
log_sources: Package registry logs (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate workflow file modifications with new package releases within 1-24 hours. Alert on version bumps published immediately after .github/workflows/ changes or from CI/CD systems with new/unusual OAuth tokens.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via CI/CD Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD workflows execute with access to repository secrets (API keys, credentials). Malicious workflows can log or exfiltrate ${{ secrets.* }} to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflow steps that reference secrets.* in subprocess calls, logging statements, or network requests (curl, wget, nc). Detect unusual artifact uploads or environment variable writes to external storage systems.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Cross-Repository Access via Compromised Tokens
suggestion.rationale: An attacker controlling workflow execution gains the token's permissions—can access organization's private repos, deploy keys, and GitHub Apps with escalated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD runners for git operations accessing organization repositories outside the current project scope. Flag runs cloning private repos with no historical access baseline from that workflow/actor.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Modification in Public Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation across 5,500+ public repositories via workflow abuse—core attack vector that should generate detection for .github/workflows/ changes in public repos, especially pull requests adding exfiltration steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow file changes (.github/workflows/*.yml) in public repositories for additions of credential export commands, HTTP POST to external URLs, or environment variable dumps. Flag pull requests modifying workflows from low-reputation accounts.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Access in GitHub Actions Environment
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon exfiltrates secrets—should detect when Actions workflows enumerate or access multiple secrets/environment variables in single run, or when secrets are dumped to logs or sent externally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Actions jobs that access >5 secrets in a single workflow, export env vars to stdout, or use `env` command without legitimate build context. Correlate with outbound network connections from runner IPs.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via GitHub Actions Runner Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions exfiltration across repositories—should detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runner IPs to attacker infrastructure, especially POST/PUT with credential-like payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from GitHub Actions runner IP ranges to non-GitHub/non-package-manager external hosts. Flag POST requests containing patterns matching GitHub secrets, API tokens, or PATs. Baseline against legitimate dependencies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Pull Request Adding GitHub Actions Workflows to Public Repos
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon uses compromised workflows—should detect PRs that introduce or modify .github/workflows files with commands that access credentials or initiate external connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pull requests that add/modify workflow files containing: 'secrets.*', 'env.*' dumping, curl/wget to external IPs, base64-encoded commands, or multi-stage exfiltration logic. Prioritize PRs from newly created or low-activity accounts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository Secret Enumeration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repos affected implies systematic enumeration—should detect when single actor/account/IP triggers secret access across multiple public repositories in short time window.
