suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is code.exe or command line references paths within extension directories. Flag PowerShell, cmd.exe, or native binary execution with working directory in .vscode\extensions.

suggestion.title: Extension-Based Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Payload achieves persistence by modifying HKCU registry for launch arguments, shell integration, or autostart hooks tied to VS Code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSCode (extension settings), HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with code.exe references, and shell context menu modifications. Correlate with extension installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Network Communication Initiated by VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload within extension initiates C2 or data exfiltration; outbound connections from code.exe to non-Microsoft infrastructure is strong compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DeviceNetworkEvents where InitiatingProcessName=code.exe and RemoteIP/RemoteUrl are not whitelisted Microsoft, GitHub, or npm domains. Baseline legitimate VS Code update and extension traffic; alert on anomalies post-compromise window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from .git, .ssh, .env via Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: VS Code typically has file access to developer credentials (SSH keys, .git config, API tokens, .env); compromised extension can read and exfiltrate these.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access (QueryName/CreateKey) from VS Code or spawned child processes to %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, .git/config, and %APPDATA%\Local\Temp\*.env files. Correlate reads with suspicious network egress or process spawning.

suggestion.title: Fileless or Staged Payload Dropped to Temp/Startup by Extension
suggestion.rationale: Extension drops second-stage executable to staging directories for persistence or lateral movement; files written from extension path to %TEMP% or Startup folders indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FileCreated events in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup with VS Code or extension process context. Hash new files and check against threat feed. Alert on double extensions or obfuscated names.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Microsoft Graph API Enumeration via Service Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article core subject: 'Open-source framework ROADtools is being misused by threat actors for cloud intrusions'—ROADtools specializes in Graph API reconnaissance (users, groups, applications, service principals). Zero UCs detect suspicious Graph API bulk enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity Microsoft Graph API GET requests for bulk user/group/service-principal enumeration, directoryObjects, or application queries from atypical service principals or IP ranges. Focus on filter patterns and request clustering consistent with automated reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Service Principal Credential Issuance and Usage
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state actors (Curious Serpens, Midnight Blizzard) abuse service principal credentials for persistence and lateral movement in cloud tenants. Article describes 'cloud intrusions' via Entra ID. No UC for anomalous service principal sign-ins or token requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service principal sign-ins from unexpected geographies or IPs, client-credential flows from interactive contexts, and newly created or modified service principal credentials outside change windows. Flag token requests to high-value resources (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams).

suggestion.title: Device Code Flow Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools signature attack: device code OAuth flow to bypass MFA and gain persistent cloud access. Article addresses 'nation-state tactics in the cloud.' No UC for unattended device code authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code flow requests (/devicecode endpoint) completed without human interaction, followed by sign-ins from ROPC clients or non-interactive applications. Flag when device code flows occur outside corporate IP ranges or from compromised devices.

suggestion.title: Bulk Azure Resource Enumeration and Policy Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools enumerates subscriptions, storage accounts, key vaults, and conditional access policies; actors modify policies to bypass controls. Article mentions 'cloud intrusions.' No UC for bulk resource discovery or policy tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential Azure resource API calls (list subscriptions, storage accounts, VMs, key vaults) from a single principal. Monitor for unusual modifications to conditional access policies, MFA settings, or authentication methods via API.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Consent and High-Risk Permission Grants
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools attackers grant Directory.ReadAll, Mail.Read, and other high-risk permissions to malicious applications. Article addresses Entra ID attacks. No UC for anomalous consent or permission escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag applications being granted Directory.ReadAll, Mail.ReadWrite, or AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All permissions by non-admins or from unusual contexts. Monitor consent from users outside developer groups or consent flows initiated by service principals.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Lateral Movement via Cloud Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes nation-state actors moving laterally between tenants and on-premises AD. No UC for detecting cross-tenant token abuse or tenant-hopping behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication tokens or credentials from one tenant being used to access resources in a different tenant. Flag principals without prior history in a tenant suddenly accessing resources there. Correlate on-premises AD auth with Azure access in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Execution of Exploit Payloads Against Project Glasswing
suggestion.rationale: Headline states '10,000+ 0-Days in Project Glasswing'—successful exploitation would manifest as anomalous process execution, privilege escalation, or unexpected system behavior on affected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation telemetry for unusual child processes, unexpected privilege escalation, or system call anomalies on systems running Glasswing components. Alert on suspicious binary execution or shellcode indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access and Credential Abuse Against Claude Mythos Preview
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Claude Mythos Preview' as the discovery source. Service compromise would be detected via unauthorized authentication, anomalous API activity, or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag anomalous API token usage, service account credential abuse, and unusual authentication patterns targeting Anthropic/Claude infrastructure. Monitor for debug-build artifact access or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Vulnerability Scanning of Glasswing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Discovery of '10,000+ 0-Days' implies prior scanning, enumeration, and vulnerability research activities that precede exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-scale scanning behavior: port enumeration sweeps targeting Glasswing infrastructure, suspicious DNS queries for Glasswing or Anthropic domains, rapid probing across multiple assets within a short timeframe.

suggestion.title: RoleMember authentication to Nezha /api/v1/cron endpoint followed by privilege-escalated cron execution
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability explicitly states 'cron routes POST /api/v1/cron and PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id are wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler, and the per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' This is the initial-access and privilege-escalation step the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST requests to /api/v1/cron or PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id from accounts with RoleMember status, followed by successful responses. Correlate with absence of an AdminApproval or CanExecuteOnServer permission check failure. Look for requests with 'servers' payload set to empty array or overly broad server selector.

suggestion.title: Cross-tenant cron task creation via vacuous-true authorization bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states the 'per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' This is the persistence mechanism—RoleMember creates a task on servers they should not have access to.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron tasks created via Nezha API with cross-tenant implications. Look for task creation events where the user account lacks direct server-level permissions but the request succeeds anyway. Correlate POST /api/v1/cron requests with subsequent cron execution logs showing commands running in unexpected security contexts.

suggestion.title: Nezha API missing authentication or role-boundary enforcement on administrative endpoints
suggestion.rationale: The core vulnerability is 'RoleMember (Role==1) can run shell on every server' via endpoints meant for RoleAdmin only. No hunt was generated for the root-cause: missing or misconfigured authz on commonHandler-wired routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline successful authentication + authorization to Nezha /api/v1/cron by role. Alert when Role=1 (RoleMember) accounts successfully invoke operations that should require Role=0 (RoleAdmin). Track HTTP 200/201 responses on admin-tier API calls from non-admin authenticated users.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized server enumeration or sideways movement via Nezha agent on multiple hosts
suggestion.rationale: A RoleMember exploiting this can 'run shell on every server.' The discovery phase (T1057, process enumeration implied) suggests attackers will use compromised agents to pivot. No hunt targets lateral movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a single compromised Nezha agent spawns process discovery commands (ps, netstat, ifconfig) in rapid succession across multiple monitored servers, or when the Nezha agent's parent shell opens new SSH/RDP connections to other hosts in the same tenant or across tenants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Version Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article states '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' were compromised. Pipeline should detect abnormal release velocity and version bumping patterns. Phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (Packagist) for Laravel-Lang releases with abnormal frequency, unusual commit metadata, or mismatched code signatures. Flag installations of versions falling within the 233 compromised versions to detect lateral spread.

suggestion.title: Mass GitHub Repository Activity After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates '700 GitHub Repos' were hacked to inject malicious code. Should detect credential compromise via abnormal repo activity. Phrase: 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with logins from unusual geographies/IPs immediately followed by mass commit or branch activity, especially to package-distribution repos. Look for repos normally inactive becoming suddenly active or code pushed outside normal development windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution via Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Developers installing compromised Laravel-Lang packages will execute embedded malicious code. No UC generated for post-install execution. Phrase: 'Compromised...Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning or network connections immediately following `composer install` or `php artisan` commands that resolve to Laravel-Lang dependencies. Track unexpected child processes from PHP interpreters, especially curl, wget, or shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Package Hash / Signature Mismatch on Installed Modules
suggestion.rationale: Compromised versions will have altered hashes or missing signatures. No UC for validating package integrity. Phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed Laravel-Lang package hashes against Packagist official metadata. Alert on hash mismatches, missing signatures, or version-to-hash pairings not in the official repository. Cross-reference against Composer lock files.

suggestion.title: Unusual Access to Compromised Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Spike in downloads or unusual geographic distribution of compromised versions should trigger alerts. Not captured by pipeline. Phrase: '700 GitHub Repos' suggests scale and intentionality requiring distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist API and CDN logs for abnormal download patterns on Laravel-Lang within the 233 compromised versions. Baseline against historical trends. Alert on geographic distribution outside developer concentrations.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP CVE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' but pipeline extracted zero indicators. F5 BIG-IP RCE/auth-bypass CVEs (CVE-2024-46985 or similar) are high-confidence indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP web server logs for malformed HTTP requests, path traversal patterns, or known CVE-specific payloads targeting authentication endpoints. Flag requests with unusual Content-Length, chunked encoding, or header manipulation attempts.

suggestion.title: SSH Session Initiation from BIG-IP to Internal Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—SSH from the compromised BIG-IP to internal systems is the pivot vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SSH connections (port 22) originating from F5 BIG-IP management or data-plane IPs to internal Linux hosts. Correlate with baseline SSH connections to identify anomalous targets or authentication methods.

suggestion.title: Process Execution on F5 BIG-IP Following Network Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE on BIG-IP requires command execution; pipeline missed detection of shell spawning or system utility invocation post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP for spawning of bash, sh, perl, or python processes from web server workers (httpd, nginx equivalents on F5). Alert on non-standard child processes or privilege-escalation attempts from web-server context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-BIG-IP Compromise via Credential Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pivoting to 'enterprise Linux networks'—attacker likely harvests credentials from BIG-IP (admin creds, SSH keys, cached credentials) for internal access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed SSH login attempts against multiple internal hosts with source IPs previously associated with BIG-IP management range. Alert on use of extracted credentials (regex patterns from config files or memory dumps).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Compromised BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may beacon to C2 or download tools. Pipeline missing detection for anomalous egress patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from BIG-IP to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially on unconventional ports (8080, 443 variant, DNS tunneling). Correlate with time-of-day anomalies and data volume.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation from Malicious Git Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'attacker exploited a GitHub feature that allows version tags to point to commits from a fork of the same repository' and 'malicious version tags appeared across multiple repositories'. No detection for supply-chain compromise via crafted version tags.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.lock and composer.json for unexpected version pins to Laravel-Lang packages; correlate package installation timestamps with 233 affected versions (May 2026 window). Alert on Composer downloading from non-canonical upstream or tag-based checkouts diverging from release history.

suggestion.title: PHP Helpers File Execution with Host Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'core malicious functionality is located in a file named src/helpers.php that's designed to fingerprint the infected host'. Pipeline missed execution phase and reconnaissance behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PHP process execution from vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php; monitor for system information gathering (uname, whoami, env var enumeration) immediately following Composer install; correlate with subsequent outbound connections to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Credentials from .env and Config Files with Recursive Directory Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer collects all .env files and config files found by recursively scanning the working directory'. No detection for mass .env file access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect recursive file enumeration patterns matching */.*env, *config.php, *database.yml across entire working directory trees by PHP processes. Alert on simultaneous read access to .env + src/helpers.php + unexpected network I/O within 5-second window.

suggestion.title: Browser Password and Crypto Wallet Extension Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'saved passwords from 17 Chromium-based browsers' and 'browser extension wallets by extension ID including MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet'. No detection for wallet/extension discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access patterns to /Users/*/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data, and ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/. Alert on access to browser extension manifests or localStorage for MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet IDs.

suggestion.title: AES-256 Encrypted Exfiltration to flipboxstudio.info C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware encrypts the payload using AES-256 and exfiltrates it to the attacker's infrastructure'. IOC domain flipboxstudio.info was not extracted; no detection for encryption + exfil pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or connections to flipboxstudio.info and whois-derived IP ranges. Flag processes performing AES encryption operations (detected via OpenSSL library calls or memory patterns) followed immediately by outbound network I/O. Baseline: PHP processes should not perform encryption + exfil in production environments.

suggestion.title: Self-Deleting PHP Process After Exfiltration Completion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deleting itself to evade forensic detection'. No defense-evasion detection for post-exfil cleanup behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file deletion of src/helpers.php or inline PHP script paths immediately following network exfiltration events to flipboxstudio.info. Correlate process termination with deletion timestamp; flag same-process file creation + exfil + self-delete sequences within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Autoload Files Addition
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The payload was hidden in a newly added file, src/helpers.php, and registered in composer.json under autoload.files.' This is the execution mechanism; Composer's autoloader unconditionally requires all files in autoload.files, making it a clear detection point for package tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications in vendor directories or Laravel-Lang packages for unexpected entries in the 'autoload.files' section, especially targeting src/helpers.php. Flag when autoload.files is populated by commits from external forks rather than official package repositories.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication to flipboxstudio.info
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it in the background' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' Direct C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any HTTP/HTTPS traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info or subdomains, especially requests to /payload and /exfil endpoints. Correlate with process trees originating from PHP execution contexts or Composer processes. Cross-reference with developer workstations and CI/CD environments.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Credential Storage Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'The second stage is a credential and secrets stealer. Once it lands, it walks through a long list of sources looking for anything of value: Cloud provider credentials, Kubernetes kubeconfig files, Vault tokens, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, .env files, browser data, password manager vaults, cryptocurrency wallets.' Pattern indicates systematic credential discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from PHP contexts that enumerate or read from credential storage paths: ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.ssh, ~/.vault, .env, ~/.browser, ~/.gnupg, ~/.ethereum, etc. Particularly sensitive: processes reading multiple credential sources in rapid succession from non-standard contexts (build systems, web servers).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Artifact Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery.' Defensive evasion pattern following exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid file deletion events with preceding outbound C2 traffic or credential enumeration activity. Flag deletion of recently modified files in temporary directories or application-writable locations immediately following exfiltration timeframes.

suggestion.title: Git Tag Resolution to External Fork
suggestion.rationale: Article explains the initial attack vector: 'The attacker did not push any commits to the official laravel-lang source repositories. Instead, they leveraged a quirk of the GitHub-to-Packagist publishing flow: a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization.' Early detection requires monitoring version control events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Git tag creation events within official organizations (laravel-lang/*) and cross-reference tag commit SHAs against source repository commit history. Alert when a tag in an official org resolves to a commit from a different owner/fork. Packagist-level detection: flag version releases where source commit author differs from repository owner.

suggestion.title: Rapid Republication of Historical Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Republication of historical tags continues in bursts, with multiple repositories receiving rewrites within seconds of each other. Total count climbs past 700 versions.' Anomalous bulk version activity indicating supply chain poisoning rather than normal development.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk republication of historical versions within a short timeframe (e.g., >50 versions across a package namespace in <5 minutes). Flag version republications where commit authors or source forks change. Alert on version re-publication after a package has been stale for 6+ months.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Tag Creation or Rewrite in Monitored Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—direct evidence of tag manipulation as delivery vector. Pipeline missed entire persistence/execution layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git tag creation/overwrite events on protected branches or high-value packages. Flag tags created by service accounts with unusual timing, pushed outside normal CI/CD windows, or modifying version tags retrospectively. Correlate with commits containing obfuscated shell code or network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized CI/CD Environment Variable or Secret Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'CI Secrets'—pipeline missed credential-access phase entirely. Attack objective was secret exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious reads or exports of CI environment variables ($GITHUB_TOKEN, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET) in workflow logs. Flag workflows triggered from unexpected commits, pull requests from forked repos, or unsigned commits accessing secrets. Correlate with exfiltration patterns (HTTP POST to external domains, DNS lookups to attacker infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Package Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes rewritten package tags leading to compromised distribution—pipeline missed initial execution within downstream users' CI pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor `composer install` / `composer update` commands for unexpected downloads of packages from non-canonical registries or CDN mirrors. Baseline expected package versions per project; alert on version downgrades or pre-release/dev versions in production environments. Track child processes spawned by composer post-install scripts, particularly shell invocations to external URLs or credential references.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connection from CI/CD Workflow to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack payload must exfiltrate secrets; article title identifies 'steal CI Secrets'—no network-based detection use case provided despite clear exfil requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected DNS lookups or HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated from CI/CD container IPs with outbound requests containing base64-encoded environment variables or bearer tokens in User-Agent or request headers. Alert on connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains during workflow execution. Implement egress filtering baseline per project.

suggestion.title: Repository Maintainer Account Compromise or Credential Misuse
suggestion.rationale: For tags across multiple packages to be rewritten, attacker required maintainer-level access—article strongly implies account compromise; pipeline missed initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication events for maintainer accounts: login from new geographies/ASNs, API token generation not tied to named applications, or successful authentication after failed attempts. Track API access patterns to repository administration endpoints (tag creation, branch protection changes, secret management). Correlate with downstream package download anomalies (spike in installation of specific version in short window).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48172 Exploited' — indicates active in-the-wild exploitation. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial-access detections despite this clear vulnerability reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to cPanel endpoints targeting LiteSpeed plugin installation directories or known vulnerable paths. Alert on 4xx→5xx responses or successful 200 responses followed by unexpected child-process spawning under httpd/lsws UID context. Apply signature rules for known CVE-2026-48172 POC traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Script Execution from LiteSpeed Daemon Context
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Run Scripts as Root' — explicit script execution component. Pipeline identified zero execution-phase techniques despite phrase 'scripts' in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell interpreter spawning (bash, sh, python, perl) with parent process = LiteSpeed httpd/lsws daemon user. Flag if spawned from unexpected working directory or with base64/obfuscated command lines. Correlate with recent HTTP requests or file writes to plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly 'Run Scripts as Root' — this is privilege escalation from unprivileged web-server UID to UID 0. Pipeline missed T1548 entirely and failed to flag escalation kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo/su invocation originating from LiteSpeed parent process tree, or root-context child processes spawned by web-server UID. Flag capability escalation, setuid wrapper exploitation, or cPanel API calls from httpd context requesting privileged operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write to cPanel/LiteSpeed Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: CVE in plugin implies file-write primitive to plugin directory followed by execution — standard web-app exploitation pattern. Article body truncated, but title confirms plugin-based exploit requiring file placement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-creation events in LiteSpeed plugin paths (/usr/local/lsws/conf/*, /usr/local/lsws/plugins/*, cPanel-managed plugin directories) with HTTP request traffic, then execution of those files within 60 seconds. Alert on script file double-extensions or executable writes from web-server context.

suggestion.title: Nginx Process Crash or Restart Loop (DoS Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'Enables DoS attacks.' Memory pool exploitation (implied by 'poolslip' name) manifests as process crashes with SIGSEGV/SIGABRT or rapid worker restart loops—core DoS signal pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx master/worker process termination with memory-related exit codes (exit code 139, SIGSEGV, SIGABRT). Flag rapid restart patterns (>3 restarts/minute). Correlate with inbound network traffic spike to confirm DoS correlation rather than legitimate failure.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from Nginx Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Code Execution Attacks' enabled by vulnerability. Pipeline failed to generate detection for any child processes, shell invocations, or privilege-escalation syscalls originating from Nginx UID—the primary post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nginx process (uid < 1000) spawning interpreters (bash, sh, zsh, python) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc, nslookup). Flag file writes to /etc, /var/spool, /root from Nginx UID. Monitor for unusual socket creation or network outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Request Triggering Memory Violation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name 'poolslip' directly implies memory pool handling flaw. Article states exploitation enables code execution, confirming request-based trigger mechanism. Pipeline did not generate any HTTP request-based detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with abnormally large header values (>8KB per header), duplicate Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding headers, malformed/non-standard header combinations, or request sizes exceeding Nginx buffer pool size defaults. Correlate with Nginx error logs for 'buffer overflow', 'memory allocation failure', or 'invalid request header'.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Package Publish Without 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states npm now gates publishing behind 2FA. Attackers targeting package takeover will bypass this control; lack of use case means no detection for publish attempts circumventing 2FA enforcement ('2FA-Gated Publishing' is the core defense).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package publish events where 2FA challenge was bypassed or not enforced for high-risk publishers. Correlate successful publishes from accounts with 2FA enabled against baseline of normal publish patterns and detect deviations (e.g., publish from unusual IP after failed 2FA checks).

suggestion.title: Installation of npm Package from Unapproved Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Package Install Controls'—npm is now restricting where packages can be installed from. Attackers may bypass this by pointing npm clients to malicious or uncontrolled registries ('install controls' imply detection when controls are circumvented).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm registry configuration changes away from official registry (npmjs.com) in CI/CD pipelines or dev environments. Flag installations from private/unauthorized registries, especially during supply chain compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Package Version Installation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Install controls imply version pinning and dependency locking—deviations (forced downgrades to versions before 2FA era, pre-release versions bypassing security checks) indicate supply chain attack. Article context: controls are to prevent this ('controls against supply chain attacks').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm package version installs deviate from lockfile-pinned versions or when pre-release/yanked versions are force-installed. Correlate with account compromise signals (stolen tokens, unusual CI runner IPs).

suggestion.title: npm Token Compromise Preceding 2FA-Bypassing Publish
suggestion.rationale: 2FA-gating means legacy offline tokens (if not revoked) become a primary attack vector. No use case exists for detecting token misuse + publish conflation, yet this is the direct threat model npm is defending against.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm authentication tokens appearing in code repositories, CI logs, or environment variable dumps. Flag tokens used for publishes from IPs/times inconsistent with legitimate maintainer activity. Cross-reference with 2FA enforcement status: if 2FA is enabled but publish succeeded via legacy token, escalate.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution During Composer Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential stealer payload deployed via Laravel-Lang packages. Composer package installation triggers arbitrary code execution (via autoload scripts) — must detect anomalous processes spawned during/immediately after 'composer install' or 'composer update'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-PHP child processes spawned by php.exe/composer.phar within 30 seconds of composer execution. Flag curl, wget, powershell, cmd, bash spawned from PHP context. Monitor for process creation with network access to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Credential Store Access by PHP Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'credential stealer' payload — must detect processes accessing browser credential stores, SSH keys, AWS credentials, environment variables from PHP/Composer contexts immediately post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads from credential paths (AppData/Roaming/[Chrome|Firefox|Edge], ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, .git/config) by PHP processes. Alert on environment variable enumeration patterns (repeated getenv calls).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Unknown Domain from PHP Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must transmit stolen data to attacker C2. Article promises credential exfiltration — detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP from PHP/Composer processes to non-whitelisted external domains carrying credential material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from php.exe to IPs not in organization ASN/CDN whitelist within 2 minutes of package installation. Monitor request bodies for Base64 or escaped credential patterns (AWS keys, SSH private keys, OAuth tokens).

suggestion.title: Laravel-Lang Malicious Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets specific 'Laravel-Lang packages' — must detect installation of affected package versions. Should monitor composer.lock/package.json for malicious versions with known CVE or IOC correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate installed laravel-lang/* package versions against known-bad versions published by Aikido or package registry metadata. Flag installations from non-standard Packagist instances or custom composer repositories.

suggestion.title: Composer Update/Install Without Version Pinning
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit wildcard version constraints. Detect development environments with loose composer version constraints allowing install of malicious package releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json for laravel-lang/* with wildcards (*, ^, ~) and correlate against composer.lock to detect version downgrades or unexpected major version jumps. Alert on absent composer.lock in source control.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Execution in Package Autoload
suggestion.rationale: PHP composer packages execute scripts defined in composer.json 'scripts' section during install. Credential stealer likely embedded in post-install or post-update hooks — detect non-standard script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 'composer install' invoked with '--no-scripts' flag bypass or wrapper scripts. Alert on execution of scripts outside vendor/bin (indicating direct package code execution). Track PHP file inclusions from unexpected package directories.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-9082 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and CISA KEV lists actively exploited vulnerabilities. Must detect unpatched Drupal instances across fleet, accounting for patch lag ('patch lag is the silent killer').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all assets for Drupal Core installations; flag any running vulnerable versions (prior to patch release 2026-05-27) regardless of self-reported patch status. Correlate web server fingerprints and known Drupal paths with vulnerability scanner telemetry.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attack on Drupal Database API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'SQL injection vulnerability' and 'specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' Requires detection of malicious SQL patterns in request payloads targeting Drupal database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Drupal containing SQL injection indicators (UNION-based, time-based, boolean-based, OR 1=1, SLEEP, BENCHMARK, database function calls) in query parameters targeting database abstraction API endpoints. Flag specially crafted requests with abnormal encoding or nested structures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Requires detection of unauthorized privilege elevation following successful SQL injection, specifically elevation of Drupal user roles or permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious permission changes in Drupal user tables or role assignments following SQL injection attack attempts. Alert on creation of administrative accounts from HTTP requests, elevation of web-process-spawned accounts, or unauthorized role reassignment in user_roles tables.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from Drupal SQL Injection Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for...remote code execution.' Requires detection of code execution indicators following successful SQL injection compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Drupal web server processes (Apache, Nginx, PHP-FPM). Detect shell execution, script interpretation, or command invocation originating from the database abstraction layer or HTTP request handlers following exploitation.

suggestion.title: Drupal Installation Exposure Baseline Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references federal patch compliance deadline (2026-05-27). Must establish complete Drupal asset inventory to quantify remediation scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Catalog all externally-facing Drupal installations via web fingerprinting (HTTP headers, Drupal-specific paths like /admin, /sites, /themes), DNS records, and SSL certificates. Correlate with vulnerability scanner to baseline vulnerable instances against federal compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: LNK Shortcut Launching Remote PowerShell Script
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The command line of the shortcut: Example of the PowerShell script downloaded and executed by the shortcut' and describes attackers using ZIP-archived LNK files to covertly execute external PowerShell. No detection use case generated despite this being the primary initial access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lnk or shortcut files spawning powershell.exe with remote script URLs (http/https). Parent process tree should show file explorer or shell accessing temp directories. Look for encoded -ExecutionPolicy Bypass or IEX patterns.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Registry Persistence via YandexBrowser_setup Run Key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup' as early persistence. No use case captured despite unambiguous registry modification for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU/HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for suspicious value names (YandexBrowser, decoys of legitimate software). Alert if registry writes originate from temporary directories or PowerShell child processes. Correlate with fixed.ps1 file drops.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Patching for Multi-User RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article section titled 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' describes a clear persistence and lateral-movement technique, but no detection use case generated. This is a highly specific and suspicious indicator of advanced persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file modifications to termsrv.dll (typically %System32%) or suspicious copies in temp/appdata. Watch for process hollowing or DLL injection into svchost.exe or lsass.exe after termsrv.dll changes. Cross-reference with failed RDP login attempts or unexpected RDP session initiations from unprivileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel for Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as a C2 mechanism. No detection use case despite this being a documented persistence and command-control tactic used by Cloud Atlas.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ssh.exe or sshd.exe processes spawned from unusual parent processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe). Alert on inbound SSH connections from internal hosts to external IPs on high ports. Correlate with registry keys or scheduled tasks created for persistence. Watch for reverse shell patterns (-R flag, local-to-remote port binding).

suggestion.title: RevSocks SOCKS5 Proxy and Tor Tunneling Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article section 'Tor tunneling' and tool list 'RevSocks Tor tunneling' describe traffic obfuscation via SOCKS proxy chains, but no detection use case generated. This is a signature C2 evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SOCKS5 proxy handshake patterns (0x05 0x01 0x00 in network telemetry). Alert on internal processes connecting to SOCKS proxies on atypical ports. Watch for Tor directionary queries (port 53 to suspicious resolvers) or connections to known Tor exit node ASNs. Correlate with PowerShell or cmd.exe child processes.

suggestion.title: PowerShower Credential Harvesting and Dumping
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber)' as a discrete payload stage, but no detection use case for credential access or memory dumping. The multi-stage architecture (Fixed.ps1 → PowerShower → credential grabber) is not decomposed into detectable actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell child processes for credential dumping techniques (Get-Credential, credential objects enumeration). Alert on process memory access from PowerShell to lsass.exe or credential manager APIs. Watch for exfiltration of SAM/NTDS hashes or Browser credential stores via HTTP/HTTPS to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attack on Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and 'exploitation attempts have been detected in the wild'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite confirming active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal application endpoints for SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, DROP, --, /**/) in parameters. Correlate payloads with PostgreSQL error responses (HTTP 500, 'ERROR:' in body) or abnormal database query execution timing from same source IP within exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Attack Surface Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exploitable without authentication'. Detection must flag SQL injection payloads arriving at unauthenticated endpoints, not just authenticated user sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HTTP requests to Drupal endpoints lack valid authentication (no session token, failed auth headers) but contain SQL keywords, database-related parameters, or encoded metacharacters (%;, %2d%2d, 0x). Flag repeated failed auth + payload attempts from single source.

suggestion.title: Post-Injection Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article lists impact as 'remote code execution, privilege escalation, and information disclosure' yet pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation stage when SQL injection enables shell access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned from web service parent processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) post-Drupal request. Alert on unusual parent-child relationships, execution outside maintenance windows, or processes with suspicious command-line arguments (wget, curl, nc).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Error Leakage in HTTP Responses
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection typically leaks database structure via error messages. Article: 'SQL injection...resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion'. Errors are reconnaissance/confirmation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response bodies from Drupal for PostgreSQL error strings ('ERROR:', 'FATAL:', relation/column 'does not exist', syntax errors). Correlate repeated error responses from same source IP as indicator of active fuzzing or exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Enumeration Prior to Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists vulnerable versions (8.9.x, 10.4.x before 10.4.10, 10.5.x before 10.5.10, etc.). Attackers enumerate version before deploying version-specific exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Drupal version fingerprinting attempts (requests to /CHANGELOG.txt, /README.md, /admin/about, X-Generator header extraction, robots.txt) followed within 30 minutes by SQL injection payloads from same source IP. Temporal correlation indicates weaponized reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Commands from Web Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Successful SQL injection execution allows attacker-controlled database operations. Article: 'deletion of database data' is explicit impact. Database audit logs should detect abnormal DML/DDL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs for commands issued by web service accounts (drupal_user, postgres_app user) containing DDL (DROP TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE) or privilege escalation (GRANT/REVOKE) outside normal application scope. Flag time-delay functions (SLEEP, WAITFOR) indicating blind SQL injection verification.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Infrastructure Takedown Attribution - VPN Service Used by Known Groups
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states '25 Ransomware Groups' used a dismantled VPN; should map ransomware family C2 callbacks routed through the VPN provider's ASN/IP ranges to establish infrastructure provenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound traffic from known ransomware families to IP space/ASNs associated with the dismantled VPN provider. Correlate with reported C2 sinkhole or takedown metadata. Flag long-duration VPN tunnel establishment from ransomware beacons.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Path via Dismantled VPN - Ransomware Data Staging
suggestion.rationale: Global VPN takedowns typically surface exfiltration infrastructure; article likely describes how 25 groups routed stolen data through the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained data transfer over non-standard ports or encrypted tunnels to the VPN provider's known endpoints. Baseline exfiltration patterns associated with staging/leak site uploads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Facilitation - VPN-Assisted Pivot Tracking
suggestion.rationale: If article describes how ransomware groups pivoted across compromised networks using the VPN, lateral movement detection should key on traffic asymmetry or unusual hop counts via the VPN ASN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internal lateral-movement traffic (e.g., RDP, SMB, WinRM) originating from endpoints with active VPN tunnel sessions to the dismantled provider.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes typosquatting attack: 'a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions' and references fifa26.shop as phishing infrastructure. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no detection logic for domain similarity or known-malicious FIFA impersonators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and web access for domains within 1–3 Levenshtein edits of fifa.com, fifa2026.com, worldcup2026.com. Correlate with recent WHOIS registrations, privacy-enabled records, and bulk registrant patterns. Alert on user access from consumer/educational networks to newly registered FIFA-themed domains.

suggestion.title: Phishing Registration Form Submission on Suspicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential harvest: fake forms capture 'name, email address, and phone number' with layout matching legitimate FIFA site. 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange at first.' Pipeline missed detection for form-based credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to non-whitelisted domains with form fields matching FIFA registration schema (email, phone, name, country, address). Flag domains with HTML rendering identical or >85% similar to official fifa.com. Correlate high-volume form submissions from different users to same domain with phishing-feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: Fake Payment Gateway Activity and Card Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and shows payment form capture. Pipeline failed to map collection phase or detect payment-fraud infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST submissions of credit card data to payment endpoints on non-PCI-compliant hosts or domains not registered with official FIFA merchant processors. Alert on payment form HTML served from typosquatted domains or SSL certificates issued recently. Correlate with abnormal outbound connections to attacker payment-processing gateways.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Distribution via Social Media and Email
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multiple delivery channels: 'sponsored search results, ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Pipeline did not map initial-access vectors or email/social phishing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails and ads containing FIFA/World Cup 2026 keywords with embedded links to typosquatted domains. Monitor click-through events on suspicious FIFA-related links from bulk campaigns. Correlate sender reputation, DKIM/SPF failures, and URL shortening services with phishing-feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: Website Cloning and Infrastructure Acquisition for Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes visual/functional cloning: 'copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow' with side-by-side comparison. Pipeline failed to map infrastructure acquisition (T1583.006) or detect website clone patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor certificate transparency logs for SSL issuance on FIFA-themed domains. Correlate CSS/layout similarity to official FIFA site (favicon hash, stylesheet URLs, JavaScript libraries) with WHOIS registration metadata. Alert on hosting infrastructure supporting multiple FIFA-impersonation domains.

suggestion.title: Event-Driven Bulk Phishing Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeted timing: 'in the run-up to major events' with emphasis on urgency ('interested, impatient and...worried that the tickets...will sell out'). Pipeline missed pattern detection for event-correlated infrastructure acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WHOIS domain registrations, DNS zone creation, and SSL certificate issuance for clusters of FIFA-related domains registered within 7–14 days of World Cup event announcements or ticket-sale windows. Flag registrants with history of event-driven phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Initial Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'From edge appliance to enterprise compromise'—F5 is the confirmed attack entry point. Zero detection use cases generated despite being primary initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP admin interfaces and known vulnerable endpoints for exploitation attempts. Track anomalous login post-compromise and outbound command channels from appliance to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Confluence Credential Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Confluence server for credential theft and identity compromise.' No credential access detection use cases surfaced despite explicit mention of theft activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk Confluence user enumeration, export requests targeting credential stores or user lists, and authentication from non-standard client IPs/user-agents after F5 compromise.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'threat actor attempted Kerberos relay.' Pipeline mapped zero techniques for this privileged attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Event IDs 4768, 4769 for pre-auth encryption type downgrades, forged TGTs, and unusual TGT requests from service accounts. Correlate with NTLM signing disabled on critical assets.

suggestion.title: Edge-to-Internal Lateral Movement via Confluence
suggestion.rationale: Attack pivots from external F5 to internal Confluence server. Article: 'Multi-stage' and 'Linux intrusion' suggest OS-variant lateral movement techniques not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH or direct service-to-service connections from compromised F5 appliance to internal Linux systems and Windows servers hosting Confluence. Flag compromised service-account usage post-Confluence breach.

suggestion.title: Defender EDR Evasion Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft Defender detected, blocked, and unraveled the attack.' Defender's observable blocks should translate to evasion detection use cases; none extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution and network activity for obfuscation, credential dumping tools, and exploitation frameworks detected post-F5 compromise. Correlate with Defender block timestamps.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Delivery via Spearphishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' as the attack mechanism. No detection use case was generated for phishing-borne malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails targeting .gov.ua or impersonating Ukrainian government domains. Detect Prometheus binary execution (DLL injection, process hollowing patterns) following suspicious email attachment opens. Flag rapid file copies and registry modifications post-detonation.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-delivered Prometheus implies C2 callback and command execution, but no network detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections to non-whitelisted external infrastructure from affected government workstations. Detect DNS queries for domains matching Prometheus C2 patterns (high entropy subdomains, newly registered .xyz/.top/.online domains hoisting Ukrainian targets).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Prometheus Execution
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus malware implicitly harvests credentials from compromised Ukraine government systems, enabling lateral movement. No credential theft or use-case was mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect memory access by Prometheus process to LSASS, clipboard APIs, and keylogging patterns (GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx). Monitor for failed/brute-force logons using stolen credentials from government email domains days following phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Government Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Successful Prometheus deployment in government networks implies stolen credentials used for internal reconnaissance and lateral movement; no post-compromise detection was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logons by government user accounts from non-standard geolocations, off-hours, or impossible travel times post-phishing. Detect AD enumeration (Get-ADUser, dsquery), network scanning, and sensitive file access by newly-compromised service accounts.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter Infrastructure Reuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ghostwriter is a known Russian-affiliated threat actor with observable patterns. Pipeline missed attribution-driven IOC correlation against historical Ghostwriter C2, sender domains, and phishing templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference sender domains, reply-to addresses, and hosting ASNs against prior Ghostwriter-attributed phishing campaigns (OSINT: abuse.ch, VirusTotal, Shodan). Flag typosquatted .ua domains or compromised legitimate government subdomains matching historical actor patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Registry or Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting of government entities; Prometheus persistence mechanisms (registry run keys, WMI event subscriptions, scheduled tasks) should be detected to prevent re-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Registry modifications (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\Load) containing Prometheus binary paths. Detect WMI event subscriptions or scheduled tasks executing unsigned binaries from AppData or Temp folders.

suggestion.title: SQL injection pattern detection in YesWiki Bazar endpoint POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement'—core attack mechanism. Pipeline generated zero detections for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comments, time-delay signatures). Direct request-body content inspection is missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP POST requests to */bazar/*vue=formulaire* for SQL keywords in decoded body (UNION SELECT, OR\s+1\s*=\s*1, ';\s*--, SLEEP\(, BENCHMARK\() with case-insensitive matching. Correlate with HTTP 200-201 responses to identify blind SQLi success indicators.

suggestion.title: Database credential hash access post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'—credential access (T1110, T1040) is the objective, but zero detection generated. No hunt for password column reads or user table enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for SELECT statements targeting password, hash, or credential columns in yeswiki_users table preceded by unauthenticated HTTP requests. Look for UNION-based extraction patterns and result set size anomalies.

suggestion.title: YesWiki version enumeration and vulnerable asset discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions '4.6.1, 4.6.2, doryphore-dev'—recon phase (T1595.002) requires identifying deployments. No detection for version banners, fingerprinting probes, or version disclosure endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to YesWiki version-disclosure paths (/?version, /CHANGELOG, /doc/version, robots.txt) or responses containing version strings matching 4.6.1-4.6.2 patterns. Correlate with subsequent Bazar endpoint probing from same source.

suggestion.title: Large-scale data exfiltration following SQLi exploitation success
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker extracts 'full database'—exfiltration (T1041) phase unaddressed. No detection for outbound data transfer, staging, or C2 beaconing post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound traffic from YesWiki application servers. Trigger on sustained large-volume outbound connections (>100 MB), unusual destination ASNs, or exfiltration-tool user agents (curl, wget to non-standard ports) initiated immediately after successful SQLi payload indicators.

suggestion.title: FormManager::create() parameter tampering and bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable sink as 'FormManager::create()'—application-layer code path. Detect direct parameter manipulation, missing CSRF tokens, or type-confusion attacks targeting form creation logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests with form-creation parameters (FormManager, vue=formulaire) where request lacks expected CSRF token, has duplicate/malformed parameters, or uses type-confusion payloads (array vs string inputs where string expected).

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum successful PATCH exploitation with confirmed response codes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows file ops outside shared directory'—move/copy/rename operations must complete successfully. Recommended hunts detect payloads but not confirmed exploitation; impact phase requires HTTP 200/204 confirmation with correlated request/response timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests with fromPath/toPath traversal payloads that receive 200 or 204 response codes and are followed within 5 seconds by GET requests to endpoints outside the share path, indicating successful file relocation. Correlate HTTP logs with web server access logs to confirm the target file is now accessible from an unintended location.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public share hash enumeration with invalid-share error patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'hash' parameter in public share URL, implying attackers must discover valid share hashes before exploitation. Recommended UC_20_2 detects volume but not the reconnaissance intent; 404 or 403 error patterns distinguish guessing from legitimate use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of PATCH requests to /public/api/resources with unique hash parameter values that receive 403 Forbidden or 401 Unauthorized responses (invalid share), followed by a successful 200 response to a different hash. This indicates hash enumeration + successful pivot. Set baseline tolerance for failed hashes per source IP and time window.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum path-sanitizer bypass via backend exception logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in `resourcePatchHandler` sanitizer being skipped due to early filepath.Join in `publicPatchHandler`. Exploitation attempts should produce detectable exception patterns. No use case for application-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FileBrowser Quantum backend logs for exceptions or panics originating from `filepath.Join`, `publicPatchHandler`, or path validation code during or immediately after PATCH requests. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP activity. Baseline exception rates per path-handling function and alert on 3x+ deviation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized file system operations outside FileBrowser Quantum share root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: files are moved/copied/renamed 'outside the shared directory.' HTTP-level detection confirms requests but not impact; file system monitoring closes the detection loop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If the FileBrowser Quantum process can be monitored, detect file operations (rename, move, copy) performed by the FileBrowser service account on paths outside the configured share root directory. Correlate timing and source paths. Flag operations that move files into world-readable directories or system paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Art-Template Package Versions with Backdoor Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article states versions 4.13.3, 4.13.5-4.13.6 were weaponized; npm.js and dependency manifests should be scanned for these pinned versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for npm install/require of art-template versions 4.13.3, 4.13.5, or 4.13.6 in build logs, CI/CD pipelines, or dependency manifests. Cross-reference package-lock.json or yarn.lock for pinned vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Domain IOCs in Bundle Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline injected hardcoded domains v3.jiathis[.]com, utaq[.]cfww[.]shop, l1ewsu3yjkqeroy[.]xyz into npm bundles; scanning source and transpiled bundles for these strings is a direct detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .js files in node_modules and built bundles for literal domain strings v3.jiathis.com, utaq.cfww.shop, and l1ewsu3yjkqeroy.xyz. Monitor DNS requests and HTTP requests to these domains. Flag any script tag injection containing these domains in runtime network events.

suggestion.title: Detect Safari Browser Fingerprinting Patterns on iOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states implant 'fingerprints site visitors' and 'only activates on Safari running on iOS 11.0 through 17.2.' Fingerprinting scripts with iOS/Safari detection logic are a clear behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript that conditionally branches on user-agent checks for Safari and iOS version strings (11.0-17.2). Look for feature-detection code patterns that isolate Safari/iOS targets. Flag unusual fingerprinting data exfiltration to external domains.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Beaconing Every 10 Seconds to Coruna Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'beacons victim data to command-and-control servers every ten seconds.' Regular 10-second interval network traffic is a strong behavioral signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for regular (periodic) outbound connections to C2 domains at ~10-second intervals. Baseline DNS and HTTP request frequency per asset; flag traffic with 9-12 second periodicity to art-template implant domains. Correlate with session key cecd08aa6ff548c2 or campaign code CHMK6IG08F42496C22 in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Detect Script Loader Injection in npm Bundles Across Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article describes evolution: v4.13.3 used obfuscation to hide loaders, v4.13.5-4.13.6 removed obfuscation and injected plaintext loaders into browser bundles. Scanning for unexpected <script> injections into art-template outputs is actionable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare transpiled/minified JavaScript output from art-template across version boundaries. Flag new <script> tags or loader function calls not present in baseline builds. Monitor build artifact checksums (SHA-256: f31bdd069fe7966ae11be1f78ee5dd44445938856dd1df12379e0e84a6851f5c) against known clean builds.

suggestion.title: Correlate CVE-2024-23222 Exploitation Attempts with iOS 17.2 Cutoff Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware exits silently on iOS 17.3+ and correlates this to CVE-2024-23222 (WebKit patch), indicating intentional targeting of unpatched versions for browser-level exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Safari crashes or WebKit exploitation attempts on iOS 11.0-17.2. Flag CVE-2024-23222 exploitation payloads. Correlate with art-template dependency presence. Alert if unpatched iOS devices with art-template dependency attempt access to Coruna-linked domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Batch File Execution from Email/Downloads Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Deliver Banana RAT Through Malicious Batch Files'—batch files are the primary execution vector and should trigger behavioral detection when spawned from typical email/download staging directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .bat or .cmd files created or executed from Downloads, %Temp%, or email client temporary directories. Alert if execution occurs within minutes of file creation (indicates fresh extract-and-run) or if parent process is explorer.exe or an email client.

suggestion.title: NF-e Themed Phishing Email with Batch File Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'NF-e Invoice Lures'—NF-e is Brazil's electronic invoicing standard. Detection should look for emails with invoice-themed subject lines (Portuguese language, 'NF-e', 'Nota Fiscal') and .bat/.cmd/.exe attachments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound emails with Portuguese keywords (NF-e, Nota Fiscal, Fatura) in subject or body, containing file attachments with extensions .bat, .cmd, .scr, or double-extensions (.pdf.bat). Correlate with file reputation (unknown/malicious hashes).

suggestion.title: Batch File Spawning Scripting Engine with Suspicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery chains typically use batch files as initial stagers that then spawn PowerShell or cmd.exe with encoded/obfuscated commands. Article describes batch file as delivery mechanism, implying execution chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .bat/.cmd files (parent process) spawning powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, or cmd.exe children, especially if parent filename is uncommon, comes from Downloads/Temp, or command line contains encoding switches (-enc, -e, -EncodedCommand) or suspicious operators (|, >, IEX).

suggestion.title: Banana RAT C2 Beaconing Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Banana RAT' as the delivered payload. C2 communication is inherent to RAT function; detection should monitor for known Banana RAT infrastructure or behavioral patterns (periodic outbound connections, specific User-Agents, port usage).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Banana RAT C2 domains or IPs (if available in threat intelligence). Alternatively, detect periodic beaconing behavior (regular interval callbacks from suspicious processes) or connections to uncommon ports from newly spawned batch/PowerShell processes.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Batch/PowerShell Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT payloads typically establish persistence mechanisms. Batch files spawning processes that modify registry Run/RunOnce keys indicate infection establishment, a step between execution and command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawned from batch files or PowerShell attempt to write to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* keys, especially with values pointing to suspicious file paths or command lines.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cron Job Creation on FreePBX
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'six-layer persistence' on FreePBX systems. Cron is a standard Linux persistence vector. Zero cron-based detections in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crontab modifications or /etc/cron.d file writes from www-data, asterisk, or fop user contexts. Alert on cron entries executing shell commands to non-standard ports, external IPs, or spawning reverse shells. Baseline legitimate FreePBX maintenance tasks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Shell Upload to FreePBX Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'hackers use' persistence mechanisms but no detection for PHP/web-accessible uploads, common FreePBX attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file creation in /var/www/html/admin/modules, /var/www/html/rest, and web-root after compromise. Correlate with web server access logs (POST to upload endpoints returning 200) followed by execution of recently-created PHP via php-fpm process spawning shells.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Database Module Injection Persistence
suggestion.rationale: FreePBX stores modules/configuration in MySQL. Article references persistence layers but pipeline generated no database-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MySQL databases (freepbx, asterisk) for unauthorized INSERT/UPDATE operations adding modules with suspicious names or paths. Flag database modifications from www-data user executing non-standard module registration queries outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Outbound Reverse Shell Callback from FreePBX Process
suggestion.rationale: Persistence requires C2 communication. Article headline establishes 'maintained access' but no command-and-control detection present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from apache2, php-fpm, or asterisk processes to non-standard ports (8888, 4444, 5555) or suspicious external IPs. Alert on process trees: php-fpm spawning sh/bash with immediate network callbacks, baseline against known VOIP trunk traffic.

suggestion.title: Asterisk Configuration Persistence via Extensions.conf Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions '6-layer persistence.' Asterisk config files (/etc/asterisk/*.conf) are filesystem-level persistence vectors not covered by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/asterisk/extensions.conf, sip.conf, iax.conf for unauthorized additions of dial patterns pointing to attacker IPs, SIP peer definitions with non-standard addresses, or exten rules calling external contexts. Flag file modifications outside change-control windows with suspicious timing.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet Command & Control Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: DDoS-for-hire operations require C2 infrastructure to coordinate attacks across compromised hosts. Article explicitly establishes 'Kimwolf DDoS Botnet' but pipeline produced zero C2 communication indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for regular heartbeat connections (beaconing) to rare or malicious IP destinations on non-standard ports. DDoS botnets typically use HTTP/HTTPS tunneling or custom protocols for C2. Flag internal hosts with anomalous outbound connection patterns: high frequency, low data volume, consistent timing intervals.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Execution from User-Writable Paths
suggestion.rationale: Botnets execute malware on compromised systems via exploitation or social engineering. Title describes botnet operations but no execution-phase indicators were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious executables spawned from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or other user-writable directories. Flag process injection patterns (suspicious parent-child relationships). Monitor for scriptable interpreters (PowerShell, cmd.exe, VBScript) executing from non-standard locations or with obfuscated command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Traffic Volume from Internal Hosts
suggestion.rationale: DDoS attack participation generates distinctive traffic signatures—high-volume outbound data. Article explicitly states 'DDoS attacks' but no impact-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal hosts sending anomalously high packet counts or sustained data volume to external destinations (especially UDP or fragmented traffic). Establish baseline per-host traffic profiles and flag deviations. Detect participation in known DDoS attack patterns (botnet-sourced volumetric attacks).

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Threat Actor Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Kimwolf' as the threat actor, establishing actor attribution. Pipeline did not surface actor name or correlate against known infrastructure/IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network observables against threat intelligence on Kimwolf infrastructure (C2 domains, hosting provider IPs, ASNs, malware hashes). Detect DNS lookups and HTTP requests to previously sinkholed or takedown Kimwolf C2 domains. Monitor for malware samples attributed to Kimwolf botnet family.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Loading via Service Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits require loading vulnerable drivers, typically via service registry paths (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services). Pipeline produced no detection for this critical execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\* for ImagePath values pointing to suspicious or unsigned driver binaries. Correlate with process execution attempting to load these services via reg.exe or sc.exe.

suggestion.title: Execution of Known Vulnerable Drivers by Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies specific vulnerable drivers are discussable. Pipeline extracted no driver hashes, filenames, or signatures despite this being core IOC data for BYOVD detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain hash allowlist of signed-but-vulnerable drivers (e.g., Intel EPTM, NVIDIA, MSI driver families). Alert on unsigned kernel modules or signed drivers loaded from non-standard paths or by unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Code Execution via Driver Exploitation Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD is fundamentally a kernel privilege escalation technique. Pipeline identified no kernel-level execution indicators such as suspicious ring0 callbacks, interrupt descriptor table (IDT) hooks, or driver entry point anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious driver loading patterns: mismatched module base addresses, drivers loaded with unusual privilege levels, or drivers that modify kernel structures (ETW disabling, ACL removal, etc.).

suggestion.title: BYOVD-Specific Evasion: Security Tool Disabling via Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD privilege escalation often precedes defensive measure tampering. Article context implies evasion. Pipeline detected no defense evasion indicators like EDR process termination, minifilter driver removal, or ETW tracing disablement.
