suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single processes reading multiple credential source categories: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.aws/*, ~/.vault*, KUBECONFIG environment, %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/*, %APPDATA%/Roaming/Slack/, browser password stores, Ethereum wallets, .env files in application roots. Alert when access to 3+ distinct credential categories occurs within minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exfiltration Forensic Artifact Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery. On Windows hosts, the chain [truncated].' Cleanup behavior correlates with prior exfiltration and warrants anti-forensics detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file deletion events following credential collection and outbound exfiltration. Alert on deletion chains targeting temporary directories (/tmp, %TEMP%), dropped second-stage files, or payload staging areas. Correlate file deletions with prior network egress to C2 within 60-second windows.

suggestion.title: Platform-Aware Stealer Execution Across Linux, macOS, and Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The launcher logic is platform-aware and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows.' Multi-OS payload deployment and execution requires platform-specific detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP spawning platform-native shells (bash on Linux/macOS, powershell/cmd on Windows) from web application contexts. Detect unusual binary execution in /tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA% following vendor file loads. Alert on process chains executing reconnaissance commands (whoami, uname, systeminfo, Get-WmiObject) from PHP or Apache contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation with Rewritten Git Tag
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' When composer.lock pulls a tag hash that has been force-rewritten server-side, the installed code differs from expected source. Detection must hook composer install/update and validate package checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on composer install/require commands followed by PHP file execution from vendor/ with mismatched source-tree hash or obfuscated code patterns. Flag when package version in composer.lock does not match registry canonical hash or when git checkout of tag differs from upstream.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration from CI/CD Process
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets CI secrets: 'Steal CI Secrets.' Malicious code injected via Composer payload enumerates and exfiltrates environment variables containing GitHub tokens, deploy keys, AWS credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CI/CD job processes that reference sensitive environment variable names (regex: .*TOKEN.*|.*SECRET.*|.*KEY.*|.*CREDENTIAL.*) followed by write operations to non-standard locations, base64 encoding, or outbound HTTP/DNS calls. Flag curl/wget/netcat calls containing base64 blobs or credential-like strings.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Force-Push or Tag Rewrite to Repository
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: attacker gained repository access and rewrote tags. Article: 'Every Tag...Rewritten.' Detect git push --force or tag manipulation on production/shared repositories by unauthorized accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git push with --force, --force-with-lease, or tag deletion/rewrite commands to shared repositories. Correlate with unusual account authentication (new SSH key, VPN, geography, time-of-day deviation). Cross-reference with package maintainer account compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Base64-Encoded Payload in Installed Composer Package
suggestion.rationale: Malicious code injected into rewritten tags must evade detection. Expect obfuscation in vendor/ directory: 'Rewritten...to Steal' implies hidden payload not visible in casual source review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-install scan vendor/ directory for suspicious PHP patterns: nested preg_replace with /e modifier, base64_decode followed by eval/assert, shell metacharacters in strings, or excessive obfuscation (high entropy, packed code). Compare installed package binary hash against registry canonical hash.

suggestion.title: Unexpected DNS or Network Callback from Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload must exfiltrate secrets: 'Steal CI Secrets' implies outbound communication to attacker infrastructure. Build/test jobs should have predictable network footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline whitelisted DNS domains and IP ranges for CI/CD pipelines (package registries, artifact repos, public CDNs). Flag DNS queries to non-whitelisted TLDs or newly-registered domains. Alert on outbound connections carrying encoded data or connecting to IPs with low reputation or no RDNS.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must have gained write-access to push rewritten tags. Detect compromise of Laravel-Lang maintainer accounts or CI/CD deploy credentials: 'packages rewritten' requires privilege escalation or credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor maintainer account logins from unusual geography, device, or auth method. Flag new SSH keys or deploy tokens added to accounts. Detect git operations (push, tag, branch) by accounts not typically performing them. Alert on API token usage patterns deviating from baseline or tokens with repository write permissions used from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root' — indicates web request exploitation of plugin endpoint. Article body absent but title establishes T1190 attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs for public-facing app exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known LiteSpeed cPanel plugin paths (version-specific or enumerated endpoints) with command-injection payloads, path traversal, or file-upload attempts. Baseline legitimate plugin management traffic and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawn from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes impact: 'Run Scripts as Root.' Must detect privilege escalation from apache/nobody to UID=0. Pipeline failed to suggest any privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent processes running as web-server user (apache, nobody) spawning child processes with UID=0 or with setuid/setgid bits. Focus on shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or compiled binaries from /tmp or web-writable paths.

suggestion.title: Shell Script Execution from LiteSpeed Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Run Scripts as Root' — directly indicates scripting execution post-exploitation. No use case for shell/interpreter spawning from plugin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of bash, sh, perl, or python with parent process or working directory in /usr/local/lsws/*, /opt/litespeed/*, or web-accessible cPanel plugin directories. Flag command arguments for reverse-shell patterns or credential-theft indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Write to Web-Accessible LiteSpeed Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of plugin requires upload or injection of malicious code. Pipeline missed file-modification detection during initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .php, .cgi, .pl, .sh files in LiteSpeed plugin directories by the web-server user, especially if the file content contains base64, hex-encoded payloads, or known malware signatures. Correlate with preceding HTTP POST requests.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Root-Spawned cPanel Process
suggestion.rationale: Root privilege escalation almost always leads to C2 callback or persistence. Article likely contains C2 IOCs (IPs/domains), but pipeline extracted none and suggested no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections initiated by cPanel daemons or root-spawned descendants to external IPs. Flag queries for known malware C2 domains, newly registered domains, or IPs geographically inconsistent with the organization.

suggestion.title: Exploit Code Artifacts in Web Logs and Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Proof-of-concept or multi-stage exploitation payloads often leave traces in /tmp, /dev/shm, or web-server logs. Pipeline suggested no log-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web-server and cPanel logs for encoding patterns (base64, gzip, hex), common exploit/webshell file signatures, or requests with oversized payloads targeting the plugin endpoint. Correlate with unusual temp-directory file creation or wget/curl commands downloading files.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized NPM Package Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing'—implies detection should monitor for publish events circumventing 2FA or from unexpected origins. Detection is the inverse of the control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish commands from IP addresses with <5 days history associated with package maintainer account, or from VPN/proxy IPs not in historical baseline. Flag publish events where 2FA verification logs are absent or show bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Package Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article's 2FA requirement implies accounts are high-value targets. 'Package Install Controls' suggests defense against account takeover leading to malicious package updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm maintainer accounts (own 10+ packages or 10M+ weekly downloads) for: failed login bursts from credential-stuffing IPs, successful login followed by immediate package update, session tokens used from unexpected geographies within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Install controls referenced suggest npm detected risk in package installation phase. Postinstall scripts executing arbitrary code is the vector; detection should monitor execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall hooks that spawn shells, invoke curl/wget to external URLs, modify PATH, or write to sensitive directories (/etc, ~/.ssh). Flag installations where postinstall execution time exceeds 10 seconds or calls network tools.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use typosquatting. Article's mention of 'Package Install Controls' implies npm addresses this. Detection should identify lookalike packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly published packages (age <7 days) with names differing from top-1000 npm packages by single-character edits, case variations, or vowel omission. Flag if published by account without prior package history and installed by >10 distinct IPs within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Downgrade Attack on Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'Package Install Controls' phrasing suggests defense against version manipulation. Downgrade attacks force installation of older, unpatched package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm resolves to a version older than latest available without explicit version pinning in package.json or package-lock.json. Flag rapid major.minor version changes (e.g., 8.x → 5.x) within single build or across dependency tree.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dependency Injection via Registry Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Controls mentioned guard against registry-layer attacks. Detection should flag when package manifests unexpectedly add or modify dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package versions where dependencies were added/modified in postinstall rather than package.json, or where a maintainer's published version differs from the same commit tag in source repository. Alert on packages that inject dependencies of other high-value packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes Laravel-Lang packages as vectors—pipeline must detect package manager activity (composer install/require) with version anomalies, timing mismatches to public registries, or suspicious post-install hooks. Missing entirely from output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications or composer install/require commands installing Laravel-Lang; correlate installed package versions against official Packagist registry. Flag installations of unexpected versions, particularly those published outside normal maintenance windows or with unusual file hashes.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Post-Install Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential stealer malware bundled with packages. Pipeline must detect PHP code execution from vendor directories, particularly calls to credential APIs (password managers, git credentials, AWS keys, browser caches). Article title guarantees this threat but no detection coverage exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process spawning with working directory in vendor/laravel-lang/* paths, especially child processes accessing credential stores (Chrome DB, Firefox, git config, .aws, .ssh). Alert on file reads to %APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome or equivalent cross-platform secret locations.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Drift Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks typically insert malicious versions alongside legitimate ones. Pipeline must detect version mismatch between declared and installed package versions, or hash mismatches vs. public registry records. Not addressed in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed Laravel-Lang package hashes (from composer.lock or filesystem) against official Packagist SHA256 records. Flag mismatches or 'phantom versions' (package versions that do not exist in official repository history).

suggestion.title: Composer Lock File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often modify composer.lock to pin compromised versions. Pipeline must baseline legitimate lock files and alert on unexpected changes, especially to Laravel-Lang pinned versions or hash fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor write events to composer.lock in development/deployment pipelines. Alert if Laravel-Lang entries are updated without corresponding code-review approval or CI/CD record. Baseline hash values for known-good versions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Drupal Core Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies product: 'Drupal Core SQL Injection vulnerability'. Detection must enumerate unpatched instances exposed to external networks with due date 2026-05-27.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Drupal Core instances. Alert on versions unpatched as of the federal due date 2026-05-27. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attacks Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'SQL injection vulnerability...via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' This is the exploitation mechanism and warrants SQL injection detection at the WAF and application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal instances for SQL injection payloads targeting database API endpoints. Flag requests containing SQL metacharacters, UNION operators, or boolean-based injection patterns in query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Within Drupal or Database Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states outcome: 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Detection should alert on unauthorized user role elevation or permission changes linked to SQL injection exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database and Drupal application logs for suspicious privilege escalation events: unauthorized role assignment, permission grants, or SQL queries modifying user access controls during or after detected SQL injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies outcome: 'remote code execution via specially crafted requests.' Detection must capture post-exploitation behavior after successful SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution, shell spawning, or file writes originating from web server processes (apache/nginx) hosting Drupal, particularly following SQL injection indicators in logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK Execution Downloading PowerShell Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file' and 'LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' This is the primary initial access vector requiring dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LNK files extracted from email-delivered ZIP archives that execute PowerShell.exe with -Command or -EncodedCommand flags downloading remote scripts. Monitor for parent process mshta.exe or explorer.exe launching cmd.exe → powershell.exe chains on systems with recent email attachment activity.

suggestion.title: YandexBrowser_setup Registry Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup.' This specific registry key is a direct, named IoC for Cloud Atlas persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RegistryValueSet events where HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or equivalent contains 'YandexBrowser_setup' pointing to any *.ps1 file in %TEMP% or user AppData. This key name is a strong Cloud Atlas indicator with minimal false positive risk.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Patching for Multi-User RDP Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' as a payload capability. Unauthorized termsrv.dll modification is a high-fidelity lateral movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor System32\termsrv.dll and SysWOW64\termsrv.dll for FileModified or FileCreated events; validate digital signature and file hash against known-good baselines. Cross-correlate with RegSetValue events modifying HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\TermService parameters (e.g., fDenyTSConnections=0).

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Execution from Temp Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as C2/persistence mechanisms. 'We observed the use of third-party public utilities (Tor/SSH/RevSocks) to gain a foothold in infected systems and create additional backup control channels.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ssh.exe, sshd.exe, or patched OpenSSH execution from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or other non-standard directories with command-line arguments containing '-R' (reverse forwarding), '-L' (local forwarding), or '-D' (SOCKS). Alert on SSH processes establishing persistent background connections without user TTY.

suggestion.title: RevSocks SOCKS5 Proxy Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'RevSocks' as explicitly deployed to 'create additional backup control channels.' RevSocks execution is a direct IoC of Cloud Atlas compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RevSocks binary execution by name or file path from user-writable directories. Alert on unexpected SOCKS5 proxy initialization patterns or outbound connections establishing SOCKS listener ports (default 1080 or variants). Cross-check against known RevSocks process telemetry (memory patterns, string signatures).

suggestion.title: PowerShower Credential Grabber Memory/Registry Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber).' PowerShell-based credential access typically involves LSASS, clipboard, or SAM hive reads, warranting sensitive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell scripts or child processes accessing LSASS (\Device\\LsaAuthenticationServer, Win32_LsassProcess), reading clipboard (Get-Clipboard, OpenClipboard API), or enumerating registry credentials hives (HKU\). Alert on rundll32.exe invoking credential provider DLLs (credui.dll, wincred.dll) from script contexts.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests to Drupal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and 'exploitation attempts have been detected in the wild'—SOCs must detect malicious request patterns before they reach the database abstraction API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for SQL metacharacters and keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, EXEC, --|comment syntax, semicolon-prefixed queries) in URL query parameters and POST body data targeting Drupal endpoints (/admin*, /user*, /search, /system*, /api*). Correlate with HTTP 5xx responses or slow query timeouts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Queries from Web Application Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL'—PostgreSQL query logs must show unexpected DDL/DML (DROP, ALTER, CREATE, DELETE with malformed WHERE clauses) from Drupal application user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multi-table UNION statements, nested subqueries, or information_schema/pg_* table enumeration executed by the Drupal service account (www-data, apache, nginx). Flag DELETE/DROP statements against core tables (users, roles, sessions, node) lacking application-pattern justification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Web Server Context Following Database Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in remote code execution'—if SQL injection achieves RCE (e.g., via PostgreSQL UDF or COPY TO execution), process spawn logs must detect shell or binary execution from web service UID in temporal proximity to SQL injection indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash, sh, python, perl, or system utilities spawned from www-data, apache, or nginx UID. Escalate if process execution immediately follows or correlates with anomalous database queries or HTTP 500 errors on Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Enumeration and Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable versions (8.9.x, 10.4–10.6, 11.0–11.3 with patch thresholds). Reconnaissance activity: attackers query /CHANGELOG.txt, HTTP headers, or /admin/reports/status to confirm version before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for GET requests to /CHANGELOG.txt, /sites/default/files/, or status/version-checking URIs. Flag repeated version-probing requests from single source followed by SQL injection attempt patterns within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Credential or Privilege Table Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in privilege escalation'—if SQL injection compromises user or role tables, UPDATE/INSERT statements modify hashes, role assignments, or administrative flags on sensitive tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UPDATE statements targeting users, roles, permissions, or sessions tables with unusual predicates (e.g., UPDATE users SET admin=1 WHERE..., UPDATE roles SET...permissions...). Flag password hash or token field modifications from non-administrative contexts.

suggestion.title: Large Data Exfiltration or Bulk Table Access Following SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of database data'—post-compromise, attackers bulk-read sensitive tables (users, contacts, orders, sessions, content).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential SELECT * queries or large COPY/EXPORT operations on sensitive tables (users, field_data_*, sessions, cache) from non-standard application contexts. Correlate with network volume spikes (large data transfers out) from database host.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-linked IP and ASN historical connection analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes VPN was 'used by 25 ransomware groups'—pipeline should identify the VPN provider's known ASNs, IP ranges, and domain infrastructure, then create use case to hunt retrospectively for connections from internal endpoints or exfil points to those ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for historical outbound connections from Windows or Linux endpoints to known dismantled VPN provider IP ranges or ASNs. Correlate with known ransomware beacon patterns or exfiltration timestamps to identify potential compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Detection of multi-hop proxy infrastructure patterns
suggestion.rationale: VPN services inherently enable multi-hop proxying; article explicitly describes 'VPN' dismantled 'used by ransomware groups', suggesting attackers leveraged T1090.003. Pipeline should generate detection for proxy or VPN client execution on endpoints combined with anomalous egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VPN client software (OpenVPN, WireGuard, proprietary clients) spawned by non-standard processes or users with concurrent non-RFC1918 network connections, or persistence via registry/startup folders for VPN configurations.

suggestion.title: Correlated ransomware actor infrastructure overlap
suggestion.rationale: Article's core finding—25 distinct ransomware groups using same VPN service—signals shared infrastructure pattern. Pipeline should create UC to detect when multiple known ransomware beacons resolve or connect to same VPN provider endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries and network connections from separate infected hosts against known VPN provider domains and IP ranges. Flag when domains associated with distinct ransomware families (based on C2 signatures or behavioral clustering) share VPN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: VPN service infrastructure acquisition and advertising
suggestion.rationale: 'Dismantled VPN' implies the service operated openly with registration, billing, hosting. Article suggests threat actors provisioned and maintained this infrastructure. Pipeline should capture T1583.006 (Acquire Infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registration, WHOIS updates, ASN announcements, or hosting account creation tied to known VPN provider infrastructure. Flag domains registered to bulletproof hosters or privacy registrars with historical ties to ransomware groups.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Access for Event-Themed Ticketing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents FIFA domain impersonation: 'relies on a common trick known as typosquatting, which involves on a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes'. Pipeline missed this primary attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network connections to domains matching FIFA/World Cup ticketing patterns with minor character variations (e.g., fifa26, fifa-26, world-cup-2026, etc.). Alert when domain structure closely resembles but does not exactly match official registrant domains. Cross-reference newly registered domains against trademark databases.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Ticketing Registration Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deceptive registration forms: 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange at first. It also asks for the usual things such as your name, email address, and phone number.' Pipeline failed to detect credential access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to typosquatted ticketing domains containing user registration form payloads (fields: name, email, phone). Detect anomalous user-agent strings or rapid sequential registrations from single source IPs. Correlate with phishing email campaigns referencing FIFA/World Cup.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Data Collection on Fake Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article documents financial theft: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and 'Once entered into the form, your payments details would travel into the hands of the cybercriminal'. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection for payment data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS traffic to typosquatted ticketing domains for form submissions containing credit card patterns (PAN regex, expiration fields, CVC). Alert on exfiltration of payment data to non-PCI-DSS compliant hosts or IPs outside typical payment processor ASNs. Correlate with user registration events on same domain.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Distribution via Email and Sponsored Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Pipeline extracted zero initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email for links to typosquatted World Cup/FIFA domains and alert on subjects containing urgency language ('limited availability', 'final tickets', 'official merchandise'). Flag sponsored search ads and social media posts linking to newly registered domains matching FIFA trademark patterns. Correlate sender domain reputation and DKIM/SPF validation status.

suggestion.title: Website Visual/Structural Cloning Detection for Brand Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes impersonation fidelity: 'The site also copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow, all in order to make the victim feel that the experience is legitimate.' Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection for website mimicry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build CSS and HTML structure baselines for official FIFA/World Cup domains. Monitor for new domains serving pages with >80% structural similarity (CSS class names, page tree topology, template layout). Flag registrations of domains within 2 character edits of legitimate domains serving ticketing/merchandise pages.

suggestion.title: Event-Driven Urgency Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of event-anticipation psychology: 'As the FIFA World Cup 2026™ draws closer, anticipation is building toward fever pitch... interested, impatient and... worried that the tickets... will sell out. Which is ultimately what makes these scams so effective.' Pipeline missed temporal/behavioral pattern for event-driven phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement calendar-triggered detection rules activating 60-120 days before major sporting events (World Cup, Olympics, Super Bowl). During these windows, increase sensitivity on email campaigns containing urgency keywords ('official', 'limited', 'last chance') and links to newly registered domains. Correlate bulk email volume spikes with event date proximity.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Configuration Utility RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SSH access to the first Linux host from a network device identified as an F5 BIG-IP load balancer' running EOL version 15.1.201000. CVE-2026-39455 is the likely attack vector but was not mapped to any detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP appliances for unauthenticated or low-privileged access to configuration utility endpoints (typically port 443 on /tmui). Flag successful authentication followed by shell process execution (bash/sh spawned as root or admin). Alert on outbound SSH from F5 appliances to internal Linux hosts.

suggestion.title: Confluence Remote Code Execution via Unpatched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Confluence server within the network with unpatched vulnerabilities' and 'leveraged these vulnerabilities to execute code remotely.' CVE-2025-33073 mentioned in search results. No detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence application logs and process events for unusual Java process spawning (Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder). Alert on HTTP POST to known Confluence RCE endpoints with payloads. Track outbound network from Confluence process to external FTP or DNS servers.

suggestion.title: Python FTP Server Launch from Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'set up an FTP server on the initial Linux host using Python's ftplib module to transfer the custom scanning tool.' This is explicit staging infrastructure but generated zero IOCs or detection cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python process spawning with ftplib import or python -m ftpserver execution. Alert on listening sockets on port 21 or high-numbered FTP ports from non-standard processes. Monitor file transfers into compromised Confluence via FTP on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack with PetitPotam Coercion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'escalated into Kerberos relay attacks and exploitation of CVE-2025-33073, using netexec with PetitPotam coercion.' This is a sophisticated lateral movement technique with specific tooling (netexec, PetitPotam) that should trigger multiple detections but pipeline generated none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netexec process execution on compromised Linux hosts. Alert on EfsRpc (Endpoint File Service RPC) calls from Linux to Windows targets—signature of PetitPotam coercion. Flag failed Kerberos pre-authentication followed by successful relay attacks in event logs (event 4768 with relay indicators, event 4769 from unexpected sources).

suggestion.title: DNS Manipulation for Domain Controller Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'DNS manipulation tooling to target a domain controller.' No DNS-based detection use case generated despite explicit statement of DNS abuse in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries from compromised Linux host to domain controller hostnames with subsequent unusual DNS responses (non-authoritative replies, mismatched A/AAAA records, queries from non-DNS ports). Alert on iptables or netfilter rules modifying DNS responses on compromised host. Monitor for in-path DNS spoofing via tcpdump or similar capture.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Confluence LDAP/Kerberos Integration
suggestion.rationale: Attack pivoted through Confluence to 'credential theft and identity compromise' and 'domain-level compromise spanning Linux hosts, an internal Atlassian Confluence server, and Windows authentication systems.' No credential theft detection mapped despite being core to the attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence process for LDAP unbind followed by credential enumeration queries (group membership, service account lookups). Alert on unusual LDAP binding attempts with cleartext credentials captured in logs. Flag Confluence spawning credential dumping tools (lsass access, /etc/shadow reads, keytab exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Detection - Ukraine Government
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware'. Phishing is the initial attack vector; no use case generated despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails targeting Ukraine government domain recipients, particularly those with attachments or links associated with Prometheus campaigns. Alert on emails from external senders claiming to be legitimate government communications or containing .exe/.zip attachments with suspicious macros or Office documents with embedded payloads.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' but no detection use case for malware execution post-phishing click. Missing the execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned from Office applications (winword.exe, excel.exe) or execution of files recently downloaded by phishing targets. Monitor for Prometheus-associated process names, command-line patterns, or network IOCs if available.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Phishing malware campaigns typically exfiltrate credentials post-execution. Article describes 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' implying credential theft capability, but no detection UC for credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual LDAP queries, credential spraying patterns, or authentication failures from machines known to have opened phishing payloads. Alert on exfiltration of credential-manager files or registry key access for stored passwords.

suggestion.title: Government Entity Email Gateway Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine government being targeted means inbound email filtering bypass, unusual volume from external senders, or whitelisting of malicious domains. Article describes targeted campaign but no detection for gateway-level indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails bypassing or failing initial phishing checks sent to government recipients. Monitor for allowlisting of domains associated with Prometheus infrastructure or unusual sender patterns spoofing internal government communications.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter Attribution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Ghostwriter as the threat actor. No detection use case for actor-specific TTPs or infrastructure indicators. Ghostwriter has known phishing domains and C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to known Ghostwriter C2 infrastructure or phishing domains. Alert on DNS queries to subdomains historically associated with Ghostwriter campaigns targeting Eastern Europe.

suggestion.title: SQL injection payload patterns in YesWiki Bazar form POST parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement' but no detection looks for actual SQLi payloads (boolean-based, time-based, union-based) in form parameters. Core exploitation vector is parameter-level injection, not just volumetric access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /BazaR?vue=formulaire for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, SLEEP, BENCHMARK) and SQL metacharacters (', --, ;, /*) in form parameter values. Blind SQLi attempts will show time delays or error messages in response bodies.

suggestion.title: Database credential material exfiltration from YesWiki
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack 'allows read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'—this is the impact. No detection for unusual query patterns, credential table access, or large result-set exfiltration to external destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for SELECT queries against yeswiki_users or similar credential tables executed via web application context. Correlate with large data transfers (MB+) out of database server to web server to external IP. Focus on any query outside normal application baseline.

suggestion.title: YesWiki installation discovery and version enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable versions (4.6.1, 4.6.2, doryphore-dev). Asset inventory hunts should identify YesWiki instances and their versions to scope exposure before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan HTTP responses for YesWiki version strings, or look for characteristic paths (/BazaR, /yeswiki, /docs/en/wakka.php) and version footprints in headers or page source. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-46670 affected versions.

suggestion.title: Error-based SQLi detection from form responses
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQLi extraction relies on timing or error channels. Article describes INSERT-statement injection; MySQL/MariaDB errors in form responses would reveal vulnerability. No detection for SQL error messages in HTTP 200/500 responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies for SQL error patterns (MySQL syntax errors, 'Column count doesn't match', 'You have an error in your SQL syntax'). Correlate with POST to vulnerable endpoint and anomalous parameter values.

suggestion.title: Time-delay blind SQLi confirmation in YesWiki POST responses
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQLi typically uses SLEEP() or similar delays to infer truth. Article mentions 'blind SQLi extraction loop'—detections should look for request/response timing anomalies consistent with conditional delays.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST response times to /BazaR?vue=formulaire endpoint. Flag requests with unusual latency spikes (5s+) that correlate with SLEEP() or time-based payloads in parameters. Normal form submissions return <500ms.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public-facing PATCH path traversal exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` with user-controlled `fromPath` and `toPath` fields containing `..` traversal sequences. Detection needed for direct exploitation attempts. Article phrase: 'publicPatchHandler...joins user-controlled fromPath and toPath body fields...BEFORE the downstream sanitizer runs.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources*` endpoints for request bodies containing relative path traversal sequences (`..`, `%2e%2e`) in fromPath or toPath JSON fields. Correlation with hash parameter presence indicates active exploitation of CVE-2026-44542.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance probing against FileBrowser Quantum public share API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes public-facing endpoint that attackers would scan for vulnerability presence and enumerate accessible hashes. Article phrase: 'Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning' and implied enumeration of multiple share hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated PATCH requests to the same public-share endpoint with varying hash parameters (3+ unique hashes in 5-minute window) or high-volume requests (10+ PATCH attempts) indicating hash enumeration or vulnerability scanning.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation file operation impact on FileBrowser Quantum shares
suggestion.rationale: Article describes concrete impact: 'the move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory.' Detection should target successful exploitation artifacts—unauthorized file modifications outside share boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file operations (rename, move, copy, delete) initiated through FileBrowser Quantum processes where target path falls outside the declared share directory boundary, combined with preceding PATCH requests from same source.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44542 asset inventory and vulnerability exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific vulnerability CVE-2026-44542 affecting FileBrowser Quantum. Standard asset-exposure hunt needed to identify vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for FileBrowser Quantum instances and cross-reference against CVE-2026-44542 vulnerability databases. Prioritize instances with public-share feature enabled and externally-facing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Command-and-Control Traffic Over Compromised Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'large-scale command-and-control operations' via 'telecom networks'—C2 detection is the core missing piece.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous callback patterns, DNS tunnel activity, and HTTP/HTTPS C2 beaconing originating from or transiting through identified compromised telecom ASN ranges. Focus on command-encoding anomalies and fallback channel activation when primary C2 paths fail.

suggestion.title: Detect Infrastructure Compromise and Persistence on Telecom Core Network Elements
suggestion.rationale: 'Large-scale' operations imply durable compromise of multiple telecom systems (SGs, MSCs, HLRs); persistence mechanisms should be tracked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized firmware/bootloader modifications on telecom switching equipment, creation of rogue administrative accounts, and installation of backdoors with suspicious privilege persistence patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement and Network Reconnaissance Within Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'large-scale' operations indicates pivot across multiple systems; discovery and lateral movement phases unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scanning, service enumeration, network topology mapping, and suspicious lateral admin tool usage targeting telecom routers, switches, HSS/HLR systems, and signaling gateways.

suggestion.title: Detect Abuse of Legitimate Telecom Protocols for C2 Relay
suggestion.rationale: 'Abuse' of telecom networks implies co-opting legitimate protocols (SS7, Diameter, SMPP) for command relay—protocol anomaly detection absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on signaling protocol (SS7, Diameter) traffic with anomalous payloads, unusual origination points, or timing patterns inconsistent with legitimate telecom operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Access via Exploitation of Telecom Infrastructure Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Title implies successful initial compromise of telecom infrastructure; exploitation or vulnerable access pathways should be tracked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts against telecom-specific services (DSLAMs, ONUs, RAN controllers) and VPN/management interface access from unusual geographies or with suspicious credential usage.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Creation from npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package'—implies malicious code execution during install. Pipeline extracted zero use cases for detecting post-install process anomalies from node_modules contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawning from npm install operations, particularly JavaScript runtimes (node.exe, node, npm) executing from %AppData%\npm\node_modules or temporary package cache directories with unexpected command lines or outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Registry Metadata Mismatch on High-Value npm Package Download
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of 'art-template' implies either registry injection or malicious version publication. Article does not name specific versions, but pipeline should flag art-template downloads against known-compromised lists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package installation requests for 'art-template' (and templating packages with high download counts) where downloaded artifact hash does not match npm registry published checksum, or where installation occurs from non-standard repository mirrors.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network from node_modules Code Context
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks require command-and-control or exfiltration signaling. Article describes attack campaign but pipeline missed detection for network callbacks initiated by compromised package code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by node.exe processes where parent process or working directory maps to node_modules installation paths, particularly to non-standard ports or domains outside known CDN/registry ranges.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Install Script Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: npm packages can execute arbitrary scripts during install via postinstall hooks. Article describes a backdoored package but pipeline generated zero detection for script execution during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned as children of npm.cmd or npm process during install, especially with command lines containing download/deobfuscation operations or environment variable tampering.

suggestion.title: Batch File Triggering Hidden PowerShell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Victim executes malicious batch file' followed by 'Hidden PowerShell command triggers silently' using 'Consultar_NF-e.bat' as delivery vehicle. This two-stage execution is the core delivery pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Batch file execution immediately followed by PowerShell process creation with -WindowStyle Hidden or equivalent obfuscation. Flag .bat files with NF-e, invoice, or financial-themed names executing powershell.exe with no visible window. Banana RAT uses this pattern as immediate post-delivery execution.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Anomalous Minute-Level Interval
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Persistence established via hidden scheduled task (runs every minute for 9,999 days)'. One-minute execution intervals are non-standard and specific to this malware's persistence strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect schtasks.exe or New-ScheduledTask operations creating tasks with RepetitionInterval < 60 seconds. Flag tasks hidden or placed in non-standard directories. Bananda RAT uses aggressive one-minute tasking for immediate remote access execution.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Payload Download to System Diagnostic Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'AES-256 encrypted payload ("msedge.txt") retrieved' and 'Files disguised in Microsoft diagnostic directories'. This combination of file naming obfuscation and directory placement is evasion-specific to this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads of innocuous filenames (msedge.txt, st.txt, st.php, payload.php) to %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft or diagnostic subdirectories. Correlate with network traffic to conviTemundial2026[.]com or windowsk-cdn[.]com on port 443. Flag in-memory decryption patterns accessing these files.

suggestion.title: Keystroke Logging and Screen Capture Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Live screen streaming and keystroke logging' as core post-infection capabilities. This combination enables account-takeover attacks against banking sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process combinations loading screen-capture and keystroke-logging libraries: GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx, User32.dll pattern. Monitor for process access to windows with Brazilian bank names (Itau, Bradesco, Santander). Concurrent screen capture + keystroke logging from same process lineage indicates RAT deployment.

suggestion.title: Banking Overlay Injection and QR Code Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Fake banking overlay injection mimicking security updates' and 'Pix QR code interception and replacement during transactions'. This is attack-specific to Brazilian Pix payment system targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL injection into banking app processes (Itau, Bradesco, Santander). Detect clipboard modification during payment workflows. Flag overlay windows with security-update-style names appearing over banking applications. Process injection + clipboard tampering + screen capture correlation indicates transaction-hijacking RAT.

suggestion.title: NF-e Invoice Phishing Campaign via WhatsApp
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body state 'Hackers Use NF-e Invoice Lures' distributed via 'WhatsApp and phishing links' targeting Brazilian users. NF-e familiarity provides social engineering leverage in Brazil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phishing campaigns with NF-e, Consultar_NF-e, invoice audit, or Receita Federal (Brazilian tax authority) lures in Portuguese targeting .com.br domains. Monitor for shortened URLs from messaging app browsers downloading .bat files. WhatsApp-specific delivery patterns indicate Brazilian financial targeting.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized Cron Job or Scheduled Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'six-layer persistence'; scheduled task persistence (cron/at) is a standard first-layer persistence mechanism. No detection use case for this was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/crontab, /var/spool/cron/*, and /etc/cron.d/. Alert on cron entries executing from /tmp, /var/tmp, invoking shells (bash, sh, python), or connecting to external IPs. Flag cron jobs running as asterisk or root without documented business purpose.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized Systemd Service or Init Script Installation
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated 'six-layer' persistence on Linux includes daemon/service auto-start via systemd or /etc/init.d. No detection for process-level startup persistence was generated despite this being a primary mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or modified files in /etc/systemd/system/, /etc/init.d/, /etc/rc*.d/. Alert on service units with ExecStart pointing to /tmp, /var/tmp, or unsigned binaries. Flag modifications to existing FreePBX service files with unusual directives.

suggestion.title: FreePBX SSH Authorized Key Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: SSH key-based persistence enables persistent remote access in multi-layer scenarios. Article emphasizes comprehensive persistence but generated no detection for SSH backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and /root/.ssh/authorized_keys for appended entries. Alert on file modifications from web server processes, PHP, or non-administrative accounts. Flag entries with encoded payloads in comment fields or keys without corresponding administrative justification.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Web Shell or Malicious PHP Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Web-facing persistence commonly leverages malicious scripts in document roots. Article describes VoIP application persistence but generated no detection for web-layer backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX web directories for new executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar). Alert on modifications to existing PHP files containing eval(), system(), exec(), or shell_exec(). Cross-reference file modification timestamps with HTTP POST/PUT requests in access logs.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized System User or Backdoor Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence typically includes hidden user accounts for shell access. Title indicates depth and sophistication, but no detection for account-based persistence was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow for new entries via useradd/adduser/vipw. Alert on accounts with UID 0 or service-range UIDs (< 1000). Flag accounts with shell access but no home directory or UID collisions with known service accounts.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Kernel Module or Rootkit Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated 'six-layer' persistence on Linux often culminates in kernel-level hooks or LKMs for deep access. No detection for rootkit or kernel-level persistence was generated despite this being a typical final layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe execution, especially loading from /tmp or unexpected module names. Alert on new entries in /proc/modules or lsmod. Flag audit log tampering, audit rule deletion, or unusual kernel error messages common in rootkit signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet C2 Communication from IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes KimWolf as a botnet with command infrastructure sending commands to millions of compromised devices. Article states 'command infrastructure to send DDoS commands to the botnet' implicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound C2-like communication patterns from IoT devices (e.g., embedded systems, routers, cameras) to non-standard ports (2000-10000 range), unusual user-agents in HTTP headers, and repetitive beacon intervals. Correlate with known botnet command server IPs if available.

suggestion.title: Detect Large-Scale DDoS Attack Traffic Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacks 'measured at nearly 30 Terabits per second' and describes 'executing DDoS attacks against targets,' indicating compromised IoT devices are flooding targets with requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal outbound traffic volume from IoT/embedded device segments (>1 Gbps sustained, >1 million packets per second), particularly from devices with previously normal network profiles. Monitor for DDoS patterns: high request rates to single destination, spoofed source IPs, or application-layer floods.

suggestion.title: Detect IoT Malware Infection and Lateral Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates KimWolf 'infected over a million devices worldwide' across geographies, suggesting worm-like propagation through vulnerability exploitation or brute-force credential compromise on IoT admin panels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed SSH/Telnet login attempts against IoT devices (routers, DVRs, IP cameras) followed by process execution of unknown binaries or curl/wget downloads from external servers. Detect unusual process spawning on embedded Linux systems, particularly shells or reverse shells initiated from network services.

suggestion.title: Detect Doxing and Swatting Campaign Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states the threat actor 'launched a volley of DDoS, doxing and swatting campaigns against [security researchers],' indicating a secondary attack infrastructure or service abuse for personal harassment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data scraping of public databases (people search, social media APIs), enrollment in social media harassment platforms, or SIM-swapping attempts targeting security researchers. Correlate suspicious activity patterns with threat actors known to operate DDoS-for-hire services.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Admin Panel Access and Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'administrating KimWolf DDoS botnet,' implying a web dashboard or control panel requiring administrative credentials to manage the botnet fleet and launch DDoS jobs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized access to web-based botnet control panels (credential stuffing, brute-force, default creds), unusual login patterns from non-endemic geographies, and rapid deployment of DDoS jobs. Alert on control panel traffic exfiltrating device lists or attack targets.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Delivery via Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates infection 'over a million devices' including 'devices located in Alaska,' suggesting either firmware compromises in IoT manufacturing supply chain or widespread exploitation of default credentials in mass-produced devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected firmware updates on IoT devices from untrusted sources, detection of backdoor accounts in firmware images, and mass provisioning of devices with non-manufacturer signing keys. Alert on clusters of devices with identical non-standard configurations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Driver Loading from Non-System Paths
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires loading vulnerable drivers—the article framing of 'exploitable without hardware' implies attackers are loading drivers programmatically. Article should describe driver loading mechanisms (registry, LoadDriver calls, sc.exe) as a step in the exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for driver loading (LoadDriver API, sc.exe create/start) of files in non-standard paths (AppData, Temp, user-writable dirs). Correlate with privilege escalation events or unexpected kernel-mode process creation. Filter on unsigned drivers and file hash reputation.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module or Driver Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Core of BYOVD is exploiting a vulnerability in the loaded driver to escape user-mode. Article must describe the exploitation step—vulnerability trigger via IOCTL, memory manipulation, or specific input sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege elevation events (token elevation, access token duplication) preceded by driver load. Look for processes transitioning from user to system/local service context. Correlate suspicious driver with known vulnerable driver CVEs (MSI Afterburner, NVIDIA GPU drivers, Intel chipset drivers).

suggestion.title: Registry Modifications Enabling Kernel Driver Persistence
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD often uses registry run keys, startup folders, or boot parameters to persist the vulnerable driver. Article should discuss persistence via Services registry hive or kernel boot parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services registry writes for new services with suspicious ImagePath pointing to non-standard driver locations. Alert on unexpected kernel boot parameter modifications (HKLMSystem\CurrentControlSet\Control). Baseline legitimate driver service creations.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Unverified Kernel Driver Execution
suggestion.rationale: While BYOVD abuses signed legitimate drivers, the wrapping or delivery mechanism may involve unsigned payloads. Article likely mentions driver file hashes, signatures, or the contrast between legitimate vs. weaponized versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag driver loads where signature status is invalid, missing, or mismatched against known-good hashes. Cross-reference against vulnerable driver version databases (e.g., SafeBreach's BYOVD driver list). Detect version downgrades of legitimate drivers to known-vulnerable editions.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Vulnerable Driver to System Access
suggestion.rationale: End goal of BYOVD is moving from user-mode to kernel/system privileges. Article must detail the outcome—process token elevation, service account compromise, or admin context acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process token elevation without prior consent_prompt or UAC interaction. Monitor for low-privilege child processes spawning high-privilege children (SYSTEM, LocalService). Correlate with recent driver load events within same session.

suggestion.title: Rootkit or Kernel Persistence Installation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD is often the foot-in-door for rootkit deployment. Article should describe the persistence payload—WinRing0, PassMark, or custom kernel-mode backdoors loaded via the vulnerable driver.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After privilege escalation via driver, detect unexpected system service creation with kernel-mode execution context. Monitor for multiple driver loads in short timeframe. Alert on known-malicious driver hashes (e.g., PassMark PoC rootkits, WinRing0 variants).

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Addition with Base64 Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'injected GitHub Actions workflows containing base64-encoded bash payloads'—encoding is signature obfuscation technique requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on addition of new .github/workflows/*.yml files containing base64-encoded strings or unusual env vars. Baseline expected workflow names and alert on mass additions across multiple repos within 1-hour windows (Megalodon pushed 5,718 commits in 6 hours). Decode base64 payloads for inline credential exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets Exfiltration to External C2
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies payload 'exfiltrate[s] CI secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens' to C2 at 216.126.225.129:8443—direct credential exfiltration is primary attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for workflows that reference ${{ secrets.* }} or ${{ env.GITHUB_TOKEN }} combined with outbound HTTPS requests to non-GitHub domains. Flag workflows using curl/wget to exfiltrate secrets. Correlate with network telemetry showing GitHub runners initiating connections to 216.126.225.129:8443 or similar C2 patterns.

suggestion.title: Forged Git Commit Author Identity Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article documents attacker 'forged author identities build-bot, auto-ci, ci-bot, pipeline-bot with emails build-system@noreply.dev and ci-bot@automated.dev'—author spoofing bypasses code review verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits where author name contains generic bot patterns (build-bot, auto-ci, ci-bot, pipeline-bot, etc.) but domain is noreply.dev or automated.dev. Flag mismatches between author names and email domains (e.g., 'build-bot' from 'ci-bot@' address). Baseline legitimate bot commits and alert on new patterns injecting workflow changes.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Workflow Injection Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'between approximately 11:36 and 17:48 UTC...5,718 malicious commits to 5,561 GitHub repositories in less than six hours'—massive scale attack requires volume-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect statistical anomaly: multiple repositories (threshold >50 in 6-hour window) receiving workflow file additions from distinct throwaway accounts or with identical workflow content hashes. Correlate with commit message patterns ('ci: add build optimization', 'chore: optimize pipeline'). Alert on coordinated push events from randomized eight-character GitHub usernames.

suggestion.title: Workflow_Dispatch Backdoor for On-Demand Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeted variant 'Optimize-Build replaced existing workflows with workflow_dispatch triggers, creating dormant backdoors that the attacker can fire on demand via the GitHub API'—manual workflow execution enables persistent remote control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag workflows modified to replace push/pull_request triggers with workflow_dispatch-only execution. Alert on API calls to trigger workflows via repository_dispatch endpoint from unusual or newly-created service accounts. Establish baseline of legitimate workflow_dispatch usage and monitor for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Throwaway GitHub Account Creation and Rapid Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Article documents attacker 'using throwaway accounts with randomized eight-character usernames'—rapid account creation and immediate high-volume commits indicate automated supply-chain attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub accounts created with randomized 8-character alphanumeric usernames (regex: ^[a-z0-9]{8}$) that immediately commit to multiple repositories (threshold >10 in 1 hour). Flag accounts with no profile, avatar, or commit history before attack window. Correlate account creation timestamps with workflow injection events.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow File Injection - Mass Repo Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 5,500+ public repositories affected by 'mass exfiltration'—this scale implies coordinated malicious workflow injection. The attacker modified .github/workflows/ files or injected commands into Actions execution contexts to achieve the exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions or modifications to .github/workflows/*.yml files with suspicious command injection patterns (e.g., bash -c with base64, output redirection, or curl/wget to external IPs).
